title: Tierschutz kritisiert den Abbau der Taubenschläge
content:
Gemeinsame Medienmitteilung von Stadttauben Schweiz und Tier im Fokus (TIF)


Bern, 7. September 2026 – Die Stadt Bern muss sparen. Das bekommen nun auch die Tauben zu spüren: Von 2027 bis 2030 will der Gemeinderat beim Taubenmanagement jährlich 81’254 Franken einsparen. Betroffen ist der Tierpark Bern, der die Stadttauben im Auftrag der Stadt in mehreren Schlägen betreut. Er soll

«Teile dieses Angebots» einstellen

, wie es im Finanzplan des Gemeinderats heisst.


Der Verein Stadttauben Schweiz kritisiert diesen Abbau. «Betreute Taubenschläge sind das wirksamste Mittel, um die Zahl der Stadttauben tief und die Tiere gesund zu halten», sagt Nina Bachellerie, Präsidentin des Vereins.


Seit der Gemeinderat die Taubenkontrolle 2010 dem Tierpark Bern übertragen hat, ist die Population von über 10’000 Tieren auf rund 1’500 gesunken – betreut in acht Schlägen in der Altstadt und den Quartieren. Die Tiere werden

jährlich geimpft und tierärztlich kontrolliert

, ihr Kot fällt im Schlag an statt an Fassaden und Haltestellen: rechnerisch rund 85 Tonnen weniger pro Jahr. Das Berner Konzept gilt als «weltweit einzigartig», wie kürzlich

im «Bund» zu lesen war

 – Städte aus ganz Europa lassen sich die Praxis erklären.


Interpellation verlangt eine Bilanz


Was das Taubenmanagement kostet, ist bekannt: rund 240’000 Franken pro Jahr (Stand 2022). Was es der Stadt erspart, hat der Gemeinderat hingegen nie beziffert. Tier im Fokus (TIF) hat deshalb die Interpellation «Was leistet das Berner Taubenmanagement für die Stadt?» im Berner Stadtrat eingereicht. Sie verlangt Auskunft über die vermiedenen Reinigungs- und Instandsetzungskosten sowie über den Beitrag der Taubenschläge an den Gesundheitsschutz, den Tourismus und den Erhalt des UNESCO-Welterbes.


«Der Gemeinderat kennt die Kosten des Taubenmanagements, aber nicht seinen Nutzen», sagt Tobias Sennhauser, Stadtrat von Tier im Fokus (TIF). «Mit dem Abbau der Taubenschläge steigt das Risiko, dass die Verschmutzungen an den Fassaden wieder zunehmen.»


Der Stadtrat entscheidet in der Budgetdebatte vom 10. und 17. September über die Kürzung.


Der Beitrag

Tierschutz kritisiert den Abbau der Taubenschläge

author: Dr. Yvonne Würz
title: Nach Angriff auf Aktivistinnen: Neue Recherche zeigt Tierleid auf Santorini
content:
Am 4. September 2026 wurden drei PETA-Aktivistinnen auf der Karavolades-Treppe auf der griechischen Insel

Santorini

 von mehreren Eseltreibern angegriffen. Die Aktivistinnen wollten auf das Leid der

Esel

 aufmerksam machen. Nun veröffentlichen wir von PETA Deutschland neues Recherchematerial, das kurz zuvor aufgenommen wurde und erneut dokumentiert, wie tierquälerisch Eselreiten auf Santorini wirklich ist.  


Eselreiten auf Santorini: Neue PETA-Recherche zeigt anhaltendes Tierleid 

 


Zahlreiche Recherchen haben in den letzten Jahren belegt, wie Maultiere und Esel auf Santorini als vermeintliche „

Tourismusattraktion

“ ausgebeutet werden. Auch das neue Material aus dem September 2026 dokumentiert erneut die tierquälerischen Bedingungen, unter denen die Tiere auf Santorini jeden Tag leiden:   


Die Maultiere und Esel werden routinemäßig

mit Stockschlägen angetrieben

.  


Viele Tiere sind sichtlich

erschöpft und apathisch

.   


Einige Maultiere lecken wiederholt Mauern ab, was auf

Wasser- oder Nährstoffmangel

 oder auch

Verhaltensstörungen

 hindeuten kann.   


Wasser steht lediglich an den oberen und unteren Enden der Treppe zur Verfügung. Viele Tiere haben jedoch nicht einmal dort ständigen Zugang dazu, da sie häufig fernab dieser Wassertröge angebunden sind.   


Schattenplätze sind vor allem in der Mittagszeit rar, obwohl die Tiere über Stunden

hohen Temperaturen

 ausgesetzt sind.   


Die Tiere müssen teilweise sehr

schwere Lasten tragen,

 obwohl laut Tierschutzregelungen ein Maximum von 100 Kilogramm gilt. Dennoch wurde beobachtet, dass auch schwergewichtige Menschen auf den Maultieren und Eseln reiten dürfen.  


Viele Tiere haben sichtbare

Narben von Verletzungen

.   


Ein altes Tier hat einen deutlich

eingefallenen Rücken

 und eine

Geschwulst

 im Achselbereich, wo die provisorischen Sattelgurte scheuern. 


„Die aktuellen Aufnahmen zeigen, dass sich für die Tiere trotz jahrelanger Kritik wenig geändert hat. Während über den Angriff auf unsere Aktivistinnen gesprochen wird, werden die Esel und Maultiere auf Santorini weiterhin für touristische Zwecke ausgebeutet und müssen dabei Tag für Tag Schläge dieser gewaltbereiten Menschen fürchten. Genau deshalb braucht es endlich einen Ausstieg aus den sogenannten Eselritten und den Umstieg auf moderne, tierfreundliche Alternativen.“ 

Dr. Yvonne Würz, Biologin und Fachreferentin bei PETA Deutschland 


PETA-Aktivistinnen bei Protestaktion von Eseltreibern angegriffen 

 


Im September 2026 bereiteten PETA-Aktivistinnen eine Aktion vor, um auf das Leid der Tiere aufmerksam zu machen und eine tierfreie Alternative zu den Eselritten zu präsentieren. Während sie die Aufnahmen auf der Karavolades-Treppe machten, wurden sie von mehreren Eseltreibern angegriffen. Die Männer zerstörten die Protestschilder, beleidigten die Frauen und versuchten, weitere Filmaufnahmen zu verhindern. Nach Angaben der Aktivistinnen wurden sie gedrängt, die Treppe zu verlassen. Als sie bereits, umringt von den Männern, die Stufen hinuntergingen, wurde eine Aktivistin von einer Person gegen eine Mauer gedrückt und ins Gesicht geschlagen.  


PETA zeigt innovative, tierfreundliche Alternative auf 

 


Die Aktivistinnen wollten bei der Aktion zeigen, dass es längst moderne und tierfreundliche Alternativen zu „Eseltaxis“ gibt. Dafür hatten sie Exoskelette, also tragbare Roboterbeine zur Unterstützung der Gehbewegung, mitgebracht. Die Technologie kann dabei helfen, die rund 500 Stufen hinauf zur Stadt zu bewältigen, ohne dass dafür Esel ausgebeutet werden. Wir von PETA Deutschland fordern, dass Eselreiten endlich von der griechischen Regierung verboten wird. Vorab hatte PETA in einem

Schreiben

 an den Bürgermeister sowie den Präsidenten der Hafenbehörde der Gemeinde von Firá angeboten, die Anschaffung solcher Exoskelette für den Treppenaufstieg finanziell zu unterstützen, sollten die Eselritte eingestellt werden. 


Helfen Sie jetzt den Eseln auf Santorini 

 


Nach wie vor werden Esel auf Santorini als lebende Transportmittel missbraucht. Buchen Sie bitte niemals „Tourismusattraktionen“ wie „Eseltaxis“ und entscheiden Sie sich stattdessen für tierfreundliche Alternativen. Unterstützen Sie zudem unsere Petition an die griechische Regierung und fordern Sie, dass die Ausbeutung von Eseln endlich verboten wird.  


Jetzt helfen

PETA Deutschland e.V.

author: Timothy French
title: New Yorkers Defeated a Pipeline Nearly 6 Years Ago — Or So They Thought
content:
The Williams Northeast Supply Enhancement pipeline has been fought, defeated, and revived multiple times.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A unique kind of relief comes from standing at the edge of the ocean. For generations, New York and New Jersey’s public beaches have offered exactly that: a free, open shoreline where people come to breathe, grieve, celebrate, fall in love, or simply exist without needing money or permission. For many, the beach is not a luxury. It is medicine.

Beneath that same water, a fight is unfolding that could put all of it at risk.

The Williams Northeast Supply Enhancement pipeline, known as NESE, has been fought, defeated, and revived more times than most New Yorkers realize. It has outlasted three formal environmental denials, a pandemic, and a change in presidential administration, only to return with the same basic promise: that it is necessary, that it is safe, and that someone other than the company building it will benefit. For nearly a decade, a coalition spanning environmental groups, immigrant families, LGBTQIA+ beachgoers, and conservative homeowners who agree on little else has fought to prove otherwise.

The current fight traces back to 2011 and 2012. After Superstorm Sandy, then-Representative Michael Grimm quietly authorized legislation allowing a gas pipeline through the Gateway National Recreation Area, the federal parkland including Jacob Riis Beach. “No community outreach was done,” said Kim Fraczek, director of Sane Energy Project, who has organized against Rockaway-area pipeline infrastructure since 2011. “When the community finally caught wind of this proposal, it was already approved.” Grimm, who later threatened a reporter and served federal prison time for tax fraud before receiving a pardon from Trump in 2025, set the precedent for the top-down decision-making that would define the fight to come.

That earlier pipeline, the Rockaway Lateral, became the entry point for a much larger project: NESE. Williams first applied to federal regulators in March 2017 to build roughly 37 miles of new pipeline, including a 23.5-mile underwater segment through Raritan Bay. New York Department of Environmental Conservation cited threats to hard clam habitat, unverified sediment-loss estimates, and an unjustified burial depth that could disturb the seafloor. The 2020 denial followed a public comment period that drew more than 16,000 responses. “We thought we beat it,” Fraczek said. “It was sort of a closed book at that time.”

In 2025, the project came roaring back. Following a stop-work order the Trump administration placed on New York’s Empire Wind offshore project, Gov. Kathy Hochul entered private negotiations with the White House. Within days, the administration publicly claimed Hochul had agreed to advance gas pipelines including NESE in exchange for allowing Empire Wind to proceed, a characterization Hochul disputed. In November 2025, her Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) reversed course, granting Transco, the Williams subsidiary behind the project, a conditional water quality certification.

The reversal rested on a striking detail: Transco’s revised application corrected what it called a math error in its original hard clam density estimate, from 69.6 clams per square foot down to 3.7, a nearly twentyfold reduction that made the project’s ecological footprint appear dramatically smaller. Transco also revised its sediment-loss projections and offered new justification for burying the pipeline four feet below the seabed rather than the traditional six.

The decision carried an added layer of scrutiny: Hochul’s husband left his role as General Counsel at Delaware North in 2023 to join Davis Polk & Wardwell, a major corporate law firm, where he now earns between $850,000 and $950,000 annually advising clients on government investigations.

Suzanne Mattei, an attorney and former DEC regional director, has authored three reports on the pipeline’s finances since 2019: False Demand: The Case Against the Williams Fracked Gas Pipeline (2019), Proposed NESE Gas Pipeline in New York: A Bad Bargain For Ratepayers and Taxpayers (2020), and The Williams NESE Gas Pipeline is Not Better the Second Time Around (2025). She said the timing of the reversal raised its own questions.

Williams initially justified the pipeline’s urgency by pointing to Winter Storm Elliott, which struck the Northeast in December 2022 …

title: Lac Simon warns LNG project it requires consent as Carney invites the world to invest in Canada
content:
The first-ever Canada Investment Summit opened its three-day run in Toronto yesterday with a reception aiming to warm up Canadian businesses and global investors hoping to lay the groundwork for a new era of well-funded Canadian innovation.


However, the Anishnabe Nation of Lac Simon sent out a press release this morning reminding participants that the First Nations–backed

Kino Aski

 liquefied natural gas (LNG) project, intended to export Canadian LNG to Europe, cannot proceed without the consent of any First Nations along the project’s path.


“The project currently lacks both community consent and significant social acceptance,” the Council of the Anishnabe Nation of Lac Simon said in its statement.


Kino Aski project involves a pipeline to ship LNG from Western Canada to Baie-Comeau, 700 kilometres east of Montreal on Quebec’s North Shore, and from there to Europe.


The project has the support of the Atikamekw Nation and its Grand Chief Constant Awashish, who was recently re-elected to his position on Sept. 1. Awashish is also one of two company directors for Kino Aski, along with Belgian engineer and executive Yves Crits. According to filings with the federal government. Kino Aski was only established in June of 2026.


A Sept. 11 French-language press release from the Atikamekw Nation Council announced a memorandum of understanding to “explore potential opportunities for cooperation” between Kino Aski and Ukrainian state-owned company NaftoGaz, the largest oil and gas company in that country.


“Given the potential positive impacts of the Kino Aski project in bridging the socioeconomic gap experienced by our communities,” the Atikamekw Council writes in the release, “we have a responsibility and a duty to examine the feasibility of the Kino Aski project in light of Indigenous values, while respecting the territory and the environment.


“The current context of global geopolitical and energy uncertainty is leading the Canadian government to promote the export of Canadian natural resources, particularly natural gas, in order to generate wealth for Canadians and First Nations.”


Awashish said the agreement demonstrated that European partners were seeking reliable and diversified energy sources, and Canadian LNG could meet those needs.


“For First Nations,” he said, “it would also represent an opportunity to play a leading role in developing new economic and energy relationships between Canada and Europe.”


The Atikamekw Council press release notes that since Ottawa is providing financial support to encourage First Nations in western Canada to participate in economic development projects, the Atikamekw Nation is interested in developing opportunities for positive impacts on First Nations in the east of the country.


The Council adds that the project is only at the technical study phase, has not been confirmed and that no LNG pipeline route has been selected.


However, Lac Simon said it’s uneasy even with this level of commitment to the project.


“While members of the Anishnabe Nation of Lac Simon and the people of Quebec still lack access to official, comprehensive, and transparent information about the project,” the Council writes in its statement, “the Government of Canada has nevertheless chosen to present it to international investors in order to promote it. Such an approach is premature and risks giving the impression that the project can move forward, even though several fundamental steps remain to be taken.”


The Council said they wished to remind potential investors as well as the federal government that the gas pipeline project “must, without exception, obtain the consent of the Anishnabe Nation of Lac Simon and the other affected First Nations. This consent cannot be presumed, circumvented, or replaced by discussions conducted without the full and meaningful participation of the many affected First Nations.”


Most First Nations in Quebec — outside the Cree and Naskapi Nations and Inuit signatories to the James Bay Northern Quebec Agreement — have not ceded their ancestral territories. According to the release by Lac Simon, the proposed pipeline route would cross multiple unceded ancestral First Nations territories.


That means, they said, that Indigenous rights on those territories remain protected by Section 35 of the Constitution, and developers and governments cannot proceed without the consent of all affected Nations.


Lac Simon’s Council said a pipeline will never be a community …

author: winter oak
title: A poet of the rooted resistance
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


John Trudell (1946–2015)

 was a poet of the resistance against spirit-denying and culture-destroying industrial imperialism.


Machine money progress

Is the cause of our common abuse

 [1]


His initial focus was on defending the rights and autonomies of Native American peoples who had been so brutally crushed by the invading and occupying empire.


Indians are Jesus

Hanging from the cross

Hanging from the cross

In the name of their savior

Forcing on us

The trinity of the chain

Guilt sin and blame

 [2]


He wondered: “How did my land become somebody else’s country?” [3] and how other Americans could expect Indians to share in the national grief over 9/11.


Now you want us

To cry your tears for you

Already we’ve bled for you

Already been dead to you

Now you want us

To cry your tears for you


Chapters of a democracy story

Descendants of genocide

Twelve score and more years ago

We went from being the majority

To being the smallest minority

Now you want us

To cry your tears for you

 [4]


The modern tyranny demands that we forget who we are and where we came from so that we can be turned into disempowered, malleable and exploitable human resources for its global

mega-racket

. [5]


But Trudell, like so many of us, felt the soul of his ancestors stirring inside him and guiding his thoughts and actions.


In the 2005 documentary film

Trudell

, he explains: “I felt as if somebody knocked me unconscious when I entered the world. It’s been a lifetime trying to come to.


“I used to get this idea that I was in the wrong time in the wrong place. I thought that I came here a hundred years too late. The hundred years too late was because I used to see this camp on the plain amongst the trees by a river. It was a tribal camp and I felt I was part of it. It’s like these thoughts were memories. Every part was familiar and I was a part of the whole thing”. [6]


Too confused to care

Is no way to live

Young ones listen

Remember who you are

Remember where you are

Remember why you are

 [7]


In 1969, his sense of indigenous roots and connections was galvanized by the Indians of All Tribes occupation of Alcatraz Island.


He was the spokesman for this 19-month long action, which brought the plight of Native Americans into mainstream American consciousness, and he

went on

 to be national chairman of the American Indian Movement (AIM) from 1973 to 1979. [8]


All of this drew the attention of the corporate empire’s enforcement squads and between 1969 and 1979 the FBI amassed a 17,000-page dossier on him, one of the longest in the agency’s history. [9]


An internal FBI memo stated: “He is extremely eloquent… therefore extremely dangerous”. Trudell commented: “All I did was talk and they cracked down hard just for that”. [10]


“The majority of the American citizens agreed with us… The way the government operates, any time any group of people start to get popular support, this becomes a threat to the government. AIM got labelled by this Eastland Subcommittee on Unamerican Affairs as a terrorist organization.


“Between ’73 and ’75, the government with the FBI, they were literally waging a Contra war against now all the AIM people and the traditionalists”. [11]


On February 11, 1979 Trudell burned an American flag during a demonstration in front of the FBI HQ in Washington, DC, explaining: “In the military, they said if the flag has been desecrated, the only way to properly dispose of it is to burn it”. [12]


Some 12 hours later, a fire “of suspicious origin” burned down Trudell’s home on a reservation in Nevada, killing his pregnant wife, Tina, their three children and Tina’s mother.


Unsurprisingly, the FBI declined to investigate, and the blaze was officially ruled an “accident”. But Trudell insisted: “It was murder; they were murdered as an act of war”. [13]


Devastated by the tragedy, Trudell withdrew from the world for a time and found something within him, from beyond him.


“Putting my love into the ground like this, putting my love in boxes, putting them into the ground and covering them up reconnected me to the earth”. [14]


It was during this period of grief and rebirth that he discovered his poetic gift.


Sometimes me and my mind

Don’t get along very well and

Sometimes I need someone to talk to

And someone to cling to

A little bit of forever for a little while

Doing the rest of the life I can’t hide

I fell through some of the wounds …

author: Monthly Review Press
title: New! Chris dePloeg’s “The Exterminating Empire”
content:
REVIEWS:


Counterpunch

, “

Capitalism is Waging War on Palestine While Creating a Burning Planet

” by Daniel Falcone:


Daniel Falcone:

What is the central argument of

The Exterminating Empire

 and how is the book structured? It looks as though the book serves as an intervention as well as an addition to current scholarship.  


Chris Kaspar de Ploeg:

 I open the book with some jarring facts that seem paradoxical at first sight. We need about 30 percent of our productive capacity to

give everyone on the planet a good life

. Not just the basics like housing, clothing and healthcare, but also modern appliances like refrigerators, laptops, access to the internet and more. At the same time, that standard of living is denied to about

80 percent of the world population

. Green energy has been cheaper than fossil fuels for years, yet climate breakdown is only accelerating. We could

solve world hunger

 with about 0.03 percent of global GDP, but hunger is only increasing.


That looks like an extraordinarily wasteful system, and it is. The point, however, is that under capitalism, these are not paradoxes at all. In fact, they are signs of capital’s success. Under our current economic system, the primary goal, ruthlessly pursued, is

profit maximization

. That profit maximization is reached through pushing down costs–and we are those costs, our labour, our environments, our lives–and by conquering markets, often through a mix of military and economic warfare. That essentially puts

capitalism on a warpath against life

. The system is working exactly as it is supposed to.


We see, for example, that profit rates are higher in the fossil fuel industry because it essentially

functions through monopolies

, despite the higher costs. We see that the military-industrial complex is growing exponentially, targeting any vestiges of resistance against

US-led global hegemony

, which globalized harsh budget cuts in social welfare, healthcare and education. These very conditions of

structural impoverishment

 then create the conditions of desperation necessary for people and countries to accept their status as sources for cheap labour, resources and land for global corporations, mostly centered in the Global North.


In the book I write about a dialectic between slavery and genocide, and between structural genocide and active genocide. A good way to understand that relationship is by going back to the

We Charge Genocide petition

, which was presented in 1951 at the United Nations by William L. Patterson, on behalf of the

Civil Rights Congress

. He estimated that, since the abolition of slavery, some 10,000 black people had been lynched, often for something as small as looking a white woman in the eyes. These lynchings were not hidden affairs, but were a

public spectacle

, for which neighbors came together, and pictures were spread on postcards across the country.


Patterson

 goes on to argue that this kind of active violence serves a deeper purpose. It was meant to intimidate the black masses to accept lower living standards, functioning as a dehumanized workforce for corporations. At the time, this led 32,000 excess deaths every year among Black Americans compared to white death rates. Patterson charges this as a ‘genocide for profit’, based on the article in the UN convention that lists “

deliberately inflicting on the group conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction

.” Combining two studies that were done since that time, I show that between 1940 and 2020 the total excess death toll of African Americans is 6 million.


Nowadays, scholars tend to call this ‘

structural genocide

’. And I argue that this is a global phenomenon under capitalism. In a sense, the active genocide in Palestine is a lynching aimed at intimidating the Global South into accepting its role as devalued lives for Western profits. The blatant, live-streamed and openly announced nature of that genocide is exactly the point, just as the lynchings of the American South were broadcast widely. It is aimed to intimidate people, because the active genocide serves the broader, structural genocide.


The histories of

genocide and slavery

 are deeply intertwined. In fact, almost every genocide in history also deployed slave labor–even in the archetypical death camp, Auschwitz – and chattel slavery also contained genocidal dynamics of cheapened lives and heightened death rates. In a sense, even in Gaza the …

author: Novara Media
title: The Next Big Shock Is Coming — Green Energy Is the Only Way Out
content:
This summer’s weather has been record breaking in all the wrong ways. Extreme heat, droughts, crop failures, wildfires and thousands of excess deaths have left experts to realise that the climate is destabilising faster than predicted. In the face of this undeniable crisis, what should be done?


Tessa Khan is the founder of Uplift – an organisation that works to challenge the fossil fuel lobby and decarbonise our energy system before it’s too late. The former human rights lawyer realised a decade ago that none of the other social questions matter, if we don’t address the climate crisis. With family in Bangladesh, a nation with 175 million people, that is set to go underwater first, she understands what is at stake better than most. She also understands that Britain is rich in renewables, and the green transition is not just a challenge, but an opportunity to fix our broken economy.


Should Britain drill for more oil in the North Sea, or is this a distraction planted by the fossil fuel lobby? Should the energy system in Britain be nationalised? Are renewables also susceptible to economic shocks? What Can We Learn from the Transition from Oil to Gas? How Does the Ageing Population Impact Climate Politics? And what exactly should Andy Burnham do, on climate change?

title: The 3M Fingerprint: How Science Disproves the Pentagon’s Denial of Okinawa PFAS Pollution
content:
Carcinogenic aqueous film-forming foam at US Kadena Air Base coats the parking lot after an overhead sprinkler system in a hangar accidentally discharged on December 4, 2013.

‍ ‍


By Pat Elder,

Military Poisons

, September 13, 2026


Independent water testing around U.S. military installations in Okinawa has exposed a specific chemical signature—a 3M fingerprint—that strips away the Pentagon’s shield of plausible deniability. For years, the United States military and the Japanese central government have deflected requests from Okinawa Prefecture for on-base environmental inspections, citing a lack of causal evidence linking the bases to localized PFAS contamination. However, explosive reporting from the

Asahi Shimbun

 recently revealed that U.S. officials had privately admitted to Tokyo as early as 2023 that aqueous film-forming foam (AFFF) used at Kadena Air Base and Marine Corps Air Station Futenma was the likely source of pollution.


While governments actively concealed this admission from the public, definitive water testing from outside the base fences has cracked the case wide open, tracing the contamination directly back to legacy 3M electrochemical-fluorination chemistry.


Military Poisons’

2023 sampling

 found 28 PFAS compounds in Okinawan environmental samples, not merely PFOS and PFOA. The profile includes PFOS, PFHxS, PFDS, PFOSA, FOSAA, N-EtFOSAA, and N-MeFOSAA—compounds and related precursor materials associated with older PFOS chemistry made by electrochemical fluorination. Before 2000, 3M was the dominant global producer of the PFOS precursor chemistry used in this legacy AFFF formulation.


This profile makes the U.S. explanation of an unspecified source for PFAS contamination implausible. Coupled with the U.S. government’s reported acknowledgment that foam at Kadena and Futenma was likely responsible for PFAS contamination in the Okinawan environment, it establishes a compelling case for what Okinawa has requested for years: independent access, full sampling, and a public accounting of PFAS use, releases, and cleanup inside the bases.


Further proof – Marine Corps Air Station Futenma


142 tons of aqueous film-forming foam from Marine Corps Air Station Futenma

was buried

 at the Kurashiki industrial-waste landfill in 2014-2015. In 2023

Military Poisons tested

 the waters draining from the site and found high levels of PFAS with a distinctive 3M stamp.


The clearest legacy 3M/POSF electrochemical-fluorination (ECF) signature in this sample is the group I marked:


FOSAA — 1.2 ppt


N-EtFOSAA — 23.5 ppt


N-MeFOSAA — 23.1 ppt


PFOSA — 5.3 ppt


Note: POSF is short for perfluorooctane sulfonyl fluoride: C₈F₁₇SO₂F.


These are PFOS-related sulfonamide compounds/precursors tied to the older POSF chemistry that 3M historically dominated. Their presence together is much more meaningful than PFOS by itself.


Supporting, but not distinctive on their own: PFOS (236.5), PFHxS (102.3), PFDS (9), PFBS (81.3), and possibly PFHxSA (9.7). They fit an older ECF/PFOS-related profile.


POSF was the key chemical building block in 3M’s older PFOS chemistry. 3M used electrochemical fluorination to make POSF, then used it to manufacture PFOS and related compounds for products including older PFOS-based AFFF, Scotchgard-type treatments, paper coatings, and industrial surfactants.


In environmental samples, compounds such as PFOSA, FOSAA, N-EtFOSAA, and N-MeFOSAA point back to that larger POSF-derived chemical family. They tend to transform over time into PFOS.


So “a POSF/ECF signature” means a pattern consistent with the older 3M-style PFOS chemical family—not merely PFOS alone. The AFFF from Futenma came from 3M. The Navy/Marine Corps purchased and used massive quantities of AFFF from 3M.


Further Proof – Kadena Air Base


In May of 2024 Rachel Clark and I again joined with Okinawan activists to test waters flowing from U.S. military bases in Okinawa. We followed Ubu stream as close as we could to the point where it drains from Kadena Air Base.


The strongest observation in the Kadena sample is the PFOS + PFHxS pairing: together they are 785.5 ppt, about 60% of all detected PFAS in this sample. 3M’s older electrochemical-fluorination (ECF) – made AFFF is known for

PFOS dominance followed by PFHxS

 with smaller concentrations of  PFHpS and PFBS.


The scientific data gathered from the Ubu stream and the Kurashiki landfill acts as an unalterable forensic record. Because federal military …

title: Police Repression on Adivasis Resisting Mining in South Odisha Draw Condemnation from Citizens Forum
content:
The Odisha government’s use of police force against Adivasi communities resisting mining is intensifying. The Concerned Citizens Forum has condemned the forcible arrest of Niyamgiri Surakshya Samiti president Lada Sikaka, along with the deployment of armed police in the villages, where people have been resisting Vedanta’s Sijimali bauxite mining project.


 


Groundxero Desk


SEP 13, 2026


 


The Odisha government’s use of police force against Adivasi communities resisting mining projects on their land is intensifying. The Concerned Citizens Forum, with lawyers, human rights organizations, trade unions, citizens’ groups, and members of various political parties, has condemned the forcible arrest of Dongria Kandh leader and Niyamgiri Surakshya Samiti president Lada Sikaka by the Odisha police, along with the deployment of armed police in the villages of Kantamal and Talaampadar, where people have been resisting Vedanta’s Sijimali bauxite mining project. The Forum has demanded the immediate release of Sikaka and the withdrawal of armed forces from the villages.


 


Sikaka was reportedly intercepted near Kalyansinghpur on September 10 while returning with his lawyer and friends after securing bail in another case. He was forcibly taken away by an armed police team and, according to the Forum, moved between several locations before being produced in court late that night and sent to jail. The Forum also points to an old 9-year-old case (number 349/2017) against him which it says had been quashed by the Odisha High Court.


Niyamgiri Surakshya Samiti president Lada Sikaka


The arrest, however, is not an isolated episode. It comes amid a sustained campaign by the state- corporate nexus to criminalise Adivasi resistance to mining in South Odisha. Since Vedanta received the Sijimali mining lease in February 2023, villagers in Kashipur and Thuamul Rampur, under the leadership of Ma Mati Mali Suraksha Manch, have been resisting the mining project through peaceful and democratic means.


 


The Forum alleges that, rather than addressing their demands, the local administration with company henchmen has attempted to divide the communities and break the movement through police cases and arrests. It says at least 43 cases have been filed in three years and more than 100 Adivasis and Dalits have been jailed.


 


The Niyamgiri Suraksha Samiti, along with all peoples’ movements of South Odisha, has continuously shown solidarity and support to all these movements, appealing for a united struggle to protect Adivasi land and the hills, forests, rivers and streams.


 


Consequently, the advisor of the Niyamgiri Suraksha Samiti and the national editor of the Socialist People’s Council, Lingaraj Azad, who has been active in both Sijimali and Kutrumali, is still languishing in Bhawanipatna jail since March 25 despite securing bail in one case, while Hiramal Naik, a leading member of the Ma Mati Mali Suraksha Manch, was arrested on August 28 and denied bail after another case was brought against him.


 


For the Forum, the pattern is clear: the criminal justice system is being deployed to clear the ground for mining. As mining projects involving Vedanta, Adani and NALCO spread across the Eastern Ghats, communities defending their land, forests, water sources and cultural heritage are increasingly being treated as obstacles to “development”. The Forum warns that the arrests and police siege are intended to break resistance and facilitate the logistical infrastructure – roads, railway, etc – required for mining. The message the state-corporate nexus is sending is clear:  to raise a voice against mining companies is a crime – and that voice will be crushed.


 


The Forum demands the release of Lada Sikaka, Lingaraj Azad and Hiramal Naik, withdrawal of armed police from the villages of Kantamal and Talaampadar, and cancellation of the bauxite mining leases.


 


The full Press Statement along with the signatories is published below.

Bhubaneswar, Odisha


Date: 12 September, 2026


 


On September 10, 2026, at around 4:30 PM, Lada Sikaka, a Dongria Kandh leader of the Niyamgiri Surakshya Samiti, was returning to his village with his lawyer and six friends after securing bail in one case from Lanjigarh Court, when their vehicle was intercepted near …

title: Volkswagen’de uzlaşma sınıf mücadelesine darbe
content:
Almanya'da Volkswagen işçileri eylemi (Fotoğraf: IG Metall sendikası)

Otomotiv sektörünün Almanya’daki durumu sınıf mücadelesinin olumsuz bir örneği. Patronlar kazançlarını sürdürüyor ama istedikleri kârı elde edemediklerini savunuyor. Bunun sorumlusu olarak maliyet yüksekliğini gösteriyor ve Almanya’daki fabrikaları kapatacaklarını ilan ediyor. Sendikalar ve işyeri işçi temsilcilikleri ise kendi taleplerini sunup bunları mücadele ile dayatmak yerine patronların tehditlerini yumuşatmak için taviz verme yolunu tercih ediyorlar. Volkswagen’daki durum en açık örnek. Fabrika kapatılmayacak, on binlerce işçi sokağa atılacak, otomobil üretilemezse tank üretilecek. Bu içerikli uzlaşmaya işçilerin “teşekkür” istenmesi ise teslimiyetin daniskası.

Fransa’da şirketlere aktarılan kamu kaynakları GSYH’nin yaklaşık yüzde 11’ine ulaşırken, bu devasa desteğin aslan payını da en büyük şirketler alıyor. Prim muafiyetleri, vergi kredileri ve sübvansiyonlar aracılığıyla şirketlere aktarılan milyarlar, kamu hizmetleri ve toplumsal ihtiyaçlar için kaynak bulunmadığı gerekçesiyle kemer sıkma politikaları dayatılırken büyümeye devam ediyor. CNRS ekonomisti Anne-Laure Delatte, etkinliği kanıtlanmayan bu desteklerin sorgulanmasını savunuyor. Bu hafta Fransa’dan çevirdiğimiz röportaj, kamu kaynaklarının toplumsal refah yerine büyük şirketlerin kârlarını ve servetlerini büyüten bir mekanizmaya nasıl dönüştürüldüğünü ortaya koyuyor.

İngiltere’de aşırı sıcaklar artık sadece yaz aylarında yaşanan bir rahatsızlık değil, birçok işçi için doğrudan bir çalışma koşulu meselesi. Kuzey Londra’daki yaklaşık 1500 otobüs işçisinin grevleri, patronları klima konusunda geri adım atmaya ve otobüslere klima takma sözü vermeye zorladı. Ancak işçilerin mücadelesi bununla sınırlı değil; tuvaletlere erişim, çalışma saatleri ve yorgunluk gibi sorunlar da hâlâ gündemde. Counterfire, bu mücadelenin nasıl kazanıldığını ve sıcaklarla karşı karşıya kalan diğer işçilerin bundan ne öğrenebileceğini sendika temsilcisi Peter Skinner ile konuştu.

Stephan Krull Neues Deutschland/Almanya

Volkswagen’in işten çıkarma programına ilişkin uzlaşma, çalışanlar için çok kötü ve ortak karar alma ilkesine bir darbe niteliğinde.

VW denetleme kurulunun oy birliğiyle aldığı karar, işçiler için bir darbe oldu. Hannover’in Yeşiller Partisinden belediye başkanı Belit Onay, “Tehdit edilen kapanma şimdilik gündemden kalktı, ancak çalışanlar ve fabrikalar için belirsizlik devam ediyor. Net ve güvenilir beklentiler hâlâ yok” dedi. Haklı ve yalnız değil: “Yönetimin hatalarının bedelini nihayetinde çalışanların ödemesi, yönetimin ise kararlarını dayatması kabul edilemez.”

IG Metall sendikasının şiddetli muhalefetine rağmen, denetleme kurulu oy birliğiyle 50 bin işçiyi daha işten çıkarmaya, daha az çalışanla daha fazla araba (yılda 900 bin) piyasaya sürmeye, yatırımları azaltmaya ve satışlardan elde edilen kârı yüzde 9’a çıkarmaya karar verdi. İşyeri İşçi Temsilciliği, yükün “tek taraflı olarak” işçiler tarafından taşınmaması gerektiğini belirtiyor. Ancak kârların yılda 30 milyar avronun üzerine çıkması gerekiyorsa, karardaki yük paylaşımı düzenlemesi zaten çok tek taraflı. Bu, Aralık 2024’teki toplu iş sözleşmesinin ardından ikinci kez oluyor; bu sözleşme ücret kesintilerini ve uzatılmış çalışma saatlerini içeriyordu ve işçiler için önemli bir yük oluşturuyordu. İşyeri İşçi Temsilciliği ve IG Metall sendikası hiçbir/herhangi bir fabrika kapanışının “kesinleşmediğini” ilan ettiğinde, bu ancak maliyetlerin önemli ölçüde düşürülmesi koşuluyla geçerli oluyor.

Çin’den gelen rekabet ve piyasa gelişmelerini göz önünde bulundurursak, bunun işe yaramayacağı öngörülebilir. Örneğin Hannover fabrikasında araç başına maliyetler, düşük kapasite kullanımı nedeniyle çok yüksek. Ve bu düşük kapasite kullanımı, yönetim kurulunun VW Bulli üretimini Türkiye’ye taşımasından kaynaklanıyor. Dolayısıyla, birçok fabrikanın gelecek beklentisi yok ve ne IG Metall ne de işçi temsilciliği otomobil, otomobil ve daha fazla otomobilden başka bir şey düşünüyor. Ve eğer bu da işe yaramazsa, SPD’li Eyalet Başbakanı ve Denetleme Kurulu üyesi Olaf Lies gibi, silah üretimine yöneliyorlar.

İşyeri İşçi Temsilciliği ve IG Metall sendikasına göre, Aşağı Saksonya eyaletiyle birlikte “çatışmanın tehlikeli bir şekilde tırmanmasını” önlediler. Bunu başarmak için tüm taraflar tavizler vermişti. Ancak sadece iki hafta önce, IG Metall Başkanı Christiane Benner, yönetim kurulunun kâr hedeflerini “hayal ürünü” olarak eleştirmişti. Şimdi …

title: Amed’s concrete towers threaten its historic skyline and community life
content:
Amed (Diyarbakır) is rapidly losing a culture of urban life that developed over millennia within its city walls, courtyard houses and narrow streets. A city that has witnessed civilisations, wars, migrations and natural disasters over thousands of years is now overshadowed by concrete blocks rising into the sky and the social fragmentation they bring with them. The rapid spread of high-rise development in Amed in recent years is reshaping the city’s collective memory, social relations and skyline.


Amed historically had a horizontal urban culture. Basalt-stone houses with courtyards and gardens, streets where neighbours’ doors opened onto one another, and neighbourhood solidarity built around shared water sources were among its most distinctive features. The 1965 Development Plan, which allowed apartment construction outside the city walls, followed by regulations that provided a legal basis for multi-storey reinforced-concrete buildings even within the walled city, marked the first major rupture in this horizontal urban memory. Over time, outlying neighbourhoods such as Rêzan (Bağlar), Peyas (Kayapınar) and Bajarê Nû (Yenişehir) filled first with informal housing built by impoverished people migrating from rural areas, and later with rapidly expanding and largely uncontrolled apartment development.


The situation today has moved well beyond the construction of multi-storey housing. Towers, residential complexes and high-rise blocks integrated with shopping centres have risen across the city and are now visible from virtually every vantage point overlooking its historic centre. Amed’s ancient skyline is no longer defined by the bastions of its city walls, but by glass-fronted towers adorned with advertisements promising a “modern lifestyle”.


A city rebuilt under government-appointed trustees


Suriçi was undoubtedly the site of the most painful and symbolic manifestation of this transformation. The demolitions carried out by the state in the Alipaşa and Lalebey neighbourhoods following the 2015–2016 self-government resistance were subsequently turned into a reconstruction project under the banner of “urban transformation”, within a framework determined by the central government and the Housing Development Administration of Turkey (TOKI), disregarding the will of local residents and the objections of the elected local administration. The destruction of these neighbourhoods, which carried thousands of years of human history and cultural heritage, could not be justified on technical or urban-planning grounds.


The new housing built after the demolitions left many rights holders burdened with heavy debts. Architecturally, despite claims that the buildings reflected the “authentic fabric of Diyarbakır”, they became standardised and anonymous structures with no meaningful relationship to the city’s actual urban fabric. The underlying purpose of this process was to alter the demographic structure of Suriçi and remove its long-established residents from its historic neighbourhoods. This was not merely a question of urban planning, but directly a process of engineering memory and identity.


How does concrete destroy neighbourhood life?


One of the least discussed yet most destructive consequences of high-rise development is the breakdown it causes in social relations. In courtyard houses, neighbours’ doors once opened onto one another, children grew up together in the streets, and women sustained everyday forms of solidarity on rooftops and in courtyards. In gated high-rise complexes equipped with security cameras, neighbourly relations are increasingly reduced to little more than making eye contact in a lift. The concept of the “mahalle” (neighbourhood), cultivated in Amed over centuries as a sense of community built around shared sorrow, joy and resistance, is rapidly being eroded by the individualism of high-rise and gated living.


This fragmentation is not accidental. Social solidarity networks in Kurdish cities have historically sustained both cultural continuity and political resistance. Replacing neighbourhoods, streets and courtyards with an urban model made up of isolated and disconnected gated complexes also weakens these networks of solidarity, collective memory and the capacity for resistance. Every intervention in the physical fabric of a city is, in effect, an intervention in its social relations.


In whose name is the skyline changing?

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Cagayan Valley activists deny terror financing raps, call for repeal of terror laws
content:
Former Kabataan Party-list Cagayan Valley regional coordinator Jhames Paredes in the protest in front of Department of Justice. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

MANILA – “Poor farmers do not have the capacity to fund terrorism. We are already poor. Where are we going to find the money?”

This is the lament of Renato Gameng, a farmer for 40 years and a leader of Danggayan Dagiti Mannalon iti Isabela (Dagami) for the past 15 years. For him, it is puzzling that he is being accused of violating the Terrorism Financing Prevention and Suppression Act (TFPSA). Ten more activists were also charged with the same case before the Department of Justice’s National Prosecution Service.

Under the banner of human rights group Karapatan, the Cagayan Valley activists, including Gameng, and other human rights defenders held a protest in front of the Supreme Court (SC) and DOJ to denounce the use of twin terror laws– Anti-Terrorism Act and TFPSA– against activists. They submitted a letter to Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, calling for the review and repeal of the twin terror laws.

“The Supreme Court, as the guardian of the Constitution and the final arbiter of constitutional rights, has the solemn duty to ensure that laws enacted in the name of national security do not become instruments for suppressing constitutionally protected dissent,” the letter stated, signed by victims of the twin terror laws.

Just last month, six activists in Cagayan Valley received subpoenas including Gameng. They are former Kabataan Party-list Cagayan Valley regional coordinator Jhames Paredes; National Council of Churches in the Philippines program assistant and Taripnong Cagayan Valley secretariat member Anne Pascual; Bayan Muna Cagayan Valley coordinator Nelson Escalante; Punganay Cagayan Valley coordinator Marifel Macalanda; and Kabataan Party-list regional coordinator Walter Villegas.

Meanwhile, five others have been previously slapped with similar complaints in January 2025. They are Isabelo Adviento, a former fourth nominee of Anakpawis Party-list; Makabayan Cagayan Valley regional coordinator Agnes Mesina; Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas National Council member Cita Managuelod; Karapatan National Council member Jackie Valencia; and Pinoy Weekly journalist Deo Montesclaros.

“This new wave of attacks against us is alarming because for them, our advocacy of providing services for the farmers, campaign for more budget in education and classrooms, and proper disaster response are terrorism,” said Paredes during the protest.

Paredes is a student at University of the Philippines (UP) and a former contributor of Northern Dispatch, an alternative media outfit reporting people’s issues in Northern Luzon.

“Of course, the initial reaction was fear when we first heard it. Because the main objective of filing these cases is to sow fear, silence us, and stop us from joining organizations that defend our rights,” Paredes told Bulatlat in Filipino. “However, this fear does not last long. There are many people who were also charged with these cases which were later dismissed. This is a form of judicial harassment.”

Three activists of Cagayan Valley filed their counter-affidavits before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor in Tuguegarao City, Cagayan, before they went to the DOJ and SC in Manila.

The case stemmed from statements made by alleged military assets Elnan Tul-ag and Rex Pagbilao, who claimed they had received supplies from the activists inside an alleged New People’s Army encampment in 2019.

Local human rights organization Umaddang Cagayan Valley Para ti Karbengan said that the only evidence against the 11 Cagayan Valley activists was an uncooked rice, allegedly found decaying inside plastic containers buried underground for seven full years.

“Our protest is not only for Cagayan Valley 11 (activists), but to all victims of political persecution and judicial harassment such as the recent attacks against the Kasibu and Dupax del Norte. This is also for all our political prisoners in the region,” Paredes said.

The activists of Cagayan Valley are targeted because of their continuous defense of the natural resources, Enjo Sarmiento of the Center for Environmental Concerns said.

author: groundxero
title: এসবিআই-এর পশ্চিমবঙ্গের চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারীদের আন্দোলনে আইনি ও পথের লড়াইতে জোর ত্রিবার্ষিক দ্বিতীয় সম্মেলনে
content:
স্টেট ব্যাঙ্ক অফ ইন্ডিয়া কন্ট্র্যাক্টচুয়াল ওয়ার্কার্স অ্যাসোসিয়েশন, বেঙ্গল সার্কেল-এর ত্রিবার্ষিক দ্বিতীয় সম্মেলনে দাবি উঠল ঠিকা প্রথা বাতিল করে সমস্ত চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মীদের স্থায়ীকরণের।


 


সুদর্শনা চক্রবর্তীর প্রতিবেদন


 


স্টেট ব্যাঙ্ক অফ ইন্ডিয়ার চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারীদের সংগঠন – স্টেট ব্যাঙ্ক অফ ইন্ডিয়া কন্ট্র্যাক্টচুয়াল ওয়ার্কার্স অ্যাসোসিয়েশন, বেঙ্গল সার্কেল-এর ত্রিবার্ষিক দ্বিতীয় সম্মেলন অনুষ্ঠিত হল কলকাতার মহাজাতি সদনে ১২ অগাস্ট, ২০২৬। উপস্থিত ছিলেন রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন জেলার প্রায় ১০০০ এসবিআই-এর চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারী, যাঁরা এই অ্যাসোসিয়েশন-এর সদস্য। ২০২৩ সালের ২৯ মে এই সংগঠনের পথ চলা শুরু। গত তিন বছর ধরে বিভিন্ন কর্মসূচীর মধ্যে দিয়ে রাজ্য জুড়ে এসবিআই-এর চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারীদের স্থায়ীকরণ ও অন্যান্য দাবিদাওয়া নিয়ে আন্দোলন, পাশাপাশি বিভিন্ন রিজিয়ন ও জেলাস্তরের কর্মচারীদের নিজেদের অধিকার, আইনি প্রক্রিয়া ও দাবি আদায়ের আন্দোলন বিষয়ে সচেতনতা বাড়ানোর কাজও চলেছে সমান ভাবে। এবং আগামীতেও এই পথেই চলার প্রতিশ্রুতি দিয়েই শেষ হয় দ্বিতীয় সম্মেলন। স্লোগান ওঠে – “ঠিকা প্রথা বন্ধ্য করো”, “কোম্পানি হটাও/শ্রমিক বাঁচাও”।


 


এই সম্মেলনের শুরুতেই সম্পাদকীয় প্রতিবেদনে যে মূল দাবিগুলি তুলে ধরা হয় –


 


১)

ঠিকা প্রথা বিশ্রি রোগ স্থায়ী নিয়োগ চালু হোক


 


২) সমস্ত চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মীদের স্থায়ীকরণ করতে হবে


 


৩) অক্টোবর ২০১৭ থেকে চালু এসবিআই-এর এ, বি ও সি জোন বন্ধ করে সমস্ত চুক্তিভিত্তিক শ্রমিকদের এ জোন-এর বেতন দিতে হবে


 


৪) চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মীদের দিয়ে সব ধরনের কাজ করানো ও অতিরিক্ত সময়ে আটকানো চলবে না।


 


সম্মেলনে রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন জেলা থেকে অ্যাসোসিয়েশন-এর সদস্যরা উপস্থিত হয়ে নিজেদের বক্তব্য তুলে ধরেন


এদিনের সম্মেলনে রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন জেলা থেকে অ্যাসোসিয়েশন-এর সদস্যরা উপস্থিত হয়ে নিজেদের বক্তব্য তুলে ধরেন। ছিলেন কলকাতার বিভিন্ন রিজিয়ন, উত্তর ২৪ পরগণা, দক্ষিণ ২৪ পরগণা, পূর্ব বর্ধমান, পশ্চিম বর্ধমান, হুগলি, বাঁকুড়ার সদস্যরা। তাঁদের সংক্ষিপ্ত বক্তব্যে যে বিষয়গুলি বারেবারে উঠে আসে সেগুলি হল –


 


১৮ থেকে ৬০ বছর নারী, পুরুষ চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারী হিসাবে নিযুক্ত হন। ম্যানেজার-এর চাপ, নিজেদের চাকরি বাঁচানোর তাগিদে তাঁদের নির্দিষ্ট কাজের বাইরে প্রচুর কাজ করতে হয়। এই মানসিক চাপ যাতে আর না থাকে সেই নিয়ে ইউনিয়নকে কাজ করতে হবে।


 


চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মীদের লকারের চাবিতে হাত দেওয়া একেবারেই নিষিদ্ধ। কিন্তু ব্যাঙ্কের স্থায়ী কর্মী, আধিকারিকেরা অনেক সময়েই তাঁদের এই কাজে বাধ্য করেন।


 


ইউনিয়নকে কাজ করতে হবে চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারীদের বোনাস কী হবে, এবিসি জোন-এর ক্ষেত্রে আইনি প্রক্রিয়া কী হবে সে বিষয়গুলি নিয়ে।


 


এমন কর্মচারীরাও বক্তব্য রাখেন যাঁরা সাময়িকভাবে কাজ হারিয়েছেন ব্যাঙ্ক কর্তৃপক্ষ বা আধিকারিকদের সঙ্গে মতান্তরের কারণে। অথচ যাঁরা ভরসা রাখছেন ইউনিয়ন-এর অবস্থানের জন্য, ভরসা রাখছেন আবার কাজ ফিরে পাওয়ার।

“ব্রাঞ্চ ম্যানেজারের সঙ্গে ঝামেলায় আমাকে বসিয়ে দেওয়া হয়েছে। ইউনিয়ন আছে বলে সাহস আর বিশ্বাস আছে যে, কাজ আবার ফিরে পাবই,”

 বললেন এক তরুণ চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারী।


 


এসবিআই কর্তৃপক্ষ বা ম্যানেজমেন্ট-এর দ্বিচারিতা নিয়ে মুখ খোলেন প্রায় সকলেই। এক ধরনের ভয় চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারীদের মধ্যে এই বিষয়ে কাজ করে যেত। ব্যাঙ্ক চৌহদ্দির মধ্যে পরিস্কার-পরিচ্ছন্নতা বজায় রাখা বা হাউসকিপিং-এর কাজ যা চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারীদের জন্য নির্দিষ্ট তার বাইরে যাবতীয় কাজ করানো হয় তাঁদের দিয়ে। বক্তব্যে উঠে আসে ২০১২ সাল পর্যন্ত তিন দশক, চার দশক ক্যাজুয়াল ওয়ার্কার হিসাবে কাজ করেছেন যাঁরা, তাঁদের স্থায়ী না করার জন্য চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারীদের রূপান্তরিত করা হয়। সমস্যা দেখা দেয়, যখন তাঁদের দিয়ে নির্দিষ্ট কাজের অতিরিক্ত করিয়ে নেওয়ার ক্ষেত্রে ‘ব্যাঙ্কের কর্মী’ বলা হয় আর অন্যদিকে চুক্তি-কর্মীরা যখনই নিজেদের ন্যায্য দাবি-দাওয়ার কথা জানান, তখনই বলে দেওয়া হয়, এগুলি অন্যায়, কারণ তাঁরা আদপে ব্যাঙ্কের কর্মীই নন। বাইরের কোম্পানির দ্বারা তাঁদের নিয়োগ হয়েছে। ফলত এই শোষনে, ম্যানেজমেন্ট-এর বিরূদ্ধে লড়াইকে একভাবে পুঁজিবাদের বিরূদ্ধে লড়াই বলেই দেখছেন ইউনিয়ন-এর সদস্যরা।


 


কর্মচারীরা জানান, কোনো কোনো ক্ষেত্রে নিয়োগকারী কোম্পানির সঙ্গে ভালো সম্পর্ক থাকলেও অনেক ক্ষেত্রেই এই রিক্রুটিং কোম্পানিগুলি কর্মচারীদের প্রাপ্য মাইনের টাকা নিয়ে বঞ্চনা করছে। একটি সুনির্দিষ্ট কোম্পানি যেমন নিয়োগ হওয়া কর্মচারীদের চার মাসের টাকা আত্মসাৎ করে চলে যায়। কোম্পানি পিএফ, ইএসআই কিছুই দেয় না, তারা কোনো রকম তহবিল হস্তান্তর করে না, এমনকি কর্মচারীদের অবসরের পরেও নয়। যা কিছু কর্মচারীদের নিজেদেরই করতে হয়। তাই শুধু ইউনিয়ন নেতৃত্ব নয়, তার সদস্যদেরও নিজেদের অর্থনৈতিক নিরাপত্তা সুনিশ্চিত করতে সচেতন ও সক্রিয় হওয়ার ভাবনাটি গুরত্ব পায় এই আলোচনায়।


 


এই চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারীদের কোনোও টাইম টেবিল থাকে না। থাকে না ছুটির নির্দিষ্ট সময়। অথচ চুক্তিভিত্তিক হওয়াতে অতিরিক্ত সময়ের জন্য ওভারটাইম-এরও কোনো প্রশ্ন ওঠে না। অন্যদিকে সিজিএম, ডিজিএম-রা যখন ব্যাঙ্ক পরিদর্শনে আসেন, তখন প্রথমেই এই চুক্তিভিত্তিক কর্মচারীদের হাউজকিপিং-এ খুঁত ধরা হয়। এক কর্মী বলেন,

title: Clôture de la rencontre Arts, Résistances et Rébellions au Caracol Jacinto Canek, Chiapas
content:
Après 29 jours, et avec plus d'un millier de participants venus de presque 40 pays différents, vient de s'achever la série de présentations, d'ateliers et de performances que les camarades zapatistes ont convoqués et organisés sur leur territoire. Ils nous ont annoncé la présence de 1111 zapatistes à Mexico, 20 ans après leur dernière venue, pour se tenir aux côtés des Mères et Pères cherchant sans relâche leurs proches disparus* à travers tout le pays.


Textes et photos par : Alexis & Piankov


Traduction de l'espagnol : Claudio


Après 29 jours, et avec plus d'un millier de participants venus de presque 40 pays différents, vient de s'achever la série de présentations, d'ateliers et de performances que les camarades zapatistes ont convoqués et organisés sur leur territoire. Ils nous ont annoncé la présence de 1111 zapatistes à Mexico, 20 ans après leur dernière venue, pour se tenir aux côtés des Mères et Pères cherchant sans relâche leurs proches disparus* à travers tout le pays.


Durant toute la rencontre, et jusqu'à sa clôture, ont eu lieu des performances musicales, de la poésie et de la prose, tant de la part des zapatistes eux-mêmes que des participants extérieurs. Les ateliers furent variés : impressions de sérigraphie sur t-shirt ou papier, auto-défense féminine, marches en territoire zapatiste pour explorer la biodiversité et les paysages volcaniques caractéristiques des montagnes du sud-est mexicain, entre autres.


Sur la scène centrale s'est tenue la représentation d'un groupe de jeunes zapatistes autour de la pièce «

 

Le commun et le jour d'après

 

», qui renoue avec les principes d'une vie harmonieuse entre les membres d'une communauté et la nature, à travers l'organisation. Avec une emphase sur l'abolition des violences patriarcales, de la propriété privée et des vieux travers de l'ancienne société. Se sont cultivés le partage, la solidarité et l'empathie en faveur d'une vie commune pour éliminer le système capitaliste.


Cette œuvre nous invite à réfléchir sur les jours à venir, sur la force et l'organisation que nous devons avoir pour ne pas permettre au capitalisme de ressurgir. Car nous savons que, comme une maladie, il sera latent pendant plusieurs années, à nous guetter

 

; et que sûrement les survivants qui n'auront pas commencé tout de suite à s'organiser autrement reproduiront les mêmes logiques qu'auparavant, simplement car il n'auront pas su faire autrement. Mais il nous faut etre plus fort et astucieux. D'où l'importance de réaliser de telles rencontres, qui nous permettent de continuer à nous confronter à d'autres réalités, d'échanger des connaissances et de maintenir vivant l'espoir.


En plus de la pièce et de la force d'organisation que nous ont démontrés nos camarades zapatistes lors de cette rencontre, ils nous ont laissé dans le cœur leur grande générosité et un exemple pour faire les choses différemment. Les soirées à danser, les journées radieuses avec les enfants jouant et illuminant tout sur leur passage. Des mères, des pères, et toute une communauté prenant soin collectivement les uns des autres. Femmes et hommes jouant au basket, aux échecs, échangeant des blagues avec les étrangers. Cette rencontre nous aura laissé la montagne et la pleine lune dans les bras, la nourriture, la nature, et au loin le Winikton (l'homme de pierre) observant nos pas.


Sans aucun doute, tout ceci a constitué un espace de formation à travers la culture. Des anciens combattants chantant sur la prise de San Cristobal jusqu'au jeunes poètes chantant à la liberté, les expressions artistiques ont appuyé le fait que les luttes en commun pour les communs sont des outils pour sauver ce qui nous reste d'humanité et arriver au jour d'après.


Finalement, lors de la clôture de l'évènement, le sous-commandant Moisés a insisté sur la nécessité de nous organiser chacun sur son territoire, de faire du «

 

buen vivir

 

» (du «

 

bon vivre **

 

») un art - que le système capitaliste nous a dénié -, de l'importance de partager les savoirs, de la convergence de nos actions, et surtout de la persévérance dans cette lutte qui avance lentement mais sûrement.


*Les personnes disparues au Mexique constituent un phénomène massif, en lien avec la violence du crime organisé.

** Le «

 

Buen Vivir

 

», ou «

 

Lekil Kaltik

 

» en maya Tseltal, est la pratique quotidienne de l'autonomie …

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: How banana plantation puts Bukidnon Lumad into turmoil
content:
A total of 195 hectares of Sëzukadang were placed under a collective certificate of land ownership award (CLOA). The beneficiaries—who are non-Lumad—leased it to banana production company Green Arrow Agriventures Incorporated (GAAVI), a subsidiary of agribusiness Kennemer Foods International.


DON CARLOS, Bukidnon — The presence of a banana plantation has deprived an Indigenous peoples community control of their entire ancestral land.


The Lumad living in Sëzukadang (the native name of Barangay New Visayas) in Don Carlos, Bukidnon, cannot assert their rights over the land that their ancestors lived in since time immemorial. They have also been disturbed by the plantation’s agricultural drone spraying which affected their health and livelihood, and by the attempt to establish fences to allegedly prevent them access.


Sëzukadang is the home of the Ompigan Clan belonging to Kirintëkën-Ilantungën Mënuvu, which is a subgroup of the Erumanen ne Mënuvu tribe that has settled in Bukidnon and Cotabato. The more than 2,000-hectare Sëzukadang is part of the more than 40,000 hectares of the tribe’s unified ancestral domain covering some areas in the towns of Don Carlos, Pangantucan, and Kalilangan in Bukidnon.


Tribal Chieftain Datu Benjie Ompigan explained to a small group of reporters who visited their community that prior to the issuance of their certificate of ancestral domain title (CADT) in 2016, their land was placed under Community-Based Forest Management Agreement (CBFMA), a production sharing contract, in 1992. It expired in 2017.


Tribal Chieftain Datu Benjie Ompigan leads a ritual prior to the start of a buron-buron (discussion) held in the Sëzukadang community in Don Carlos, Bukidnon, on September 4, 2026. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat


It was in 2019 when the community learned and was able to confirm that 195 hectares of Sëzukadang were placed under a collective certificate of land ownership award (CLOA), a document issued by the government to provide ownership to qualified landless farmers and farmworkers. 


The beneficiaries—who are non-Lumad—leased it to banana production company Green Arrow Agriventures Incorporated (GAAVI), a subsidiary of agribusiness Kennemer Foods International.


What confuses the tribe members was that the collective CLOA was issued by the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) in 2011 despite an existing CBFMA contract at that time.


Ompigan said they used to occupy more than a hectare only of the 2,000 hectares of Sëzukadang. However, they were able to reclaim a total of seven hectares now through reforestation. Asked if they would continue their collective action to recover more lands, he said they ceased for now to avert any escalated conflict.


“Because of our pushback, in 2019, before Covid, residents from three barangays went to us,” he said in the vernacular. “There is a commotion. Since we believed in the name of spirits, I asked my colleagues to control their emotions considering that there were children with us.”


The Lumad community decided to wait for the resolution on the Agrarian Law Implementation (ALI) case pending before the DAR secretary. The petition seeks to cancel the issued collective CLOA.


Fence them out


The Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center (LRC), a non-government organization that serves as a support group for the Kirintëkën-Ilantungën Mënuvu tribe, reported in May that GAAVI-Kennemer was in the process of establishing a perimeter fence after holes were seen in the area.


A hole allegedly dug up by GAAVI-Kennemer personnel for the establishment of a perimeter fence. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat


After a few days, the community found out that company personnel were in the process of cementing the fence.


Cemented parts of the planned perimeters were placed on the ground after their removal. Photo by Franck Dick Rosete/Bulatlat


Prior to these incidents, in April, a

pulong-pulong

 (a customary practice of discussion) was held in the community’s meeting place to talk about the concerns of the Lumad. The meeting was participated in by the affected Indigenous families together with representatives of DAR, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP), and the World Bank.


Ompigan said they reached out to these agencies following the attempted fencing, which prompted the World Bank to direct DAR to investigate the matter.

title: Caminata de Warmis: “Pachamama pide a gritos que la defendamos”
content:
Durante más de un mes mujeres de la Cuenca de Pozuelos, en la Puna jujeña, recorrieron el país hasta llegar al Congreso de la Nación reclamando un freno al extractivismo contaminante que está destruyendo el agua y la tierra de sus comunidades. En Buenos Aires, la Policía de la Ciudad las hostigó y ningún legislador quiso recibirlas. Dialogamos con Florencia Solís, una de las impulsoras de la Caminata, para compartir un balance sobre esta travesía de denuncia y visibilización.

La movilización conocida como Caminata de Warmis – Mujeres del Kollasuyu en defensa de la Pachamama (en Instagram:

@caminata.warmis

), partió el 3 de agosto desde Rinconada, Jujuy, a 3.500 metros sobre el nivel del mar, y atravesó localidades de todo el país, del norte hacia la Capital, donde mantuvieron encuentros con comunidades y el activismo ambiental.


Decidieron la fecha porque agosto es, entre otras cosas, el mes de la Pachamama.


En la Ciudad de Buenos Aires realizaron diversas actividades, entre las cuales la central fue la movilización hasta el Congreso de la Nación. En ese trayecto fueron hostigadas por efectivos policiales, tanto en la caminata por Avenida Rivadavia partiendo desde Once -donde quedaron impactadas tras ver “mucha gente abandonada, mucha pobreza”, dijo Florencia, conmovida porque en su comunidad “en mi lugar mío, no hay eso”- como en los alrededores del Congreso.


Allí ningún legislador las recibió, pero por la insistencia, al menos les recibieron los petitorios.


Finalmente, y tras más de un mes de recorrer el país, las Warmis volvieron a Jujuy. Desde allí, telefónicamente, hablamos con Florencia Solís, para hacer un balance de todo lo vivido.

title: The Saddle Lake Cree Nation, located northeast of Edmonton near St. Paul, says health care is a…
content:
The Saddle Lake Cree Nation, located northeast of Edmonton near St. Paul, says health care is a right under Treaty 6 and falls under its inherent jurisdiction. The First Nation has invoked the “medicine chest clause” provision from the treaty signed in 1876, which Indigenous Peoples interpret as a promise to provide comprehensive health care. “All children, including trans and two-spirit children and their family, will have safety under our treaty,” Saddle Lake Chief Dale Steinhauer said on Wednesday.

title: Şiddetten kaçan engelli kadın için sığınma evine ulaşmak daha zor: Erişilebilir bina yetmez, erişilebilir sığınma hizmeti ihtiyaç
content:
Şiddete maruz bırakılan bir kadın evinden ayrılmaya karar verdiğinde güvenli bir yere ulaşabilmek için çoğu zaman polis, Şiddet Önleme ve İzleme Merkezi (ŞÖNİM), belediyelerin danışma birimleri veya destek hatlarıyla iletişime geçmek zorunda. Ancak bu süreç, her kadın için aynı ölçüde erişilebilir değil. Kadın engelliyse şiddetten uzaklaşmanın önündeki engellere; erişilemeyen binalar, iletişim kanallarındaki sorunlar, işaret dili desteğinin bulunmaması, kişisel bakım ihtiyacının karşılanmaması ve ayrımcı kabuller de ekleniyor.

Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığının 2025 Yılı Faaliyet Raporu’na göre Türkiye’de bakanlığa, yerel yönetimlere, bir sivil toplum kuruluşuna ve Göç İdaresi Başkanlığı’na bağlı toplam 151 kadın konukevi bulunuyor. 3 bin 726 kapasiteli bu kuruluşlar, aynı yıl kadınlar ve beraberlerindeki çocuklar dâhil 62 bin 698 kişiye hizmet sundu. Türkiye genelindeki 86 ŞÖNİM’e yapılan başvuru sayısı ise 310 bin 136 olarak kayda geçti.

Ancak Bakanlığın raporunda kadın konukevlerine başvuran veya bu kuruluşlardan yararlanan engelli kadınların sayısı, engel grupları, kabul ve yönlendirme süreçleri ayrı ayrı açıklanmıyor. Dolayısıyla kritik sorular yanıtsız kalıyor: Kaç engelli kadın sığınma talebinde bulundu? Kaçı kabul edildi? Kaçı öz bakım veya iletişim desteği sağlanamadığı için başka bir kuruma yönlendirildi? Avukat Deniz Yazgan’a göre veri eksikliği, ayrımcılığın boyutunu da görünmez hâle getiriyor: “Hangi engel gruplarında ret veya yönlendirme yoğunlaşıyor? Hangi makul düzenlemeler talep ediliyor ve bunların ne kadarı karşılanıyor?”

Mor Çatı Gönüllüsü Kübra Karagöz ise engelli kadınların karşılaştığı sorunların çoğu zaman sığınağın kapısından içeri girmeden başladığına işaret etti. Mevcut sistemde kadınlar konukevine doğrudan başvuramıyor. İl müdürlüğü, ŞÖNİM, ilgili kamu birimleri veya kolluk aracılığıyla yönlendirme yapılıyor. Bu nedenle ilk temas kurulan görevlinin yaklaşımı, doğru bilgi vermesi ve süreci geciktirmeden yürütmesi büyük önem taşıyor.

Karagöz, kadınların bu süreçte zaman zaman şiddetin nedenine ilişkin sorgulayıcı yorumlar, küçümseme, caydırıcı ifadeler ve sığınaklar hakkında yanlış bilgilendirmeyle karşılaştığını belirtti. Engelli kadınlar söz konusu olduğunda ise bu tutumların daha da ağırlaşabildiğine dikkat çekti. Ayrıca kadınların “engelli bir kadın olarak sığınakta kalmasının zor olacağı” yönünde bilgilendirilebildiğini, hatta bazı kadınlara sığınaklara engelli kadın kabul edilmediğinin söylendiğini aktardı.

Bu tablo, erişilebilirliğin yalnızca sığınak binasının girişindeki rampadan ibaret olmadığını gösteriyor. Bir kadın yardım hattına ulaşamıyor, telefonda iletişim kuramıyor, kendisine sunulan bilgiyi anlayabileceği biçimde alamıyor veya güvenli ulaşım desteği bulamıyorsa, bina fiziksel olarak erişilebilir olsa bile koruma zinciri daha ilk aşamada kopuyor. Bazı kadınlar ise engeller nedeniyle destek alamayacaklarını düşünerek hiçbir mekanizmaya başvurmuyor.

Mor Çatı’ya ulaşan kadınların anlatımları, sığınaklar arasında da ortak ve yerleşik bir standardın bulunmadığını gösteriyor. Koşulların yalnızca kentten kente değil, aynı kentteki farklı sığınaklar arasında dahi değişebildiği belirtiliyor. Bazı kadınlar saat ve telefon kullanımına ilişkin kısıtlamalar ile bina içindeki düzenlemeler nedeniyle sığınakları “hapishaneye” benzetirken, bazıları iyi koşullarla karşılaşabiliyor.

Oturmuş bir standart olmadığı için ana dilde destek, işaret dili desteği ya da erişilebilirlik konusunda kapsayıcı bir çalışma olmadığını ifade eden Karagöz, bununla birlikte olumlu örneklerin de bulunduğunu aktardı. Bazı durumlarda engelli kadınların ilk kabulde daha kısa sürede yerleştirildiğini ve çocuklarıyla tek başına kalabilecekleri bir odaya yerleştirildiklerini söyleyen Karagöz, “Ancak bu uygulama tüm sığınaklarda yok” dedi.

Avukat ve Engelli Kadın Derneği Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Özlem Kara’nın anlatımına göre; engellilik ve destek ilişkisi fail tarafından yeni kontrol araçlarına dönüştürülebiliyor. Tekerlekli sandalye, beyaz baston, işitme cihazı veya iletişim aracının saklanması; ilaç, beslenme, tuvalet, hijyen ve kişisel bakım desteğinin kasten engellenmesi; engelli aylığına veya banka hesabına el konulması bu şiddet biçimleri arasında. Telefon, internet, işaret dili tercümanı, Braille (görme engelliler için alfabe) veya kolay okunur bilgiye erişimin engellenmesi de kadını ihbar ve destek mekanizmalarından koparabiliyor. Failin aynı zamanda bakım veren kişi olması ise şiddet ortamından …

title: Nurses Across US Demand Hospitals Cut Ties With Palantir, Citing ICE and Gaza
content:
National Nurses United is expanding its campaign against Palantir in a global week of action starting on September 28.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

National Nurses United (NNU), the largest union of registered nurses in the U.S., is demanding that hospitals cut ties with Palantir, with nurses citing the firm’s role in developing technology used to surveil immigrants in the U.S. and target civilians in Gaza.

The union – which represents more than 225,000 nurses in all 50 U.S. states — has announced a global week of action against Palantir, set to begin on September 28.

Palantir’s “AI-powered tools for large-scale data collection and mass surveillance… threaten human rights globally,” the union said in a press release announcing the campaign.

The global week of action is aimed at pushing all public institutions — including hospitals and other health care providers — to end contracts and partnerships with Palantir, and to divest from the company, the union said.

The global week of action builds on a national day of action, also led by the union, which saw demonstrations in eight cities across the U.S. on August 27, including in Portland, Maine; Washington, D.C.; Chicago; Austin; and Los Angeles.

The global week of action is also coordinated with health care workers in the U.K., where National Health Service (NHS) workers and activists will protest Palantir’s use in health care on October 1. Other organizations, like Amnesty International and the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) Movement, are also part of the global week of action.

“Palantir has no place in patient care, no place in our communities, and no place in our society,” a NNU nurse said in a video from the August 27 day of action.

The nurses have outlined Palantir’s complicity in human rights violations both nationally and internationally, from detentions of immigrants by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to the genocide in Gaza.

“We think that a company that specializes in mass surveillance, kidnappings and killings, has no place in patient care,” one nurse explained in a video posted by the California Nurses Association.

During the August day of action, nurses placed 50 pairs of baby shoes in the street in each city – to represent the 500 babies and toddlers who have been detained in immigrant jails since President Donald Trump started his second term. The nurses also brought letters written by children in ICE detention.

“Palantir, we know, helps ICE identify people to kidnap off of our streets,” another nurse said during the day of action.

The company also has “their hands in the genocide and murders of civilians in Gaza,” another nurse present at the protests said. “They’ve [helped with the targeting of] hospitals, schools, mission workers taking food and aid….”

In a statement shared with Truthout and read at the August 27 day of action, Chicago-based nurse and NNU member Elizabeth Lalasz said that “nurses, health care workers, our patients, immigrants, and allies from every walk of life stand united here in Chicago and all across the country to demand an immediate end to the violence inflicted by Palantir technologies and the Trump administration.”

“As we speak, Palantir’s AI is enabling atrocities and human rights abuses: ICE killings, mass deportation, and concentration camps with no access to health care – even the imprisonment of more than 500 babies and 6,200 children – and Palantir is providing the technology for Israel’s U.S.-funded genocide in Gaza, the cruel and illegal war in Iran, and mass surveillance at home and abroad,” she went on.

Lalasz also noted that Palantir has partnered with the world’s largest health care corporations “to suck more and more profit from our broken health care system, causing untold suffering in our hospitals.”

“This country could fund health care for 12 million children with the money spent on ICE detention alone,” she said.

João Paulo Connolly, an activist in the Bay Area who has organized protests against Palantir, explained in a webinar that “Palantir’s profit model is data extraction and surveillance,” and then “giving employers new, powerful ways to monitor and spy on their workers at all times and track their behavior,” while also selling the health care industry and the federal government “unprecedented levels of access” to this data.

title: İstanbul Barosu’ndan engelli çocukların eğitim hakkı için veli rehberi
content:
İstanbul Barosu Engelli Hakları Merkezi, yeni eğitim-öğretim döneminde engelli çocukların ve ailelerinin okullarda karşılaşabileceği hak ihlallerine karşı 

“Eğitimde Sağlamcılığa Hayır! Engelli Çocukların Eğitim Hakkı İçin Veli Rehberi”

 başlıklı bir çalışma yayımladı.


Eylül 2026 tarihli 68 sayfalık rehber; okul kaydı, sağlık raporu talepleri, “gölge öğretmen” dayatması, başka okula ya da sınıfa yönlendirme, Bireyselleştirilmiş Eğitim Programı (BEP), destek eğitim odası, erişilebilirlik, yardımcı cihazlar, akran zorbalığı, ayrımcılık ve mahremiyet gibi başlıkları ele alıyor. Ailelerin sorun yaşaması halinde başvurabileceği idari ve hukuki yollar ile örnek dilekçeler de rehberde yer alıyor.


“Çözüm çocuğu eğitim ortamından uzaklaştırmak değil”


Rehberde öne çıkan sorunlardan biri, engelli çocukların okul kaydı sırasında karşılaştığı doğrudan ya da dolaylı ret uygulamaları.


Baro, bir çocuğun engelli olmasının tek başına okul kaydının reddedilmesi için gerekçe oluşturamayacağını hatırlatıyor. Okulların “Bu okul çocuğunuza uygun değil”, “Sınıf çok kalabalık”, “Öğretmenimiz bu konuda eğitimli değil” ya da “Başka okul daha iyi olur” gibi gerekçelerle çocuğu eğitim ortamından uzaklaştırmasının eğitim hakkını ortadan kaldırmadığını belirtiyor.


Engelli Odaklı Habercilik Atölyesi sona erdi: "Kafamızdaki sağlamcıyı öldürmeliyiz"


25 Haziran 2026


“Gölge öğretmen tutamazsanız okula alamayız” denilemez


Rehberin dikkat çektiği uygulamalardan biri de bazı ailelerden çocuklarının okula devam edebilmesi için kendi imkanlarıyla “gölge öğretmen” ya da destek personeli sağlamalarının istenmesi.


İstanbul Barosu, çocuğun sınıf içinde desteğe ihtiyaç duyması halinde öncelikle BEP, destek eğitim ve sınıf içi uyarlamalar gibi kamusal yükümlülüklerin değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini vurguluyor.


Ailenin ekonomik gücüyle özel bir personel çalıştırabilmesi ile çocuğun anayasal eğitim hakkının birbirine karıştırılamayacağını belirten rehber, okul kabulünün ailenin ücretini ödeyeceği bir personel bulmasına bağlanmasının eğitim hakkı ve ayrımcılık yasağı bakımından ciddi hukuki sorun doğurabileceğine dikkat çekiyor.


Okul yönetimi tek başına “Bu çocuk bu sınıfta yapamaz” diyemez


Baro ayrıca, engelli bir öğrencinin başka okula veya özel eğitim sınıfına gönderilmesine yalnızca öğretmenin ya da okul yönetiminin karar veremeyeceğini hatırlatıyor.


Çocuğun eğitim ortamının değiştirilmesinin eğitsel değerlendirme ve tanılama sürecine bağlı olduğu; değerlendirmelerin Rehberlik ve Araştırma Merkezi (RAM) bünyesindeki kurul tarafından yapılması gerektiği belirtiliyor.


Yerleştirme kararında velinin yazılı talebinin de dikkate alınması gerekiyor. Bu nedenle öğretmenin ya da okul müdürünün “Bu çocuk burada yapamaz” şeklindeki değerlendirmesinin tek başına yerleştirme kararı sayılamayacağı ifade ediliyor.


Engelsiz Erişim Derneği: Otizm “farkındalık” değil, kabul ve eşit erişim meselesi


2 Nisan 2026


Destek eğitim odası çocuğu sınıftan uzaklaştırmanın aracı değil


Rehber, tam zamanlı kaynaştırma/bütünleştirme yoluyla eğitim gören öğrenciler bakımından destek eğitim odalarına da geniş yer ayırıyor.


Destek eğitim odasında verilecek eğitimin öğrencinin haftalık toplam ders saatinin yüzde 40'ını aşamayacağı; temel olarak bire bir yürütüleceği, BEP geliştirme biriminin kararıyla en fazla üç öğrenciden oluşan gruplarla da eğitim yapılabileceği aktarılıyor.


Ancak rehber özellikle bir noktaya dikkat çekiyor: Destek eğitim odası, öğrenciyi akranlarından soyutlamak veya genel eğitim sınıfından uzaklaştırmak için kullanılamaz.


Okul yönetiminin “odamız yok” ya da “öğretmenimiz yok” demesinin de tek başına öğrencinin ihtiyaç duyduğu desteğin karşılanmamasını hukuken haklı hale getirmeyeceği belirtiliyor.


Zorbalığa karşı önlem almak okulun yükümlülüğü


Çalışmanın “Güvenli okul, ayrımcılık ve mahremiyet” bölümünde engelli çocukların karşılaşabileceği akran zorbalığı da ele alınıyor.


Alay etme, hakaret, tehdit, dışlama, fiziksel şiddet, çocuğun eşyalarına veya kullandığı yardımcı cihazlara müdahale ve dijital ortamda rahatsız etme zorbalığın farklı biçimleri arasında sayılıyor.


Rehber, Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı'nın ilgili genelgelerine işaret ederek okul yönetimlerinin zorbalığa yol açabilecek riskleri belirlemek, önleyici tedbir almak ve rehberlik hizmetlerini işletmekle yükümlü olduğunu hatırlatıyor.


Ailelere her bir olayı tarih, yer ve gerçekleşme biçimiyle ayrı ayrı kaydetmeleri öneriliyor.


Çürük


7 Eylül 2026
