title: Over 100,000 students face violation of the  right to education in Rojava
content:
“I am Kurdish, my language is Kurdish”, “Our language is our identity, culture and dignity”, “It is our right to learn in our own language”, “We want our language”, “There is no life without language” and “The Kurdish language will live forever."


These slogans have echoed through the streets of Hasakah (Hesekê), Kobanê, Dirbêsiyê, Tirbespiyê, Qamishlo, Amûdê, Çilaxayê, Dêrik, Til Temir and many other cities since 27 August. Students and teachers have been marching with banners for days, stressing that education in Kurdish is a fundamental right. Among the most prominent participants in the protests are the children of fighters martyred in the Rojava Revolution. They too stress that Kurdish is not simply another school subject or a language spoken at home, but the language of their identity, culture and future.


The scale of what has been achieved is considerable: over the past 14 years, more than one million students in Rojava have received education in their mother tongue as part of what has been described as a “language revolution”. That achievement, however, is now under threat from the interim government in Damascus.


The Ministry of Education of the Syrian Interim Government issued a decree ending Kurdish-language education in schools run by the Autonomous Administration and replacing it with three hours of elective Kurdish lessons. Students, teachers and parents began protesting as soon as the decision was announced, while students have been boycotting schools. They say restricting Kurdish-language education would also erase the Kurdish people’s collective memory and expose a new generation to assimilation.


A grave injustice against children


How did Kurdish-language education in Rojava begin, how did it develop, and what happens next? Semira Hec Elî, Co-Chair of the Autonomous Administration’s Education Committee, spoke to ANF about the Kurdish-language education experience in Rojava and the implications of the decision taken by Damascus. Hec Elî said said, “First and foremost, Damascus’s decision is a grave and irreparable injustice against children,” and calling on Damascus to immediately withdraw or revise the decision.


The journey of Kurdish-language education


In 2012, the year the Rojava Revolution began, Kurds organised around the Kurdish Language Institute (Saziya Zimanê Kurdî, SZK) and, despite repression by the Baath regime, opened Kurdish-language academies from Kobanê to Afrin (Efrîn) and Dêrik. A widely attended Kurdish Language Conference was also held in Amûdê that year, where participants decided to train teachers to provide education in Kurdish and open Kurdish-language schools.


SZK opened its first language and literature academy in Afrin on 11 August 2013 under the name Martyr Ferzat Kemenger Academy, where it began training dozens of teachers. In October, the first Institute of Kurdish Language and Literature, named after Martyr Viyan Amara, was opened under the leadership of SZK and the Rojava Teachers’ Union. The Celadet Bedîrxan Academy for Kurdish language, history and literature was established in Qamishlo, while the Martyr Viyan Amara Institute began operating in Kobanê.


The declaration of Cizîr Canton on 21 January 2014, Kobanê Canton on 27 January and Afrin Canton on 29 January was followed by a decision to make Kurdish a language of education and teach it in all schools across the region. By 2016, Kurdish had become the language of instruction across all school grades. Arabic and Syriac were also recognised as official languages of education.


It was a process filled with struggle


Semira Hec Elî, who has been involved in language initiatives since the beginning of the revolution, described the 14-year effort as both deeply emotional and marked by struggle. She said: “It was a very important and emotional process, filled with struggle. We faced many difficulties, but there was also immense joy. Just imagine: for the first time, Kurdish children were speaking, reading and writing in their mother tongue.”


Hec Elî criticised the decision by Syrian Interim President Ahmed al-Sharaa to reduce Kurdish to an elective subject despite the years of work invested in Kurdish-language education. Hec Elî also said: “We held numerous meetings with the Ministry of Education. At every meeting, we made clear that Kurdish must not be an elective but one of the official and primary languages of education. We were therefore shocked by the decision that was taken.”


Protests grow …

title: Molina: The law is a first step, Öcalan’s status must be resolved
content:
The search for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question continues as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began following Abdullah Öcalan’s historic call on 27 February 2025. As part of the process, a framework law recently submitted to and adopted by the Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM) was subsequently signed by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and entered into force after being published in the Official Gazette.


The law is regarded as an important step towards advancing the process, but has also drawn criticism for failing to provide a fundamental and comprehensive solution to the Kurdish question.


Developments in the process are being closely followed internationally as well as in Turkey, Kurdistan and the wider region. Fabian Molina, a member of the Swiss Federal Parliament who has closely followed the Kurdish question for many years, spoke to ANF about the latest developments in the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


 


The law is only a beginning


Molina said he was closely following developments in Turkey and described the law adopted by the TBMM as an important first step on the path towards lasting peace.


Molina added: “It is important that a consensus has been reached on this legislation. This law marks the beginning of a process towards genuine, just and lasting peace. In that sense, I believe the law adopted by the TBMM is important. But this is certainly not the end of the road. There are still many unresolved questions that will need to be addressed in the future.”


The question has caused immense suffering for decades


Molina stressed that the Kurdish question has deep historical roots and therefore requires a comprehensive solution.


He said the conflict between the Turkish state and the Kurdish people had continued for decades, adding: “It is a tragedy that has claimed many lives and caused immense suffering. That is why I believe it is important to now try to address these issues through a peace process. It is also important that they are discussed in parliament, within the framework of democratic debate.”


Questions over Kurdish identity and language remain unresolved


Molina said the existing legislation alone was not sufficient to resolve the Kurdish question, stressing that Kurdish identity and language rights, as well as the democratisation of Turkey, must be among the central issues addressed by the process.


He said: “Despite the law, many issues remain unresolved. Among the most important are the identity of the Kurdish people, the Kurdish language and the democratisation of the Turkish state.”


Molina also described the measures targeting the opposition as unacceptable at a time when a solution to the Kurdish question is being discussed.


Molina also said: “The treatment of the opposition is concerning. Further steps are needed to safeguard the rule of law, democracy and human rights. The international community also has a responsibility to support these values and ensure that the process does not stop at this stage.”


Molina stressed that alongside the legislation, the government must demonstrate its political commitment to the process through concrete action.


He said: “It is important that the government now demonstrates its political will and proves its commitment to honouring the agreements that have been reached.”


Mutual trust must be built


Molina said building mutual trust between the parties would be crucial in the next stage of the process and that legislation alone would not be enough. Molina continued: “Legal measures alone are not sufficient. What matters now is for both sides to move towards fostering and building mutual trust. This process is also a political matter. Both sides need to have confidence that the legislation and what has been agreed will be implemented. This is important so that the other outstanding issues can then be addressed.”


Kurdish language and cultural identity rights must be addressed


Molina stressed that safeguarding the fundamental rights of the Kurdish people is essential for the process to move forward. Molina said: “One of the issues that definitely remains unresolved is the rights of the Kurdish people within the Turkish state. This includes the right to language and the right to cultural identity. The situation of political prisoners in prisons is another issue that needs to be addressed. Questions also remain over the political prisoners who are still in prison and how to deal with …

title: DEM Party calls on Parliament to recognize the right to education in one’s mother tongue
content:
The DEM Party’s Commission on Language, Culture and the Arts said in a written statement: “As the new academic year begins, Turkey's education system is facing multidimensional crises, ranging from child poverty and insufficient funding to the commercialization of education, the transformation of children into workers, and gender-discriminatory policies. One of the most meaningful steps that can be taken to address these crises is to provide millions of children with the opportunity to receive education in their own mother tongue.”


The statement continued: “Today, millions of children, particularly Kurdish children, begin their educational lives without having access to this opportunity. Yet education in one’s mother tongue is a guarantee that a child can develop as a free individual with their own identity, language and culture.


Turkey has been going through an important process for the past two years. The Peace and Democratic Society Process aims for a democratic order in which every individual and community lives together on the basis of equal and dignified citizenship and their inherent rights. A democratic, pluralistic and egalitarian social climate is possible only when the rights of different languages and cultures are guaranteed. Therefore, providing legal and constitutional guarantees for the right to education in one’s mother tongue is one of the most important steps toward peace and democratic transformation.”


The statement added: “Guaranteeing the right to education in the child’s mother tongue is also essential for quality education and social peace. The existing right to two hours of ‘elective language classes’ per week is an important achievement resulting from years of struggle and efforts to preserve and promote the language. The crucial next step, building on this achievement, is to make the mother tongue a language of instruction and provide guarantees for this right.


Recent pressure and attacks against Kurdish language institutions and, even if only in isolated cases, against people who speak Kurdish are creating space for provocations. Preventing this and strengthening democratic coexistence and fraternity is possible only by establishing genuine equality among languages.”


The statement underlined that “the right to one’s mother tongue does not divide us; on the contrary, it unites us. This right is the foundation of social peace and is an inalienable right.


We call on administrative and civil institutions, particularly the Grand National Assembly of Turkey, as well as society as a whole, to assume a historic responsibility for recognizing the right to education in one’s mother tongue.”

title: Öcalan: My aim is to achieve peace and political participation
content:
The Imrali Delegation of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) met with Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan on the Turkish prison island of Imrali on Sunday. The delegation consisted of MPs Pervin Buldan and Mithat Sancar, as well as lawyer Faik Özgür Erol from the Asrin Law Office in Istanbul.


In a statement about the meeting, the DEM Party Imrali Delegation said the following:


“As the DEM Party Imrali Delegation, we held a meeting with Mr. Abdullah Öcalan on Imrali Island on September 13, 2026.


During the meeting, we discussed the current process in Turkey, the development of a democratic solution and lasting peace, the concrete steps that need to be taken to advance the process, and regional developments.


Mr. Abdullah Öcalan’s assessments, intended to be shared with the public, can be summarized as follows:


‘The Peace and Democratic Society Process has reached a stage that requires historical responsibilities to be fulfilled without delay. In the period following the adoption of the law, it is of great importance that mutual practical steps be taken within the framework of this responsibility and that the relevant committees begin actively carrying out their work.


My aim is to achieve peace and political participation. Peace corresponds to laying down arms, while political participation corresponds to democratic politics and a democratic society.


Turkey has a historic opportunity before it. In order for this opportunity to lead to lasting peace and a democratic solution, I expect everyone and every section of society to act with this awareness, and I believe they will do so. Ensuring that the will for peace does not remain without concrete backing, but is instead guaranteed through tangible legal and political arrangements, is a task that can no longer be postponed.


The Peace and Democratic Society Process also aims to ensure that all peoples and faiths in the Middle East can live together in peace, freedom and equality. Developments in the region clearly demonstrate that the process is unfolding amid delicate balances, and is directly affected by these developments. Therefore, in order to thwart potential provocations, it is essential that the region’s problems be addressed through dialogue and negotiation. The events taking place in Rojava should also be evaluated within this framework.’


As the DEM Party Imrali Delegation, we would once again like to emphasize that Mr. Öcalan’s fundamental approach is to make peace permanent, strengthen democratic politics and advance the democratization of Turkey.


The path to peace is clear. Now is the time to demonstrate the political will and put into practice the steps needed to move forward along this path.


Respectfully,


DEM Party Imrali Delegation


September 14, 2026”

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Nuevos intentos de desalojo de comunidades indígenas y campesinas
content:
Boletín de pueblos originarios actualizado al 14.9.2026


Tres casos de intento de desalojo de comunidades indígenas y campesinas en Peñas Negras (Catamarca), San Pedro (Misiones) y Lof Melo (Villa La Angostura)


Mario Hernandez


Empresarios, personal policial y autoridades provinciales con complicidad judicial aceleraron en los últimos días el hostigamiento a comunidades indígenas y campesinas con el objetivo de despojarlas de sus tierras. El conflicto que involucra a Emanuel Ginóbili en Villa La Angostura. Convocan a un acto en defensa del agua en Mendoza el 9 de diciembre.


Se agrava el conflicto entre una comunidad indígena y las mineras en Catamarca


Por Juan Manuel Erazo


Peñas Negras denuncia una escalada de violencia ante el avance de actividades extractivas en su territorio. Responsabilizan al gobernador Rubén Jalil por el hostigamiento policial.


La Comunidad Indígena de Peñas Negras, perteneciente al pueblo diaguita, resiste al proyecto minero Aguas Calientes I, II y III en Belén, Catamarca. La iniciativa empresarial está a cargo de Minera Millaray S.A., y las operadoras Elevado Gold S.A. (de capitales australianos) y Amalaya S.A., quienes intentan llevar a cabo los estudios iniciales en una zona donde la comunidad desarrolla tareas de pastoreo, actividades comunitarias y que declaran como un territorio ancestral y sagrado.


El miércoles 2 de septiembre, los comuneros fueron golpeados y agredidos con gas pimienta por personal policial. De acuerdo con lo relatado por la comunidad, personas no identificadas y sin orden judicial visible intentaron ingresar al territorio en motocicletas sin identificación. La comunidad sostiene un campamento en la zona. Sus voceros afirman que el operativo policial que derivó en la represión respondió a una orden directa del gobernador de Catamarca, Raúl Jalil, para habilitar por la fuerza el ingreso de la minera al territorio y avanzar con la toma de muestras, pese a la falta de orden judicial y a la ausencia del proceso de Consulta Previa, Libre e Informada.


Según su relato, el conflicto se agravó en los últimos días cuando la empresa, escoltada por personal policial, intentó subir al cerro para realizar estudios mineros, lo que derivó en sucesivos episodios de violencia contra los comuneros que resisten el proyecto. La comunidad remarca que, pese a haber puesto los hechos en conocimiento de los organismos de Justicia, hasta el momento no se dispuso ninguna medida de protección.


El 6 de setiembre, los comuneros realizaron una denuncia penal ante la Fiscalía de Belén tras los hechos de violencia policial ocurridos en su territorio. La presentación fue realizada por la abogada de la comunidad, Andrea Morales Leanza, quien solicitó la inmediata intervención fiscal, custodia policial para su traslado y el desplazamiento de personal judicial al territorio para tomar denuncias in situ. La denuncia pide que la Fiscalía verifique la identidad y legitimidad de quienes intervienen en el lugar y que se constaten médicamente las lesiones sufridas por los comuneros.


“Estamos en un Estado sin derecho, sin garantía de nada”, declaró Morales Leanza y denunció la presencia constante de policías y personas vinculadas a la actividad minera en los alrededores del territorio. Según explicó, el acceso a la comunidad desde Catamarca se encuentra dificultado y existen grupos que impiden el ingreso de personas que intentan acercarse para brindar asistencia. Por ese motivo, Morales Leanza debió coordinar su ingreso desde la localidad salteña de Jasimaná, utilizando caminos solo conocidos por las propias comunidades.


El arqueólogo, docente e investigador de UNCA, Gustavo Pisani, comentó: “La respuesta del gobierno provincial fue seguir adelante con el proyecto minero, a pesar de que no contaba con el consentimiento de las comunidades indígenas, lo que significó no solo no revocar, sino incluso renovar, los permisos de exploración a las empresas, y accionar junto con ellas para tratar de favorecer la instalación de este emprendimiento en el lugar”.


Un poco de historia


El 7 de febrero del 2024, el Ministerio de Minería de Catamarca aprobó la Declaración de Impacto Ambiental para la etapa de exploración del proyecto minero. La comunidad impugnó esta resolución ante la ministra Olga Teresita Regalado, reclamando su nulidad absoluta por no haberse realizado el proceso de Consulta Previa, Libre e Informada que exige el Convenio 169 de la Organización Internacional del Trabajo y el …

title: Trove of Evidence Sheds New Light on How Saudi Intelligence Asset Helped 9/11 Hijackers Before Attack
content:
Did Saudi Arabia play a role in the planning and execution of the September 11 attacks of 2001? That question was raised immediately after the attack, when 15 of the 19 hijackers were revealed to be Saudi citizens, and it has only grown louder in the 25 years since as more evidence emerged of the attackers’ connections to Saudi figures inside the United States.


We speak with

ProPublica

 journalist Tim Golden, who reports that the

FBI

 failed to fully investigate Omar al-Bayoumi, a Saudi intelligence asset who helped two of the hijackers as they arrived in California in early 2000. Key evidence, including a handwritten note by al-Bayoumi calculating an airplane’s trajectory to a point on the horizon, was not fully disclosed to investigators.


“Al-Bayoumi was incredibly important, but this evidence … sort of went missing for more than 20 years,” says Golden. “If the Saudi government is indirectly responsible, or even if this was some rogue cell of Saudis within the religious bureaucracy, we would hope that that should come out.”

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Isaruit Inuit Arts takes over Ottawa Inuktitut radio program
content:
For Jessie Kangok, hosting an Inuit radio program brings back memories of sitting with her father in Igloolik, listening to the community radio together.


She has hosted

Uqallagvik

 on CKCU 93.1 FM at Carleton University in Ottawa since it first aired in 2019.


“The excitement and the feeling of being in the studio, the feeling of being home reminded me of my dad,” she said in an interview Wednesday.

“That same love for the radio can be heard and passed down here, even in the city. It doesn’t have to be only in Nunavut or isolated communities, and that’s what I’m proud of.”


Now, the program Kangok helped establish is entering a new chapter.


Isaruit Inuit Arts, which, according to its website, celebrates Inuit art through skill development, took over management last month of

Uqallagvik

 from Tungasuvvingat Inuit, a non-profit that offers social support and employment opportunities.


“Isaruit taking on the partnership is a great asset because they really believe in sharing

Uqalla

g

vik

’s

 vision to share stories that are elder-led,” said Kangok, who is also a communications adviser on the organization’s board of directors.

“I’m really happy that we’re going to really strengthen that more.” 


The program began in 2019 after

Nipivut

, an Inuit community radio program in Montreal, approached Tungasuvvingat Inuit about creating a similar program in Ottawa. 


The organization agreed and hired Kangok and two other hosts.


Tungasuvvingat Inuit supported

 Uqallagvik

 from its launch until this year. But it could no longer fund the program, said Beverly Illauq, Isaruit Inuit Arts founding co-ordinator, in an email to Nunatsiaq News. 


When funding dried up, Kangok and co-host Franco Buscemi

stepped in on a volunteer basis to keep the show running.


Tungasuvvingat Inuit then approached Isaruit about taking over the partnership last month, Illauq said.


Nunatsiaq News reached out to Tungasuvvingat Inuit but did not receive a response.


The show will now be funded through Isaruit’s Back to Roots program, which is supported by the Canada Council for the Arts, Indigenous Services Canada, the City of Ottawa and Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. 


Elders, artists and hosts will all be paid, Illauq said.


Isaruit is also recruiting new hosts, with training planned through CKCU-FM in October. Kangok said Isaruit program co-ordinator Ben Ilauq and elder consultant Asenath Kannutaq will be joining the hosting team. 


“We’re looking for someone who just wants to share their Inuit culture, their language, and promote it, and are not shy to speak,” said Kangok.


Uqallagvik airs every Wednesday from 11 a.m. to noon and broadcasts in Inuktitut and English.

title: "One Betrayal After Another": 9/11 Widow Blasts U.S. Cover-Up of Saudi Role in Attacks
content:
A quarter-century after the September 11 attacks that killed nearly 3,000 people in the United States, a group of victims’ families is continuing a lawsuit against Saudi Arabia to hold the kingdom accountable for any role it played in the planning and execution of the plot. While the Saudi government has always denied advance knowledge of the 9/11 attacks, 15 of the 19 plane hijackers were Saudi citizens, including some with connections to Saudi officials and intelligence assets in the United States. Terry Strada, the national chair of 9/11 Families United, raised the issue during an official commemoration on Friday in New York while paying tribute to her husband Tom, who was killed in the World Trade Center. With Vice President JD Vance and all four living ex-presidents in the audience, Strada asked: “How can it be 25 years and still we have no justice for the role that Saudi Arabia played in your murder?”


Strada tells

Democracy Now!

 that evidence has only grown that Saudi agents “were directly involved with providing the support network” to carry out the 9/11 attacks, and that she hopes President Donald Trump will tell the Saudi government “that they can no longer hide and that they need to confront the evidence and work things out with the families.”

title: "NAZA" Film on Gaza Genocide Wins Venice Special Jury Prize; Israel Threatens Directors' Citizenship
content:
The film

NAZA

, which documents the Israeli military’s use of secret AI-powered systems to deliberately and systematically target and massacre civilians in Gaza, won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival Saturday. The film was directed by Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham and filmmaker Rachel Szor, both of whom won an Oscar for the documentary

No Other Land

 in 2025 along with Palestinian co-directors Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal.

NAZA

 was shot in secret on rooftops in Tel Aviv over three years and builds on testimony from Israeli military and intelligence sources who spoke on the condition their identities be concealed. The film’s title refers to an acronym used by the Israeli military as a shorthand for civilian killings in Gaza.


The film’s reception in Venice, where it received a record-breaking 25-minute standing ovation, was met with angry backlash from Israel’s government as Culture Minister Miki Zohar threatened to revoke Abraham and Szor’s Israeli citizenship.

title: IG Metall vor der Metall-Tarifrunde: Christiane Benners Programm gegen den Industrieabbau – eine deutsche Kopie des Trump’schen Protektionismus.
content:
„…

Im Handelsblatt-Interview vom 28.07.2026 skizzierte IG-Metall-Chefin Christiane Benner ihre Rezepte, um Arbeitsplätze zu erhalten. Zölle, Local Content, ein Bekenntnis zu Wachstumsbranchen wie Rüstung und Rechenzentren – und eine Kampfansage in der Rentenfrage. Ein genauerer Blick auf die Fakten hinter diesem Programm zeigt: Es ist weit weniger kämpferisch, als es klingt, und an entscheidenden Stellen schlicht die deutsche Kopie einer gescheiterten US-amerikanischen Blaupause. (…) Wer als Aufsichtsrätin eine Arbeitszeitverlängerung mitträgt und als Gewerkschaftsvorsitzende gleichzeitig für eine Arbeitszeitverkürzung eintreten müsste, gerät zwangsläufig in einen Rollenkonflikt – vierzig Jahre nach dem größten Erfolg, den die eigene Organisation mit genau dieser Forderung je erzielt hat. (…) Standortnationalismus verspricht kurzfristigen Schutz für die eigene Belegschaft, erkauft ihn aber durch Konkurrenz zwischen Beschäftigten verschiedener Standorte und Länder – ein Spiel, das die Arbeiterklasse, gleich wer gerade nachgibt, auf Dauer nur verlieren kann

…“

Artikel von Jörg Wuttke vom 14.9.2026

 – wir danken!


IG Metall vor der Metall-Tarifrunde: Christiane Benners Programm gegen den Industrieabbau


–  eine deutsche Kopie des Trump’schen Protektionismus.


Die Metall- und Elektroindustrie steht vor einer der schwierigsten Tarifrunden ihrer Geschichte. Seit 2019 sind 320.000 Jobs verloren gegangen, Hunderttausende weitere stehen laut Arbeitgebern auf dem Spiel. Nicht wenige sprechen von einer Kernschmelze des industriellen Kerns. Im Handelsblatt-Interview vom 28.07.2026 skizzierte IG-Metall-Chefin Christiane Benner ihre Rezepte, um Arbeitsplätze zu erhalten.  Zölle, Local Content, ein Bekenntnis zu Wachstumsbranchen wie Rüstung und Rechenzentren – und eine Kampfansage in der Rentenfrage. Ein genauerer Blick auf die Fakten hinter diesem Programm zeigt: Es ist weit weniger kämpferisch, als es klingt, und an entscheidenden Stellen schlicht die deutsche Kopie einer gescheiterten US-amerikanischen Blaupause.


Trump’scher Protektionismus im EU-Gewand


Christiane Benner fordert europäischen Zölle auf chinesische Hybridfahrzeuge, um die unter Druck stehenden deutschen Hersteller zu schützen. Ihr Argument ist nicht aus der Luft gegriffen: Der Anteil chinesischer Marken an den in Europa verkauften Plug-in-Hybriden erreichte im Juni 2026 einen Rekordwert von 34 Prozent, begünstigt durch staatliche Subventionen, die drei- bis achtmal höher liegen als in der OECD-Region, sowie eine geschätzte Unterbewertung des Yuan von mindestens 40 Prozent. Das ist kein fairer Marktwettbewerb.


Nur: Genau diese Politik – Zölle und Protektionismus als Antwort – hat Trump in den USA bereits vorexerziert, mit ernüchterndem Ergebnis. Seit Trumps “Liberation Day”-Zöllen im April 2025 wurden dort 89.000 Stellen im verarbeitenden Gewerbe abgebaut, das dritte Jahr in Folge sinkt die Beschäftigung im Sektor. Von der versprochenen Rückverlagerung der Produktion keine Spur: Das US-Handelsbilanzdefizit erreichte 2025 einen Rekordwert. Und wer zahlt die Zeche? Die Zollpolitik kostet US-Haushalte im Schnitt rund 2.400 Dollar im Jahr – eine Summe, die nach Berechnungen der Bank of America bereits rund ein Viertel aller US-Haushalte hart trifft, die von Gehaltsscheck zu Gehaltsscheck leben; nach Fed-Zahlen könnte gut ein Drittel der US-Amerikaner nicht einmal eine unerwartete Ausgabe von 400 Dollar stemmen. Wer also von Zöllen eine Rettung der deutschen Autoindustrie erwartet, sollte diese Bilanz kennen.


Hinzu kommt eine Doppelmoral, die Christiane Benner nicht anspricht: Wenn die EU China Marktverzerrung durch Subventionen vorwirft, sollte sie den Blick auch auf sich selbst richten. Die direkten EU-Agrarexportsubventionen sind zwar seit 2003 offiziell abgeschafft, doch die strukturellen Effekte europäischer Überproduktion wirken bis heute: Importiertes Milchpulver wird in Westafrika zu bis zu 40 Prozent niedrigeren Preisen an Verarbeiter weitergegeben als lokal produzierte Milch – mit der Folge zerstörter bäuerlicher Existenzen und Landflucht.


Local Content: Auch eine Kopie des Trump’schen Irrweg


Auch bei Benners zweiter Forderung – verbindliche Local-Content-Quoten für Zulieferer, verankert im “Industrial Accelerator Act” – handelt es sich um den aus den USA importierten nationalen Protektionismus. Ausländischen Herstellern, die in Europa Werke bauen, die Freiheit zu nehmen, dort einzukaufen, wo es am günstigsten ist, ist eine klassische …

author: Daniel Camargos
title: O site da Amazônia que deixou de cobrir eleições por medo de morrer
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


A redação do Tapajós de Fato passou parte deste ano definindo a pauta e buscando financiamento para cobrir as eleições de 2026. Mas

ameaças e episódios de violência levaram o site de Santarém, no oeste do Pará, a abandonar o projeto antes da primeira reportagem. 


Criado em 2020 durante a onda de negacionismo da pandemia, o Tapajós de Fato é um veículo independente, membro da

Rede Cidadã InfoAmazonia

, que se tornou referência no jornalismo feito na Amazônia, denunciando violações sociais e ambientais. Mas,

na campanha deste ano, a redação não vai abordar os problemas, propor soluções para a região, nem investigar vínculos de candidatos com o garimpo, o agronegócio e as grandes obras. 


‘Quando é melhor não falar, por uma questão de sobrevivência, na verdade, quem perde é a sociedade”, afirma o coordenador de projetos João Paulo Serra, de 27 anos.


A decisão de não cobrir as eleições deste ano foi tomada após uma série de ameaças que mostraram não haver segurança para trabalhar.

 Na eleição presidencial de 2022, a cabeça decapitada de um gato apareceu no terreno baldio onde a equipe estacionava a caminhonete de reportagem. Ao lado, um bilhete trazia o nome de Marcos Wesley Pedroso, o fundador do Tapajós de Fato, e avisava que ele seria a próxima vítima. Dias antes, os quatro pneus do veículo haviam sido rasgados.


Em outro episódio, uma comunicadora foi atacada com uma faca e conseguiu se desviar de vários golpes. O agressor não foi identificado, e o Tapajós de Fato não conseguiu determinar se o objetivo era matá-la, intimidar a redação ou se o episódio não tinha relação com o trabalho jornalístico. 


A violência não impediu a cobertura daquela eleição.

 Em 2022, o Tapajós de Fato entrevistou candidatos progressistas com atuação no oeste do Pará e debateu assuntos da região, como garimpo, desmatamento, mudanças climáticas e direitos dos povos tradicionais. 


Acompanhou também um encontro no qual movimentos sociais cobraram compromissos com a agroecologia e a agricultura familiar. Depois da votação, analisou quem o Pará havia eleito e a relação dos novos representantes com as pautas amazônicas. A equipe ainda foi às ruas para cobrir os atos bolsonaristas diante de uma unidade do Exército. 


Em 2024, porém, a insegurança levou o site a suspender a cobertura das eleições municipais. “A gente decidiu recuar de novo em 2026”, lamenta Marcos.


“Eu tenho medo de pessoas aleatórias na rua, no supermercado”, conta. “Chegou um tempo que eu dormia e, se escutasse um cachorro latindo de madrugada, acordava com taquicardia”, detalha. Marcos deixou Santarém devido às ameaças e após um diagnóstico de depressão.


Os casos foram denunciados à Polícia Civil e ao Ministério Público, mas, até o momento, não há nenhuma informação conclusiva e, por isso, não há autores identificados nem provas de que os atos estejam relacionados entre si. Ainda assim,

jornalistas da equipe decidiram deixar suas casas e passaram a morar em hotéis durante os períodos mais tensos.

 Marcos já trocou de endereço seis vezes nos últimos três anos. E João Paulo precisou ficar um ano sem visitar a mãe.


Marcos Wesley Pedroso fundou o site para trazer novos olhares à cobertura jornalística do Oeste do Pará


Tapajós de Fato: origem popular e formação de jovens comunicadores


A ideia de fundar o Tapajós de Fato surgiu num encontro de comunicadores rurais, em 2019, quando Marcos atuava na comunicação do sindicato rural de Santarém. Em julho de 2020, em plena pandemia de Covid-19, ele e mais uma jornalista criaram as redes sociais do veículo. Depois lançaram o site.


Foi em casa que Marcos aprendeu a cobrar direitos e a se organizar para defendê-los, experiência que mais tarde orientaria o jornalismo do Tapajós de Fato. Os avós dirigiram o sindicato dos trabalhadores rurais de Belterra, cidade a 50 quilômetros de Santarém.


Marcos viveu com os avós em Aramanaí, comunidade de Belterra às margens do rio Tapajós. Desde os anos 2000, a pavimentação da

BR-163

 e a abertura do terminal da Cargill, em Santarém, transformaram o oeste do Pará em corredor de exportação de grãos e fronteira agrícola na Amazônia. As lavouras avançaram pelo Planalto Santareno até as vizinhanças da comunidade. Ali ele ouviu que o mamão deixara de vingar e que a produção de mel e de andiroba diminuíram com os agrotóxicos.

author: Mag
title: Kahlschlag bei VW ab 2024? Autobauer plant Kürzungen in Milliardenhöhe, um »Effizienz« zu steigern
content:
Dossier


„…

Seit Anfang Oktober verhandelt das VW-Management mit dem Betriebsrat hinter verschlossenen Türen über ein »Effizienzprogramm«, das die Kosten in den kommenden drei Jahren um zehn Milliarden Euro senken soll. Nun zeichnet sich ab, welche Formen der Kahlschlag namens »Accelerate forward« (Forwärtsbeschleunigung) annehmen könnte. Wie am Montag das Handelsblatt berichtete, plant Schäfer, allein in der Verwaltung der VW AG zwischen 4.000 und 6.000 Stellen zu streichen. Die betroffenen Angestellten sollen bevorzugt über Alterszeitregelungen entsorgt werden, den Rest könnten Abfindungsprogramme erledigen. Ziel sei es, die Zahl der Beschäftigten dauerhaft zu reduzieren, Neueinstellungen sollen auf ein Minimum reduziert werden. Passend dazu wurde schon Anfang November ein Einstellungsstopp für die wichtigsten deutschen Standorte Wolfsburg, Hannover, Braunschweig, Salzgitter, Emden und Kassel verhängt. Selbst bei den höchstbezahlten Tarifbeschäftigten der Gruppe »Tarif-Plus«, die aktuell rund 9.000 Mitarbeiter umfasst, will der Autobauer den Rotstift ansetzen

…“

Artikel von Ralf Wurzbacher in der jungen Welt vom 14.11.2023

 

 und mehr dazu und den Alternativen (für alle Auto/Metall-Belegschaften):


IG Metall kämpft für VW, holt ein Plus von neun Prozent heraus!


„Hochfliegende Transformationspläne in der deutschen Autoindustrie. Leitlinie: Dem Profitstreben müssen alle Hindernisse aus dem Weg geräumt werden.


Der Aufsichtsrat von VW hat sich am 3. September mit den Stimmen der Gewerkschaftsvertreter/innen auf den Zukunftsplan des Vorstands verständigt, also dessen Verabschiedung den Weg geebnet (auch wenn danach gleich der Kampf um die Deutungshoheit losging). Aber Achtung, damit will die IG-Metall nicht für die eigenen Mitglieder bei VW eine Erhöhung der Löhne um neun Prozent durchsetzen. Sie will vielmehr daran mitwirken, dass sich die Umsatzrendite bei VW von drei auf neun Prozent erhöht. (…)


Bemerkenswert, hier hat man es mit einem Anliegen zu tun, dem sich die Vertreterinnen der Gewerkschaft nicht verschließen wollen. Neun Prozent für die eigenen Mitglieder käme in ihren Augen nie in Frage, für die Nichtmitglieder von der Kapitalseite gleichwohl, obwohl sie keine Gewerkschaftsbeiträge zahlen. Denn auch die Sozialpartner von der Gewerkschaftsführung wissen um den Gegensatz von Kapital und Arbeit, wenn es um die Sicherung der Unternehmensgewinne geht. Schließlich stehen Löhne im Gegensatz zum Interesse der Kapitalseite, sie sind Kosten, die die Gewinnrechnung belasten. Die muss aber entlastet werden (und nicht eine stressgeplagte Belegschaft): „Für den Weg dorthin wird der Vorstand ein Programm auflegen, dass er ‚Operative Exzellenz‘ nennt und das alle Kostenarten angehen wird – zum Beispiel auch Material- und Vertriebskosten. Ein großer Posten davon sind aber auch die sogenannten Gemeinkosten, zu denen wiederum die Personalkosten gehören. Aus der angestrebten Reduzierung dieser Gemeinkosten beziehungsweise Personalkosten ergibt sich rechnerisch das Vorhaben, auf 50.000 zusätzlich abzubauende Stellen kommen zu wollen.“ (…)


Da macht es schon einen wesentlichen Unterschied in den Augen der IGM-Chefin, wenn die Ankündigung weiterer 50.000 Entlassungen als eine reine Rechengröße verkauft wird. Doch Entlassungen zur Steigerung der Profite zeugen in den Augen maßgeblicher DGB-Funktionäre eben nicht vom Gegensatz von Kapital und Arbeit, wenn und solange diese in Form von Abfindungen unter Mitwirkung der Gewerkschaft erfolgen. Dabei erweist sich auch der Sozialstaat als sehr hilfreich. Schließlich kalkuliert der Betrieb seine Abfindungen unter Ausnutzung aller sozialstaatlichen Regelungen. Denn bei einem Aufhebungsvertrag in beiderseitigem Einvernehmen unter Wahrung der Kündigungsfrist wird der Arbeitnehmer entweder arbeitslos oder frühverrentet oder beides. Das heißt in jedem Fall, dass der so Entlassene erhebliche Einkommenseinbußen hinzunehmen hat.


Diese Einbußen abzumildern ist das Ziel der Abfindungen, die den Schaden aber nicht vollständig kompensieren. Deshalb heißen sie auch so, die Betroffenen sollen sich mit dem geschmälerten Einkommen abfinden. Mögen die Abfindungen im Einzelfall sich auch auf große Summen belaufen – sie sind ja verteilt auf viele Jahre, in denen diese Einbußen stattfinden –, so stellen sie doch keinen Ausgleich des Einkommensverlustes her. title: UNIVERSITÀ POPOLARE T28
content:
Capire il presente per trasformare la realtà: la scelta dell’autoformazione.


Ciclo di lezioni gratuite di storia e geopolitica tenute da esperti e professori di varie università Tutti i mercoledì alle ore 19 presso il Centro Occupato Autogestito T28 in via dei Transiti 28


(Milano)


Oggi muoversi alla cieca non è più un’opzione, senza una direzione chiara e senza una struttura solida si è vulnerabili e incapaci di essere all’altezza del periodo storico che stiamo attraversando. Una sempre più ristretta cerchia di potenti tecnocapitalisti e speculatori, con l’arma della propaganda, influenza governi, istituzioni, università, agenzie di informazione e social, tentando di fermare il declino del proprio sistema capitalista attraverso la forza militare e le guerre. Per questo dobbiamo dotarci di strumenti che ci permettano di capire “che fare”, attraverso la critica materialista dobbiamo leggere il presente per agire tutti verso un’unica direzione.


Da questo nasce all’interno del

Centro Occupato Autogestito T28 di Via Dei Transiti 28, l’Università Popolare T28:

 non come un accademico esercizio di stile, ma come una necessità politica stringente per darci un’organizzazione compatta e camminare insieme, come un unico corpo, verso un unico obiettivo. Conoscere la storia è indispensabile per avere gli strumenti attraverso cui affrontare i nodi e le contraddizioni irrisolte nel presente. Sapere chi siamo è l’unico modo per capire dove stiamo andando.


OLTRE IL VERBALISMO E L’ATTIVISMO CIECAMENTE PRATICO:


la rivoluzione e la trasformazione sociale non si fanno con i discorsi vuoti e le parole astratte (il puro verbalismo), ma nemmeno con l’azione frenetica fine a sé stessa. La nostra forza deve risiedere nell’unione e nel corretto equilibrio tra la riflessione profonda e l’azione concreta.


DALLA PARTE DEGLI OPPRESSI:


non esiste denuncia autentica del presente se non c’è l’impegno a trasformarlo e non esiste impegno reale senza un’azione materiale sui territori. Non per essere solidali, ma per qualcosa di più profondo che va oltre l’assistenza,

per lottare insieme per la trasformazione radicale della realtà

, questa è l’unica solidarietà possibile. Questo gesto cessa quindi di essere una debolezza sentimentale e diventa un atto politico collettivo, una presa di coscienza di massa per essere parte integrante di una storia di lotta e resistenza mondiale contro il nemico dell’umanità, il capitalismo.


ROMPERE IL SILENZIO COL “PERCHÉ?”:


ci hanno sempre raccontato che la cultura e la storia sono neutrali, sospese sopra le parti. È una menzogna della narrazione dominante. La storia è, innanzitutto, storia di lotta di classe. Nessun ordine costituito fondato sull’oppressione e sullo sfruttamento può tollerare che gli sfruttati comincino a chiedersi collettivamente: Perchè? Noi rifiutiamo quel posizionamento ambiguo di chi, fingendosi equidistante, sceglie di fatto di non schierarsi. Noi vogliamo sapere da che parte stare. Rivendichiamo la necessità di ricostruire la storia delle lotte e dei popoli.


Vorremmo affrontare tutti quei temi e periodi storici che scuole e università evitano o narrano in maniera falsata e parziale: la storia d’Italia dalla resistenza, ai primi anni 2000, con un’ottica marxista per arrivare ai temi di attualità e geopolitica. Lezioni frontali con momenti di confronto in cui porci le giuste domande.


UNIRE LA COSCIENZA ALL’ORGANIZZAZIONE:


l’Università Popolare di T28 vuole trasformare lo studio in uno strumento,

l’autoformazione come presa di coscienza

. Non accettiamo un sapere calato dall’alto, da istituzioni che difendono gli interessi del capitale. L’autoformazione è lo strumento per svelare l’inganno in cui viviamo, per leggere il presente con occhi critici e acquisire gli strumenti teorici necessari per affrontare e superare le contraddizioni attuali. Il sapere borghese esclude; il sapere popolare include e arma la mente. L’accesso alla conoscenza della storia e del presente deve essere accessibile a tutti e a tutte, senza barriere. L’università popolare vuole essere uno spazio di

autoformazione

 dove si impara a leggere il mondo per trasformarlo.


CONOSCENZA CONTRO LA REPRESSIONE:


più forte è la coscienza politica, più solide sono le radici collettive di fronte ai tentativi di frammentazione e repressione dello Stato.


STUDIARE PER COMPRENDERE, ORGANIZZARSI PER LOTTARE.


VERSO UN COMUNE OBIETTIVO.

title: Novedad editorial: ‘Memorias de una columna olvidada. De la Tierra y Libertad a la 153 Brigada Mixta (1936-1939)’
content:
Memorias de una columna olvidada. De la Tierra y Libertad a la 153 Brigada Mixta (1936-1939)

 es el nuevo título publicado por la 

Fundación Anselmo Lorenzo

. La investigación de 

Miguel G. Gómez

, su autor, nos acerca la historia de una columna olvidada, rescatando la experiencia de aquellos hombres y mujeres que durante un tiempo 

llevaron a cabo la revolución y la guerra 

con toda la fuerza de sus corazones.


El libro lo podréis adquirir en la librería de la calle Peñuelas, 41, en Madrid, así como en 

nuestra tienda online

. Y Os recordamos que el título será presentado el sábado, 

19 de septiembre

, en 

Manresa

, donde 

Miguel G. Gómez

 (

La CNT y la Nueva Economía

), nos invitará a descubrir la historia de esta emblemática columna. Tenéis la información ampliada 

en este enlace

.


Sinopsis:


Tierra y Libertad fue una de las grandes columnas libertarias de la Guerra Civil española. Las más conocidas partieron de la capital catalana en julio y agosto de 1936 hacia el Frente de Aragón, como las columnas Durruti, Ascaso, Aguiluchos y la Roja y Negra. La columna Tierra y Libertad fue enviada a los frentes del Centro por la Generalitat de Catalunya y el Comité Regional de la Confederación Regional del Trabajo de Cataluña (CRTC-CNT) para apoyar la defensa de la capital española, amenazada por entonces por las columnas del Ejército Nacional.


Con el transcurso de la guerra, la columna fue militarizada y reforzada convenientemente y se convirtió en la 153.ª Brigada Mixta del Ejército Popular de la República. Aquella unidad participó en diversas batallas a lo largo de la guerra: Belchite, ofensiva de Aragón, Segre, Ebro y ofensiva de Cataluña.


Organizativamente perteneció durante medio año a una división dirigida por la Confederación, la 24.ª, y más adelante quedó bajo el control de la jerarquía comunista, que gozaba de gran poder en el ejército republicano, en la 30.ª División. Aun así, pudo mantener su idiosincrasia y no quedó totalmente sometida a la voluntad del estalinismo, convirtiéndose en un símbolo de la lucha libertaria.


Esta es la historia de aquella columna, de aquellos hombres y mujeres que durante un tiempo llevaron a cabo la revolución y la guerra con toda la fuerza de sus corazones.


La entrada

‘Memorias de una columna olvidada. De la Tierra y Libertad a la 153 Brigada Mixta (1936-1939)’, es la última novedad editorial de la FAL

 se publicó primero en

Fundación Anselmo Lorenzo

.

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

author: CNT Galiza
title: El concello de Cervo es condenado por incumplimiento muy grave en materia de prevención de riesgos
content:
El ayuntamiento deberá abonar casi 50.000 euros en concepto de indemnización a los miembros del GES.


Estas reclamaciones motivaron la decisión del ayuntamiento de clausurar el GES como represalia.


Tras la denuncia de la CNT, el ayuntamiento de Cervo es condenado por vulnerar el derecho fundamental a la vida y a la integridad física y moral, consagrado en el artículo 15 de la Constitución española, al incumplir la normativa sobre prevención de riesgos laborales. La situación se agrava al haberse alcanzado un acuerdo judicial al respecto que el ayuntamiento posteriormente incumplió sistemáticamente.


De este modo, el tribunal considera que el GES se encuentra en grave riesgo para su integridad física, un riesgo reiterado y prolongado en el tiempo, y declara «el incumplimiento por parte del Ayuntamiento de Cervo de la normativa sobre prevención de riesgos laborales, en particular en lo que respecta a la obligación de evaluar riesgos y planificar actividades preventivas; la falta de coordinación de la actividad empresarial; la falta de asignación de recursos preventivos y, finalmente, la falta de información y formación preventiva que debería haberse proporcionado al personal del GES; y la existencia de una violación del derecho fundamental del art. 15 CE».


Desde la sección sindical de la CNT, se recuerda que, aunque el GES no esté en activo, seguirá exigiendo el cumplimiento de la ley en materia de prevención de riesgos y salud laboral en el resto de los servicios y departamentos del Ayuntamiento, desde el departamento de obras hasta el de limpieza.


Desde la CNT recordamos la importancia del cumplimiento de las normas de seguridad y salud laboral. Los trabajadores arriesgan su salud física y mental en el trabajo mucho más de lo que creemos. Si tiene preguntas sobre el cumplimiento de las normas relativas a los riesgos laborales, ergonómicos y psicosociales en su empresa, consulte con el sindicato.

El concello de Cervo es condenado por incumplimiento muy grave en materia de prevención de riesgos

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Steven Methven
title: Will Reform’s Billionaire Donors Force a Dramatic Burnham U-Turn?
content:
Ching-ching-ching-ching-ching! No, that’s not your alarm clock going off, but the sound of Reform UK hitting the jackpot not once but twice on the billionaire one-armed bandit this weekend. 


The joint £72m gift from two billionaires is made up of £36m from each. And each of those is now the largest ever given in British political history, and almost

double the campaign funding

 jointly received by Labour or the Tories this year. Talk about bringing a bazooka to a fistfight. But that’s how billionaires roll these days.  


The red flags are raising themselves. We only have to look across the Atlantic to see what happens when big money becomes politics’ piper. The real question is not whether we want billionaires in public life – we don’t –  but why prime minister Andy Burnham backed down when he had the chance to stop it.  


On Friday night, British billionaire and

Donald Trump-pardonee Ben Delo

 announced he would be giving a £36m donation to Reform UK. By Saturday, that figure had been matched by

Thailand-based billionaire Christoper Harborne

, he of an earlier

£5m personal gift

 to Farage,

the purpose of which


nobody has ever

 quite been able

to get clear

. Harborne’s expressed motivation for the stonking new sum? “My competitive spirit inspired me to match [Delo],” he

wrote in the Telegraph

. 


Explaining his gift, Delo, who gave the party another £4m earlier this year, wrote in the Telegraph

that he wanted

 “a fair fight and a level playing field” for Reform ahead of the next general election. What it was all about, he implied, was protecting British democracy from “the political monoculture that is driving this country off a cliff”. 


Except, look around. We don’t have a political monoculture. Reform has, until recently,

topped every poll for months

. It’s now slipped into third, as much to do with the party’s

knack for financial scandal

 and Farage’s

appearing to egg on street violence

 (very offputting to Reform-curious Tories) as it does with Andy Burnham’s grasping the reins of the Labour party. And if it was just monoculture Delo was concerned about, why not split it with the Greens or Lib Dems? 


In his article, Delo insists he’s “not supporting Reform for personal gain”. And while he, like Harborne, could well

 gain professionally

and

personally from a Reform government

, there’s no point projecting piddling concerns over tax bills onto these men. Fortunes as vast as theirs multiply far faster than any state can divide. Time and again, we’ve seen it is king-like dominion the world’s billionaires seek – not that of our decorative contemporary royals, mind, but of pharaohs, emperors, and all the others who labelled ‘divine’ their brute power to force us to their will. 


In an average person, that would be called anti-democratic psychosis. Amongst most billionaires, it’s just another Monday. And while he hasn’t yet exhibited any of the anti-human zeal of others in his emerging class, it’s not like Delo hasn’t aired his own political humbugs. “We’ve seen political correctness metastasise into a totalising ideology that’s actually strangling our societies,”

he said in 2024

, “And quite frankly, I’ve had enough of it.” 


A little over-dramatic as opinions go, but almost refreshingly quaint. Like everyone else, Delo is entitled to it. Except, unlike everyone else, Delo has the resources to steer the normal ebb and flow of society’s political evolution when he doesn’t like its direction. 


Earlier projects have included

a posh suite of rooms

 provided free to the like-minded for podcasts, offices and the launch of dystopian fantasies. It’s called, in the typical self-pitying language of the right, ‘The Sanctuary’ – as though becoming specimens in a billionaire’s terrarium is the only thing that keeps these powerful networks safe. 


Delo’s and Harborne’s donations will certainly shift Reform’s fortunes. In the casino of current political life, you simply can stack the odds with money. You can also create dramatic U-turns, which is what we might soon see from the prime minister. Before entering Downing Street, Burnham

pledged a legal cap

 on the size of UK-based political donations, in an effort to stop “any one party being unduly influenced or swayed by one person or organisation”. Months later, he

reversed that position

, apparently under pressure from some of Labour’s biggest donors –

the trade unions

.


They may have

changed their tune this morning

, as the …

author: Amina Khan
title: The EU must act now to protect privacy and encryption from Canada’s overreaching Bill C-22
content:
Access Now, alongside several European civil society organisations, is urging Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, European Union commissioners, and members of the European Parliament to push for changes to Canada’s

Bill C-22, the Lawful Access Act

.


The

highly criticised

 Bill C-22,

threatens end-to-end encryption

, carries sweeping surveillance capabilities and blanket data retention mandates, and is not just a domestic privacy and data issue in Canada. Bill C-22 puts the privacy and data of millions of people in Europe, and elsewhere, at risk as it also applies to certain service providers and people outside of Canada. It allows Canadian authorities to compelEuropean-based companies to comply with demands relating to security and data of their customers based in Europe without oversight or transparency.


The European Commission cannot speak about Europe’s tech sovereignty and at the same moment, ignore Canada’s overreaching Bill C-22 threatening the privacy and security of people and businesses in Europe. The Commission must urgently initiate an honest dialogue with Canada and voice the serious concerns that academics and civil society on both sides of the Atlantic have raised regarding the bill.


Marcel Kolaja, Policy and Advocacy Director — Europe at Access Now


Bill-C22 could become law as early as October, 2026, therefore, the European Union must act now.


Canada’s Bill C-22 could undermine years of work in the EU, and around the world, to protect privacy and end-to-end encryption. The bill threatens to normalise excessive surveillance powers as routine obligations for service providers, and convert devices that work for people into devices that work against them. Steps must be taken to prevent it from becoming law.


Namrata Maheshwari, Global Encryption Policy Lead and Asia Pacific Policy Manager at Access Now.


The open letter calls on the European Commission to:


Call for the removal of Bill C-22’s sweeping surveillance capability and metadata retention mandates.


Call for the introduction of a provision that categorically prevents any measures that would, directly or indirectly, undermine or weaken end-to-end encryption.


Call for amendments to Bill C-22 to ensure alignment with the principles of necessity, proportionality, and strict access limitations, for data retention, storage, and use.


Raise Bill C-22 in the Digital Trade Agreement negotiations with Canada. A partner cannot credibly seek deeper digital integration while legislating the power to compel European providers to weaken their products in secret.


Initiate a review of Canada’s adequacy under

Article 45(4) GDPR,

 and clarify what safeguards transfers to Canada would require should the bill pass as drafted. If no appropriate safeguards could be implemented, use the European Commission’s powers to suspend the adequacy pursuant to

Article 45(5)

.


Support an oral question on Bill C-22’s implications for people in the EU addressed to the European Commission according to Rule 142 of the European Parliament’s Rules of Procedure with a resolution. 


State publicly that measures weakening encryption are incompatible with the EU’s own commitments to cybersecurity and fundamental rights and that Bill C-22 will not be treated as a precedent for policy-making.


Read the open letter.


The post

The EU must act now to protect privacy and encryption from Canada’s overreaching Bill C-22

 appeared first on

Access Now

.

author: Marcel Kolaja
title: Open letter from European civil society organisations on encryption and privacy threats in Canada’s Bill C-22
content:
To: 

Ursula von der Leyen

, President of the European Commission

Maroš Šefčovič

, Commissioner – Trade and Economic Security

Michael McGrath

, Commissioner – Democracy, Justice, the Rule of Law and Consumer Protection

Members of the European Parliament


We, the undersigned organisations and experts, write to urge you to act before Canada’s Senate completes its consideration of Bill C-22, the Lawful Access Act, and to press Canada to remove the bill’s surveillance capability mandates and its blanket data retention regime. The bill was referred to Canada’s Senate in June of this year, which is the bill’s second and final stage in Parliament before it becomes law. The Senate committee’s study of the legislation will commence after Parliament resumes its fall sitting dates in late September, and could be concluded as early as October of this year.


This is not a domestic Canadian matter. Bill C-22 reaches any provider whose services are used by people in Canada, any Canada-based provider whose services are used by people outside Canada, and to providers with no Canadian users at all, if they have a Canadian entity or are an entity belonging to a corporate group that carries out any business activity in Canada. It would allow a Canadian minister to order a European company, in secret, to weaken the security of products used across the EU, and to retain the metadata of European users. It would also do so as the EU and Canada negotiate a Digital Trade Agreement and deepen the integration of their digital economies. 


Bill C-22


has been

widely


criticised

, including by the


Internet Architecture Board

 and members of the

Global Encryption Coalition

. Bipartisan members of the United States Congress have

written

 directly to Canada’s Minister of Public Safety,

warning

 that the bill would degrade cybersecurity. Europe should not stay silent.


The bill mandates capabilities that break security for everyone. It compels an unidentified class of “electronic service providers”, such as messaging apps, cloud storage, connected vehicles, camera networks, and health trackers, to develop “any form of technical capability” and to host any device, equipment etc., enabling government access. The exception for “systemic vulnerabilities” in “electronic protections” does not save it, as non-systemic vulnerabilities remain permitted; systemic ones may be pushed into other network components, and the government retains wide discretion over the definitions. A capability built to compromise one target is a reusable weakness against every other user. The stated intention of using the bill only for targeted surveillance does not match with the language in the proposal, which could facilitate mass surveillance through weakened security systems or backdoors enabling access to data.


The bill does not prohibit orders that defeat end-to-end encryption. Canada’s government rejected explicit prohibitions sought by the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, Signal and others, who testified that the law should bar measures that negate the purpose of encryption without touching encryption directly. The narrow amendment permitting objection to “decryption” orders leaves the most damaging techniques on the table that effectively undermine end-to-end encryption: client-side scanning, compelled hidden accounts inside encrypted chat groups, and engineered entry points of the kind


zero-click spyware exploits

. The European Parliament has repeatedly opposed the weakening of encryption, most recently by excluding end-to-end encrypted communications from the scope of

Regulation (EU) 2026/1881

 on a temporary derogation from certain provisions of

Directive 2002/58/EC

 as regards the use of technologies by providers of number-independent interpersonal communications services for the processing of personal and other data for the purpose of combating online child sexual abuse. The

ECHR

 has held that weakening encryption for all users of a service cannot be necessary in a democratic society. Bill C-22 rests on the premise the Court rejected.


Its metadata retention is irreconcilable with EU law and will jeopardise Canada’s adequacy status in the EU. There are no required limits on which Canadian or foreign agencies may access the data, on what the providers may do with the retained data, or on its fate when the period ends. The European Court of Justice has held repeatedly (

Digital Rights Ireland, Tele2/Watson, La Quadrature du Net

author: CNT Madrid
title: Sparta Commodities se niega a cumplir la ley y el convenio con su plantilla
content:
Sparta Commodities es una scaleup fintech que presta servicio a grandes petroleras y energéticas, acumula más de 65 millones de dólares de inversión y se anuncia como «el futuro del trading». Desde abril,

la sección sindical de CNT le viene reclamando por escrito cuatro cosas.

 Cinco meses, dos denuncias ante la Inspección de Trabajo y tres reuniones después, la empresa ha demostrado dos cosas al mismo tiempo. Que sabe moverse cuando la miran. Y que, precisamente en lo que fija la ley y el convenio, ha decidido pasar.


Lo que pedimos desde abril es esto:

un registro horario real

, que refleje la jornada que de verdad se trabaja; la

jornada intensiva de verano

 que marca nuestro convenio;

una compensación del teletrabajo desglosada

, en una empresa cien por cien remota; y

una clasificación profesional clara.

 Lo pedimos por las buenas y nos respondieron con silencio: dos reuniones canceladas y cuatro ocasiones en las que la empresa nos dijo que no tenía respuesta. Por eso el 24 de junio presentamos denuncia ante la Inspección de Trabajo por los cuatro incumplimientos, y el 10 de julio una segunda por vulneración de la libertad sindical, presión sobre nuestro delegado y ausencia de prevención de riesgos psicosociales.


Lo que sí se ha movido


Conviene decirlo, porque es la clave de todo lo demás. Desde que existe una sección sindical organizada, la empresa:


Ha aceptado desglosar en nómina la compensación por teletrabajo y la mejora voluntaria, que estaban agrupadas en un mismo concepto.


Ha aceptado corregir la clasificación profesional en la nómina, hasta ahora genérica.


Ha puesto el protocolo frente al acoso sexual a disposición de la plantilla.


Ha pasado la encuesta de riesgos psicosociales, y comprometido a instruir a los responsables de personas para que ofrezcan de forma proactiva la compensación de las horas adicionales, sin represalias y respetando la desconexión digital.


Nada de esto llegó por buena voluntad

, llegó con una sección sindical constituida, dos denuncias en Inspección y una plantilla mirando. Y por eso mismo lo que viene después no se puede explicar como incapacidad: una empresa capaz de rehacer sus nóminas, publicar un protocolo y encuestar a su plantilla en cinco meses es una empresa que hace las cosas cuando le apetece. Si no cumple con el registro de jornada ni con la jornada intensiva, es porque ha decidido no hacerlo.


El registro de jornada, sometido a votación


Lo pedimos por escrito en abril. Nos dijeron cuatro veces que no había respuesta. Denunciamos en junio. Y el 22 de julio, en reunión con toda la plantilla española, la dirección anunció por fin su plan: someterlo a encuesta.

Como si cumplir la ley fuese una preferencia que se vota.

 En la misma reunión se advirtió a la plantilla de que el registro horario es un arma de doble filo que la empresa también podría usar en su contra: un derecho pensado para proteger a quien trabaja, presentado como amenaza para desanimar su ejercicio.


El 27 de julio, en una reunión con la sección sindical, la empresa nos dijo que prefería centrar los esfuerzos en la causa de fondo antes que en «la formalidad legal». Ahí queda: una obligación del Estatuto de los Trabajadores, degradada a formalidad.


El 1 de septiembre llegó el resultado. Con un 78% de respuestas contrarias al fichaje, la empresa se niega a implantar un sistema de registro de jornada. Es decir: preguntó a la plantilla si quería fichar después de haberle presentado el fichaje como un riesgo, y ahora usa esa respuesta como coartada para no cumplir. Pero una encuesta no deroga una ley, y ningún trabajador puede renunciar válidamente a un derecho irrenunciable ni votar que se le deje de aplicar. Lo dijimos en la mesa y lo repetimos aquí. Mientras tanto,

la sección llevará su propio registro de tiempo

 y lo trasladará a la empresa.


La jornada intensiva, negada con una excusa fabricada después


Nuestro convenio colectivo recoge jornada intensiva de verano. Sparta no la aplica. La reclamamos desde abril, propusimos dos días adicionales de vacaciones como compensación y nos ofrecimos por escrito a estudiar cualquier otra fórmula.

El 22 de julio la dirección lo negó ante toda la plantilla: «a nivel de empresa, no, porque no podemos». Y añadió una advertencia: si exigimos la ley, las vacaciones bajarían de 25 a 24 días. «Si queréis la ley, eso es la ley». Es decir,

se nos invitó a renunciar a un derecho adquirido por reclamar otro distinto.

author: Unknown
title: Autistici/Inventati - A/I (Autistici/Inventati) shuts down
content:
Author

: Autistici/Inventati

Title

: A/I (Autistici/Inventati) shuts down

Subtitle

: Stay human

Date

: September 6 2026

Notes

: On August 26, 2026, the United States government

classified

 the Italian collective Autistici/Inventati as a “Specially Designated Global Terrorist,” citing the collective’s “far-left” politics to justify the designation. They announced similar designations of the British group Palestine Action and the transnational Palestinian movement Masar Badil in the same statement.

Source

: Retrieved on September 6 2026 from https://keepitfree.ai/announcements/a/i-shuts-down-stay-human/


 The day we discovered we had been designated a global terrorist organization, we promised that we would try to resist as long as this was possible, that we would not back down as long as we could see options to stand our ground. For years, we have proudly maintained and defended a free, privacy-friendly, autonomous and politically committed infrastructure.


“Stay human”

 is not an empty phrase to us.


 It means, above all, that we have a responsibility to protect our users, those who build the human networks we rely, and for the communities who flooded us with messages of support and solidarity.


 We cannot engage in a fight or expose ourselves to manipulations that threaten the lives of these people and their loved ones, leaving them at the mercy of autocrats, fascists and agencies that take extra-legal courses of action. The possibility that our work may cause legal and financial consequences to those who are close to us — or even only have something to do with us — leaves us no choice.


A/I is shutting down. The Autistici/Inventati collective is shutting down and will soon discontinue all of the services we provide.


There is no easy way to announce or explain this


 Every day we stayed online after August 26, 2026, has been a victory, but now we are forced to stop.


 None of us holds eroic gestures and martyrs in high esteem, therefore we will demand no sacrifices. Not from us, not from anyone else. In this political climate, continuing to offer our services endangers our users and anyone who is part of our communities. In a world where allegations are disconnected from reality, we can only expect repression to be increasingly disproportionate. Under these circumstances, we are no longer able to maintain our original mission — offering secure and non-commercial digital tools.


These 25 years have been amazing. It’s been an “incredible ride”.


Now turn off your PCs, get out of your homes, struggle, hug each other and keep on smiling. We are stopping, but the Resistance and ideas do not stop. Stay human.


 We will soon send instructions on how to back up the content of your blogs, mailboxes and websites, along with more technical recommendations. But keep in mind that, just as the autistici.org domain was made unreachable without previous notice, in the next few days we might suffer similar issues that we may not be able to predict.


Autistici/Inventati Collective

author: Aline Melo
title: Doctoralia compartilha dados de saúde com Google, TikTok e LinkedIn
content:
Uma investigação do

The Markup

 (veículo especializado na cobertura de tecnologia nos Estados Unidos

)

 com a

Agência Pública

 identificou que

a plataforma de saúde Doctoralia envia informações sobre médicos, especialidades e consultas para Google, TikTok e LinkedIn em diferentes países da América Latina, como Brasil, Colômbia e México.

 O

The Markup

 já

havia detectado

 o uso de tecnologias semelhantes em sites de hospitais, serviços relacionados a

aborto

, testes de HIV e outros tipos de assistência à saúde nos EUA. 


No Brasil, os testes mostraram que, quando um usuário avançava para o agendamento, os dados sobre médico, data e horário da consulta também eram enviados ao Google. Na Colômbia, o experimento constatou que, se um usuário na cidade de Cartagena, por exemplo, marcasse com um profissional, as mesmas informações seriam redirecionadas ao LinkedIn. Já se a pessoa estivesse em Bogotá ou no México, as informações seguiriam para o TikTok.  


A análise do tráfego de dados no Brasil, realizada pela

Pública

 e pelo

Markup

, consistiu em acessar a Doctoralia e monitorar, por meio das ferramentas de desenvolvedor do Google Chrome, as requisições feitas pela plataforma médica durante a navegação. Da busca por uma especialidade de saúde ao agendamento de uma consulta, foram observadas diferentes etapas para identificar quais dados eram enviados, para quais domínios e em que momento. A análise no Brasil permitiu verificar que as informações eram transmitidas ao Google durante esse percurso. 


A lógica por trás dessas tecnologias é usada na publicidade digital: são os chamados

pixels de rastreamento, isto é, códigos embutidos nas páginas e invisíveis ao usuário.

 Eles permitem que empresas acompanhem a navegação (por exemplo, onde a pessoa clica, os assuntos pelos quais se interessa, o que compra) em determinados sites e enviem informações para plataformas de publicidade. Assim, esses dados podem ser utilizados para identificar interesses e direcionar anúncios. 


O rastreamento começa antes mesmo de o usuário fornecer informações como nome ou endereço de e-mail. Os rastreadores podiam associar a navegação a identificadores únicos, que empresas de tecnologia podem usar para vincular aquela atividade de navegação a perfis que elas já tenham em seus bancos de dados.

Informações produzidas em contextos potencialmente sensíveis, como a busca por atendimento médico, ajudam a identificar o perfil de quem utiliza essas plataformas. 


Dados do

relatório

 “Paciente Digital”, lançado pela própria Doctoralia, mostram que, em 2024, foram mais de 9 milhões de consultas agendadas por mês no Brasil na plataforma. Mulheres eram maioria entre usuários (63%). Entre as especialidades mais buscadas, estão ginecologia e obstetrícia (12%), psiquiatria (9%) e dermatologia (8%).


As buscas por atendimento e informações de saúde também estão relacionadas a mercados que movimentam grandes volumes de publicidade. Um

estudo

 da Ilumeo, empresa de inteligência de dados fundada no ecossistema da Universidade de São Paulo (USP), mostra que, no caso dos produtos de

skincare

, a decisão de compra muitas vezes acontece nas redes sociais, e não no consultório: 71% dos consumidores escolhem produtos sem orientação profissional e 57% experimentam produtos que conheceram por meio das redes. 


Usuários que agendam consultas na Doctoralia podem ter dados sobre médicos, datas e horários enviados a plataformas como o Google


O que dizem as plataformas


A Doctoralia afirmou que as ferramentas mencionadas na investigação são utilizadas para medir o desempenho das próprias campanhas publicitárias da plataforma de saúde.

A empresa ainda negou utilizar essas ferramentas para vender dados pessoais e afirmou que não recebe pagamentos de plataformas de publicidade em troca destas informações. 


A empresa também informou que está realizando uma revisão técnica e jurídica detalhada das questões levantadas pela reportagem, incluindo as configurações técnicas, e que pretende tomar as medidas consideradas adequadas a partir dos resultados dessa análise.


O Google afirmou que possui “políticas rigorosas e de longa data contra a coleta de informações privadas de saúde ou a veiculação de anúncios baseados em informações sensíveis” e disponibiliza ferramentas para ajudar os clientes a evitar a coleta de dados de saúde.


O LinkedIn declarou que suas políticas “proíbem a instalação” de sua principal ferramenta de rastreamento, a Insight …

author: Unknown
title: Mourning declared in Kobanê
content:
A fire broke out at Kobanê Prison at around 2:00 a.m. on Saturday, September 12, killing nine people. Today, two days of mourning were declared in the city for the victims.


Since early this morning, shops and businesses across Kobanê, particularly those in the central market, have remained completely closed as a sign of mourning and respect for the deceased.


All business activity across the city has come to a halt, and Kobanê’s streets remain empty.


A funeral ceremony for the nine victims had been scheduled for today, but was postponed due to the mourning period. The ceremony will instead be held on Monday at 5:00 p.m.

author: Unknown
title: Aydın: People who suffered so much loss stand firmly for peace
content:
The Freedom Movement has begun announcing the names of those who lost their lives in clashes, particularly over the past 10 to 15 years. The announcements, which have been made over the past month, have been followed by condolence gatherings and commemorations in many cities across Turkey and Kurdistan.


The large turnout at these gatherings has been subject to attempts at criminalisation, particularly by circles opposed to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which have issued statements to this effect.


ANF spoke to anthropologist Derya Aydın from the Initiative for Respect for the Dead and Justice (IRDJ) about the right to mourn and hold condolence gatherings during conflict-resolution processes, examples from around the world, and the significance of the gatherings now being held across Kurdistan and Turkey.


We need to use the term “right” carefully


Let me begin with this: What is the right to mourn, and what does it mean?


At the time it emerged that the remains of members of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) had been transferred from Garzan Cemetery in Bitlis (Bedlîs) to Istanbul, both what had happened there and the neglect and indignities inflicted on politically contested dead bodies were largely discussed within a legal framework. Both the violations and the arguments against them were confined to questions of legislation. That was in 2018, and I began to think that violence directed at politically contested dead bodies could not be reduced to a matter of law, but had to be understood as a political and ethical issue.


For this reason, I think we need to use the language of “rights” carefully when discussing condolence rituals, mourning and commemoration; in other words, the ways in which the dead are received, honoured and laid to rest, the practices through which they are transferred to the afterlife in the manner considered most appropriate, and the ways in which people say goodbye to them or continue living with them. We need to think beyond both legally codified “rights” and what are often described as “natural rights”.


Across history, the ways in which people send the dead to the afterlife have been complex and diverse, both in their duration and their rituals. A positivist approach, for example, may regard biological death as an absolute end and construct the notion of “rights” on that basis, but others may not understand death in the same way. They may say, “It is the body that has gone,” and continue living with their dead. This does not necessarily have to be a theological understanding; it may also be cultural or political. Anthropology has made this remarkably visible over the past two centuries. I find this particularly important because I believe the perception of political death arising from conflict in Kurdistan encompasses precisely this understanding. I am not saying, of course, that we should not speak of “rights”. Rather, I am saying that we must address rights without overlooking biological and symbolic forms of death shaped by political and ethical frameworks.


A number of legal instruments seek to protect the dignity of the dead and those left behind and to restore the dignity that has been violated. Within international human rights and humanitarian law, these include the customary international humanitarian law compiled by the International Committee of the Red Cross, the 1907 Hague Convention, the 1949 Geneva Conventions and, finally, the United Nations Manual on the Effective Prevention and Investigation of Extra-Legal, Arbitrary and Summary Executions, known as the Minnesota Protocol, which sets out principles directly concerning the treatment of dead bodies. These legal frameworks were also designed to apply in situations of conflict.


The Hague and Geneva Conventions, for example, contain fundamental obligations requiring parties to a conflict to search for and recover the dead and prevent their bodies from being pillaged; to record all available information about the dead and safeguard belongings of material or sentimental value before returning them to the opposing side or their relatives; to ensure that the dead are buried with dignity and, where possible, in accordance with the rites of their religion; and to mark graves and protect burial sites. Many of these principles are reflected in domestic legislation, and as a party to these conventions, Turkey is already obliged to implement them.
