title: Yaşlanmanın sinyalini veren 5 şaşırtıcı işaret
content:
Fotoğraf: cottonbro studio/Pexels

Yaşlanma çoğu zaman yüzde oluşan kırışıklıklar, saçların beyazlaması veya fiziksel gücün azalmasıyla ilişkilendiriliyor. Oysa biyolojik yaşlanma yalnızca dış görünüşte meydana gelen değişimlerden ibaret değil. Uyku düzeninden kavrama gücüne, denge becerisinden iyileşme hızına kadar günlük yaşamda fark edilmeyen pek çok değişiklik, vücudun yaş alma sürecine dair ipuçları verebiliyor.

Bu belirtilerin tek başına “yaşlandığınızı” göstermediği, ancak bazı değişikliklerin yaşla birlikte daha sık görüldüğü belirtiliyor.

Gençlik döneminde birkaç saatlik uykusuzluk, yoğun egzersiz veya yorucu bir günün ardından vücudun toparlanması daha hızlı olabilir. Yaş ilerledikçe ise kasların ve diğer dokuların kendini yenileme süreci yavaşlayabilir.

Bunun nedenleri arasında kas kütlesindeki azalma, dolaşım ve metabolizmadaki değişiklikler ile bağışıklık sisteminin yaşla birlikte değişmesi bulunuyor.

Bu nedenle eskiden bir gecede atlatılan yorgunluğun artık birkaç gün sürmesi, yaşlanmayla birlikte ortaya çıkabilen değişimlerden biri olabilir.

Yaşlanmanın ilk belirtileri her zaman güç kaybı şeklinde ortaya çıkmıyor. Bazen denge ve hareket koordinasyonundaki küçük değişiklikler daha erken fark edilebiliyor.

Merdivenlerden inerken daha dikkatli olma, tek ayak üzerinde durmanın zorlaşması veya ani yön değiştirirken eskisi kadar rahat hareket edememe bunlara örnek gösterilebilir.

Denge; kas gücü, görme, iç kulak sistemi ve sinir sistemi arasındaki koordinasyona bağlı. Bu sistemlerin herhangi birindeki yaşa bağlı değişiklikler hareket becerilerini etkileyebiliyor.

Kavanoz kapağını açmak, ağır bir çantayı taşımak veya bir nesneyi sıkıca kavramak eskisinden daha zor hale geldiyse bu yalnızca “el gücünün azalması” olarak görülmemeli.

Kavrama gücü, genel kas gücü ve fiziksel işlev hakkında bilgi veren önemli göstergelerden biri olarak araştırmalarda kullanılıyor. Yaşla birlikte kas kütlesinin ve kas fonksiyonlarının azalması kavrama gücünü de etkileyebiliyor.

Ancak belirgin veya hızlı gelişen güç kaybının normal yaşlanma olarak kabul edilmemesi gerekiyor. Özellikle tek taraflı güç kaybı gibi ani değişiklikler tıbbi değerlendirme gerektirebilir.

Yaşlandıkça yalnızca uyku süresi değil, uykunun yapısı ve zamanlaması da değişebilir. İleri yaşlarda insanlar daha erken uyanabilir, gece boyunca daha sık uyanabilir ve derin uyku süreleri azalabilir. Bu durum, kişinin sabah daha erken kalkmasına veya gece uykusunun daha parçalı hale gelmesine neden olabilir.

Ancak sürekli uykusuzluk, aşırı gündüz uykululuğu veya yeni ortaya çıkan ciddi uyku sorunları yalnızca yaşa bağlanmamalı. Uyku apnesi, depresyon, kullanılan ilaçlar ve çeşitli sağlık sorunları da benzer şikayetlere yol açabilir.

Vücudun kendini onarma kapasitesi yaş ilerledikçe değişir. Derinin yenilenmesi yavaşlayabilir ve özellikle ileri yaşlarda küçük kesik, sıyrık veya morlukların tamamen düzelmesi daha uzun sürebilir.

Bunun arkasında hücre yenilenmesindeki değişiklikler, bağışıklık yanıtındaki farklılıklar ve cildin yapısal özelliklerinin değişmesi gibi birçok faktör bulunur.

Bununla birlikte yaraların belirgin biçimde geç iyileşmesi normal yaşlanmanın kaçınılmaz bir sonucu değildir. Özellikle tekrarlayan veya uzun süre kapanmayan yaralar diyabet gibi sağlık sorunlarının araştırılmasını gerektirebilir.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Randi Beers
title: The Canadian roots of Donald Trump’s wealth
content:
Canadians are well aware that America’s boorish and vulgar president

 is wealthy.


Donald Trump received a head start in life with money from his father, a real estate developer in New York who bent the rules and skirted legalities while amassing the wealth that he left to his children.


Fred Trump set up trust accounts for his five children, of which Donald Trump was the fourth.

 By the age of three, he was earning the equivalent of US$200,000 per year in today’s dollars, or about C$276,000. At the time he graduated from college, he was receiving about US$1 million annually (C$1.38 million).

By some estimates, he received over US$400 million (C$553 million) from his father.


Most of this is well known. Less well-known are the northern Canadian roots to the family’s fortune. 


In Kallstadt, Germany, in 1885, Donald Trump’s grandfather, Friederich Trump, was 16 years old and didn’t like the thought of working in the family vineyard or as a barber, a job for which he was being trained. So he left a note for his widowed mother and left home one night. He wanted to be rich and headed for Manhattan, eventually becoming an American citizen. 


He moved on to Seattle, where he changed his first name to the more American-sounding Frederick and where he thought the easiest money would be made in the red-light district, known as the Lava Beds. He leased a restaurant, the Poodle Dog, and renamed it the Dairy Restaurant. It had a dining area and a bar, and it advertised “private rooms for ladies.” This was thinly-disguised code for the availability of prostitutes. 


In 1894, he was attracted to an area north of the city named Monte Cristo. He filed a bogus mining claim there and built a cheap hotel that offered food, drink and women.


Three years later, in 1897, he saw newspaper headlines claiming that gold had been discovered in the far North.


He sold his eatery and headed there. The following year, in Bennett, B.C., just south of the Yukon border, he opened a business called the Arctic Restaurant and Hotel. It was a two-story, shoddily-built structure with an impressive façade, where c

ustomers could pay their bills with gold dust.


Following the same recipe for success that he had used in the south, Frederick Trump’s business was little more than a brothel.


A reporter for the Yukon Sun wrote, “I would not advise respectable women to go there to sleep as they are liable to hear that which would be repugnant to their feelings and uttered, too, by the depraved of their own sex.” 


His stay there was short. Greener pastures beckoned in Yukon.


Frederick Trump dismantled his flimsily-built hotel in Bennett, loaded it onto a barge, and floated it downriver to Whitehorse. There the Arctic Restaurant occupied a prime location right across from the railway depot. It offered booze and gambling, and of course the company of what were euphemistically called “sporting ladies” in an area curtained off by dark velvet.


The elder Trump made a lot of money in a short time. Whitehorse author Pat Ellis, who wrote

Financial Sourdough Starter Stories

, said, “He made quick money on booze, and he was a good cook.”


But in 1901 the North-West Mounted Police wanted to curtail gambling and liquor sales, and the business of the “scarlet ladies.”


Frederick Trump left town.


He returned to Germany where he visited his mother and married the girl next door, Elizabeth Christ, in 1902. Shortly thereafter, they immigrated to New York. But Elizabeth became homesick and they returned to Germany. Frederick Trump tried to regain his German citizenship, but was ordered deported.


The couple returned to New York. They had three children. 


When Frederick Trump left Whitehorse, he reportedly had $16,000 in U.S. currency, a sum worth over $600,000 today. He was always careful with money and, in 1910, he began to invest in real estate in Queen’s, a borough of New York City.


He died eight years later, leaving his properties to his wife, who proved to be a capable manager and grew the business.


Eventually his son Fred, who had been only 12 when his father died, took over the enterprise. When he died in 1999, he left a property empire valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars.


This is the source of Donald Trump’s fortune. It grew from his grandfather’s nest egg, earned through a restaurant, bar and brothel in Whitehorse.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Repression and Resistance in Russia: An Overview
content:
from the

CrimethInc.

 collective

 (

09/09/2026

)


Across three decades, Russia has been at the forefront of the worldwide 

descent into authoritarianism

. Vladimir Putin’s government has suppressed opposition in ways that aspiring autocrats like Donald Trump are still striving to emulate. Yet despite widespread repression, there is still resistance in Russia, and as Putin’s model proliferates, people everywhere around the world stand to benefit from learning about it. Likewise, we should support Russian anarchist and 

anti-war

 prisoners, both because resistance within Russia offers hope for the eventual end of war and totalitarianism and because, should autocrats consolidate power where we live, we will wish for people to support us, as well.


The following text is based on a presentation Antti Rautiainen offered at the 

Baltic Anarchist Book Fair

 in Tartu on May 30, 2026. You can watch a video of the presentation 

here

 or listen to it via 

Spotify

. The above photograph shows the consequences of an action carried out by the anarchist Ruslan Sidiki.


In Russia, street protests against the war were crushed in 2022, the first year following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. According to the human rights organization 

OVD Info

, 18,901 arrests for anti-war protests in year 2022 were followed by 274 arrests in 2023, 41 arrests in 2022, and just 13 arrests in first half of the year 2025. The reason for this sharp decline was the “Ilya Dadin” law of 2014, according to which “repeated offenses in following the established organization of protests” across a period of 180 days can result a prison sentence of up to 5 years. Thousands of people were arrested once or twice for taking part in anti-war street activities in 2022 and received either a fine or a prison sentence of a few days—but few risked being arrested for a third time.


Detentions for anti-war actions by year, first half of 2025, according to OVD-Info.


Russian polls have been unreliable since spring 2022. After the criminalization of anti-war opinions, some polling companies reported that up to 60% of people queried refused to give answers. Before the polls became unreliable, 58-71% of Russians indicated a pro-war sentiment in various polls. However, opinions were intensely polarized between different groups. People in major cities were more anti-war than those in other locations; younger people were more anti-war, as were women. The greatest division was between people who watch television, the chief propaganda tool of the state, and people who do not watch it. Among people less than 30 years old who do not watch television, 

80% were anti-war

.


The general impression among critical Russians is that the majority of those in Russia still share a pro-war sentiment. However, a shift is visible even in officially tolerated opinion polls. According to polls by the 

Levada Center

, over the past two years, the share of Russians supporting the continuation of the war effort has dropped from around 41% to around 28%, and share of those who support peace talks has grown from 51% to 62%. At the same time, the number of those who support making concessions to Ukraine is at 24%: people want peace, but on terms favorable to Russia.


Of course, this may simply reflect what people are willing to say to anonymous pollsters.


Another difference is that now, people in small cities and rural localities are expressing more anti-war sentiment than those in major urban centers. Moscow is the most pro-war city. The likely explanation is that most of the frontline casualties are from small, peripheral communities.


Factors Undermining the Anti-War Movement


Why, after more than four years of war, with more than a million Russian soldiers wounded or dead, is anti-war sentiment still confined to a minority?


As the saying goes, “It’s the economy, stupid.” During the first years of the war, salaries were growing even with high inflation rate. Starting in 2004, the Russian ruling class hoarded huge profits of the oil and gas trade in a fund currently known as the “National Wealth Fund.” Instead of raising the standard of living by investing in healthcare, social benefits and services, and the like, the money was stashed to be spent on wars and militarization. Now these billions are finally flowing into the economy in the form of wartime investment. The unemployment rate is negligible; in some cases, salaries have multiplied at factories in regions …

author: Cierra Bettens
title: Fighting fires with good fire: How Indigenous land guardians are protecting the boreal forest
content:
Spanning 270 million hectares in Canada, the boreal forest is home to billions of trees, 150 bird species, and 85 per cent of the country’s wetlands.


More than 70 per cent of Indigenous communities in Canada call it home.


As the executive director of the Indigenous Leadership Initiative, Innu forester Valérie Courtois believes Indigenous land guardianship is key to protecting it.


“Fire is a natural part of the boreal ecosystem,” Courtois said. “Many of the species within the boreal depend on fires for propagation.”


“What we’re worried about, though, are large catastrophic fires that are seemingly happening more often and at a higher intensity and severity than what we would necessarily call natural. And that is due to a number of factors related to climate change.”


This week on APTN News InFocus, Courtois joins us to talk about protecting the boreal forest through Indigenous fire guardianship. We also hear from Arnold Lazare, the interim CEO of the National Indigenous Fire Safety Council.


“We strive to enable the communities to empower themselves,” Lazare said. “When we go into a community, we don’t just go in, give the training and leave. We like to leave equipment behind so that they have the resources.”


Back in June, the Standing Senate Committee on Agriculture and Forestry released Canada on Fire. The 119-page report detailed the catastrophic and escalating effects of wildfires on lives and communities.


The committee also learned that there isn’t a single authority responsible for wildfire preparedness. Instead, duties are delegated across federal, provincial and municipal levels.


However, with the sheer speed of wildfires, coordination challenges between governments can lead to delayed response times, inconsistent planning, and difficulties accessing equipment and personnel.


“There seems to be a lot of finger-pointing going on saying it’s provincial, it’s federal, it’s community,” Lazare said.


On Sept. 11, Canada announced the completion of the Parks Canada National Fire Equipment Cache in Banff National Park. The feds say the hub will provide equipment storage and boost wildfire preparedness, response and operations across the country.


With First Nations leaders in Ontario calling for a public inquiry into wildfires, Courtois and Lazare join me on InFocus to discuss why they think empowering communities and supporting traditional fire practices is key to protecting forest for future generations.

author: Randi Beers
title: News quiz Sept. 12 | Stranger than fiction
content:
It’s quiz time! Let’s roll.


1. An Ottawa-based non-profit is paying Nunavut teens to do what while scrolling their social media feeds?


A. Report the types of advertisements they are seeing.


B. Fact check viral social media posts.


C. Like and share posts about from the organization about media literacy.


2. Nunatsiaq News introduced readers to a new northern correspondent last week. What is different about her?


A. She is a licensed pilot.


B. She is a high school student.


C. She’s not human. She’s one of 121 AI “correspondents” that repackages existing news stories for a website based out of Hong Kong.


3. Oil spills are bad for the environment, but scientists are in Chesterfield Inlet studying one type of creature seems to benefit from it. What creature is that?


A. Sea cucumbers seem to love oil and grow to massive sizes when exposed to it.


B. There are naturally occurring microbes that feed off of oil.


C. Oil adheres to plankton floating in the water, making them shimmer, which makes them more visible to predators, like whales.


4. A new development in Grise Fiord is making it easier for people to determine when it’s safe to travel. What is it?


A. Better radar and satellite imagery helps determine when precipitation is coming.


B. A new weather station about five kilometres east of the community shows real-time conditions.


C. A high school student has taken up amateur meteorology as a hobby and is providing local weather reports that residents say have been extremely accurate so far.


5. A sea can full of non-perishable food arrived this month in Igloolik, from a New Brunswick-based non-profit. How much does it cost to ship a sea can on the sealift?


A. $10,000


B. $12,000


C. $14,000


David Didier, left, a geography professor and director of the Northern and Arctic Coastal Research Lab, with his child strapped to his back, and Terry Noah, owner of Ausuittuq Adventures, install a live timelapse station near Grise Fiord on July 8. The automated camera system set up near the coastline helps researchers monitor the sea ice conditions. (Photo by Anne-Marie Dubé)


Answers:


1. B — Teens aged 13 to 19

can apply

 to learn different fact-checking skills like reverse image search and fact verification and use those skills to fact check viral posts that pop up on their social media accounts. They earn $150 for their first analysis, then $100 for subsequent fact checks.


2. C — Leah Qammaniq is an AI “correspondent” who

republishes

 copyrighted news content and renders AI images to go along with it.


3. B — Scientists are in Chesterfield Inlet

studying microbes

 that feed off of oil. Some new species have been discovered during the study, said one researcher, and local Inuit are being invited to help name these new species.


4. B — A new

weather station

 outside the community allows people to check real-time conditions before heading out onto the land. It’s part of a larger project studying coastal erosion and water conditions around Grise Fiord.


5. B — The sea can, which is filled with approximately $50,000 worth of food,

costs $12,000 to ship

, said Rick Maher, who runs the non-profit group A Tapestry of Kindness with his wife Linda Maher. The group gets some funding help from Nutrition North Canada for the project, which aims to send two sea cans per year to northern communities.

author: Eman Abu Zayed
title: War Has Produced Lasting Severe Delays in Gaza’s Divorce and Custody Rulings
content:
Courts in Gaza face frequent power outages and shortages of printing supplies. Some have only one computer.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

In a makeshift structure made of worn-out fabric in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, 25-year-old Samira Abdel Hamid is trying to build a life for her two children, 3-year-old Mohammad and 18-month-old Issa.

Abdel Hamid does not call the place where she lives a tent. As she describes it, it is “a place where the most basic necessities of life are unavailable, and where a person cannot feel that they are living a normal life.” While trying to meet her children’s needs, Abdel Hamid is also carrying the burden of a court case, waiting for a decision that could determine the shape of her and her children’s lives in the coming period.

“I never imagined my life would end up like this,” Abdel Hamid told me, recalling her life before the war. She married Salim Al-Astal on June 1, 2023, and lived with him in their apartment in northern Gaza, while he worked in a metalworking workshop. But after the war began, the family was forced to flee on October 11, 2023. Their home was bombed that same day, as was the metalworking workshop on which her husband depended for his livelihood.

“In one day, we lost our home and our work, and there was nothing left for us to return to,” Abdel Hamid said. The family fled to Deir al-Balah, where the harsh conditions of displacement and the lack of stability began to affect their marriage. With the loss of their income and the mounting pressures of war, Abdel Hamid said her relationship with her husband deteriorated. She said he no longer treated her as he had before and eventually stopped providing financial support for her and their children.

“I tried to endure it for the sake of my children, but I reached a point where I felt I could not continue,” Abdel Hamid said. As married life became an additional source of pressure, she decided to separate from him, hoping to raise her children away from the pressures she had been experiencing in the relationship.

“I didn’t choose separation because it was easy. On the contrary, I knew my situation was already difficult, but I wanted to have some peace and raise my children without having another person constantly pressuring me,” she said.

But her decision did not end her suffering. Between displacement, the lack of a stable source of income, and the responsibility of caring for two young children, Abdel Hamid also found herself waiting for a legal process with no clear end in sight.

“I just want the case to be over and to know what my future is. Every time the hearing is postponed, I feel like I’m still stuck in the same situation.”

“Every day that passes while I wait, my children and I pay the price,” she said, alluding to the difficulty of supporting her children while in legal limbo.

The legal delays faced by Abdel Hamid are an obstacle that many other Gaza residents are facing as well. Israel’s war on Gaza, which has killed more than 72,000 Palestinians according to the latest figures cited by the United Nations from Gaza’s Ministry of Health, has not only destroyed homes and livelihoods but has also caused extensive damage to civilian infrastructure and essential services, including the judicial system. Gaza’s judicial system operates through two complementary tracks: regular courts, which handle civil, criminal, and other legal disputes, and religious Sharia courts, which primarily handle personal-status matters such as marriage, divorce, custody, and alimony. The two systems operate within the broader Palestinian justice system, with distinct areas of jurisdiction.

To obtain a divorce and secure the legal and financial rights arising from it, Abdel Hamid had to turn to the Sharia court and substantiate her case. But she began the proceedings while the judicial system was operating under extraordinary conditions imposed by the war, including damage to court buildings, mass displacement, the dispersal of staff and litigants, and difficulties accessing files and documents. UN reports have indicated that access to legal remedies in parts of Gaza has been severely disrupted, while courts have faced significant pressure due to displacement and the influx of large numbers of litigants.

For Abdel Hamid, the delay in her divorce proceedings has become an ongoing obstacle to ending her marriage and starting an independent life with her …

author: Frances Madeson
title: Louisiana Residents Are Resisting Plans to Build ICE Jail on Contaminated Site
content:
Organizers are hard at work to convince officials to roll back an agreement with a private prison operator.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Alexandria International Airport, which is part of England Airpark in central Louisiana, is currently known as the busiest ICE Air Operations hub for deportations in the United States. Immigration and Custom Enforcement’s Alexandria Staging Facility, a terminus for people being removed from the U.S., is reviled the world over by abused and deported refugees from Cameroon to Haiti. Even as the town’s tourism office works in overdrive to entice visitors to the area’s natural and cultural attractions — the scenic Red River, lush butterfly gardens, and historic homes such as the one where venerated Harlem Renaissance poet Arna Bontemps lived from birth to three years old — violence against immigrants keeps coming.

Last year, Alexandria was mentioned in a lawsuit regarding a child with Stage 4 kidney cancer who was deported along with two siblings in April 2025. Now, the same polarizing federal agency that has killed people on the streets and in its custody is planning to expand its operations in Alexandria. ICE has grabbed another chunk of the England Airpark, which is situated on a former U.S. Air Force base that shuttered in 1992 due to groundwater contaminated with catastrophic levels of PFAS, a class of persistent “forever chemicals” linked to cancer, reproductive harms, and other serious health problems.

If ICE has its way, as soon as the end of September, it aims to place immigrant women (including those who are pregnant), infants, and children, on top of this toxic site in a 528-bed facility, to be housed in a former military barracks. To further sully the atmosphere, ICE has contracted with the LaSalle Family Foundation, an affiliate of the private prison operator LaSalle Corrections, which runs the Irwin Detention Center in Georgia. A congressional investigation found ample evidence of rampant medical abuse at the facility, including medically unnecessary gynecological procedures performed on migrant women.

Louisiana residents are mobilizing in opposition to the immigration jail with the help of CENLA Activism, a grassroots group of concerned residents that mobilizes activists in central Louisiana and organizes mutual aid for communities under siege by ICE.

At the center of this scheme is England Economic and Industrial Development District (EEIDD), an independent political subdivision of the State of Louisiana charged with taking over and redeveloping the England Air Force Base after it was decommissioned.

EEIDD, the governing authority for England Airpark, has a board of commissioners who are all appointed by the mayors of Alexandria and Pineville, the Central Louisiana Regional Chamber of Commerce, and Rapides Parish officials. The 10 commissioners, all men, were persuaded last February to rubber-stamp the contract for the ICE jail. Their executive director Ralph Hennessy told Verite News that “the facilities are set up like a traditional dorm room,” and said to ABC affiliate WBRZ that it would bring an economic benefit to the Airpark.

As Hennessy put it: “There are a lot of people in Central Louisiana that make a living off of the immigration world, the prison world.” ICE will pay EEIDD, the district he works for, $530,000 annually. In May, Hennessy’s own base salary rose from $209,615 to $240,000.

Since learning of EEIDD’s plan to allow ICE to detain children in their community, mothers, grandmothers, Christian clergywomen, and educators organizing with CENLA Activism have showed up to EEIDD board meetings, and they have no intention of letting up. They’ve channeled their fury into demonstrations to raise public awareness in heavily trafficked parts of town on the National Day of Action: ICE Out Visibility Event, and have held prayer services that have often brought participants to tears. Pastor Leah Rachal said at an August 25 service she helped organize: “We might disagree on some of the other minutiae of immigration policy. But not this. Nobody wants children to be detained.”

At an August 27 EEIDD board of commissioners meeting, where more than 100 Louisianans packed the overflow room, Rose Marie Norton greeted board chair Oday Lavergne as “the heart of Alexandria” and reminded him, “The protests aren’t necessarily against you; they’re against the system.”

author: Clare Hymer & Charlotte Reck
title: Police Raid Home of 84-Year-Old Priest Who Joined Just Stop Oil Protest
content:
Police raided the home of an 84-year-old priest following her arrest last week at a Just Stop Oil protest.


Sue Parfitt had been arrested alongside other protesters at Parliament Square in London on Wednesday 2 September during Andy Burnham’s first PMQs, with activists calling on the prime minister

not to approve new oil and gas licenses

.


Parfitt’s home in Henbury, Bristol, was searched sometime between 7.30pm that evening and noon the following day while she was being held in police custody. 


She only discovered her home had been the site of a swoop when she returned on Thursday afternoon following her release. 


She recalled being told what had happened by her landlord. “I was quite surprised,” she said, “and then I was terrified.” 


It hasn’t been made clear to Parfitt why the raid occurred, although she suspects the police had intended to seize her laptop. 


Parfitt doesn’t have a smartphone or social media. “They [the police] think you’ve got all these contacts on your devices,” she said. “Well, I don’t because I’m not in any of these chats.” 


Parfitt shares her home with her landlord and another tenant, who was not home at the time of the incident. 


No other protesters held in custody last week are believed to have had their homes raided.


Novara Media has approached the police for comment.


Parfitt has been arrested more than 30 times in total, mostly for defying the proscription of Palestine Action but also for participating in climate protests with Just Stop Oil, Insulate Britain, Extinction Rebellion and Christian Climate Action.


At a protest opposing the ban on Palestine Action in July 2025,

Parfitt told Novara Media

 she wasn’t afraid of being arrested.


“I know that we are in the right place doing the right thing,” she said, while holding a sign reading “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action”. 


“As my friend Ruth always says, ‘we cannot be bystanders’.”

author: Unknown
title: Fire at Kobane Prison: 9 killed, 16 injured
content:
A fire broke out at a prison in Kobane. According to initial reports, 9 detainees lost their lives and 16 others were injured, some of them seriously.


 


The injured were taken to hospitals in Kobane for treatment.


 


The cause of the fire is not yet known, and the relevant authorities are continuing their investigation. Kobane’s Internal Security Forces are expected to issue a statement regarding the incident.


 


The fire at the Kobane prison broke out following public protests in the city. Protesters were demanding an investigation into the abduction and killing of Defense Ministry member Sami Hiso in Heseke.


 


General Security Forces intervened against the protesters and detained several young people from the city.


 


According to sources in the region, General Security Forces have begun surrounding the city.

author: infolibre
title: «NAZA»: Ο μηχανισμός της γενοκτονίας στη Γάζα με AI, στο Φεστιβάλ Βενετίας
content:
Το

«NAZA»,

 ένα ντοκιμαντέρ που εξετάζει τις

μαζικές δολοφονίες στη Γάζα με τεχνητή νοημοσύνη

 από το Ισραήλ, έλαβε 25λεπτο χειροκρότημα στο

Φεστιβάλ Κινηματογράφου της Βενετίας

 στις 10 Σεπτεμβρίου. Η ανταπόκριση του κοινού σηματοδοτεί τη μεγαλύτερη σε διάρκεια επευφημία που έχει σημειωθεί ποτέ στη Βενετία, με το κοινό να επευφημεί και να κυματίζει παλαιστινιακές σημαίες. Σε σκηνοθεσία των

βραβευμένων με Όσκαρ

 Ισραηλινών σκηνοθετών 

Yuval Abraham

 και

Rachel Szor,

, η ταινία αντλεί τον τίτλο της από έναν ισραηλινό στρατιωτικό όρο για τους θανάτους αμάχων (παράπλευρες απώλειες) και αποτελεί το μοναδικό ντοκιμαντέρ που διεκδικεί το βραβείο Χρυσού Λέοντα..


Ο τίτλος της ταινίας προέρχεται από ένα ισραηλινό στρατιωτικό ακρωνύμιο που χρησιμοποιείται ευφημιστικά για τις «παράπλευρες απώλειες», τη δολοφονία αμάχων – αποκρύπτοντας τόσο την εκ των προτέρων γνώση που έχει για το πόσοι άνθρωποι είναι πιθανό να σκοτωθούν σε κάθε χτύπημα, όσο και την πρόθεση καταστροφής που συνοδεύει την στρατιωτική εκστρατεία από την αρχή.


Υπό αυτό το πρίσμα, η παρουσία ενός ατόμου που το Ισραήλ θεωρεί στόχο δολοφονίας σε ένα συγκεκριμένο σπίτι γίνεται το «παράπλευρο» ζήτημα. Μάλιστα, σε πολλές περιπτώσεις, ο στόχος αποδείχθηκε ότι δεν ήταν καθόλου παρών. Η ίδια η δολοφονία ήταν το ζητούμενο.


Την

παραγωγή

 υπογράφει ο Guardian και η ταινία περιλαμβάνει εκτενείς μαρτυρίες Ισραηλινών αξιωματικών των μυστικών υπηρεσιών και στρατιωτών που εμπλέκονται στην παρακολούθηση και την εξ αποστάσεως δολοφονία Παλαιστινίων πολιτών.


Γυρισμένο νύχτα στις στέγες του Τελ Αβίβ, το ντοκιμαντέρ αποκαλύπτει τα συστήματα πίσω από τις μαζικές δολοφονίες Παλαιστινίων αμάχων στη Γάζα. Περιλαμβάνει συνεντεύξεις με ισραηλινούς αξιωματικούς των μυστικών υπηρεσιών που περιγράφουν λεπτομερώς

πώς τα συστήματα στόχευσης με τη βοήθεια τεχνητής νοημοσύνης επέλεξαν παλαιστινιακούς στόχους χρησιμοποιώντας δεδομένα που εξήχθησαν από χιλιάδες χακαρισμένα κινητά τηλέφωνα.

 Το «NAZA» διεκδικεί το βραβείο Χρυσό Λέοντα, το οποίο έχει προγραμματιστεί να απονεμηθεί στις 12 Σεπτεμβρίου.


Μέσα από τις συνεντεύξεις τους, οι δημιουργοί υποστηρίζουν ότι

οι μαζικές απώλειες αμάχων δεν αποτέλεσαν απλώς «παράπλευρες απώλειες»,

 αλλά συνδέονταν με ένα οργανωμένο σύστημα εντολών, διαδικασιών και αποφάσεων που επέτρεπε τον εκ των προτέρων υπολογισμό των απωλειών και την έγκριση επιθέσεων ακόμη και όταν ήταν γνωστή η παρουσία οικογενειών και αμάχων.


Η ταινία επιχειρεί παράλληλα να εξετάσει την

κοινωνία του Τελ Αβίβ

 και την απόσταση ανάμεσα στην καθημερινότητα της ισραηλινής κοινωνίας και την καταστροφή στη Γάζα. Οι  μαρτυρίες δείχνουν την ύπαρξη ενός ευρύτερου συστήματος συνευθύνης, πέρα από συγκεκριμένα πρόσωπα ή μόνο την πολιτική ηγεσία, και θέτουν το ερώτημα πώς μια κοινωνία μπορεί να αποδεχθεί ή να κανονικοποιήσει την απανθρωποποίηση ενός άλλου λαού.


Η ταινία μας δεν επικεντρώνεται στα κίνητρά τους, κάτι που ήταν μια συνειδητή επιλογή. Ασχολείται κυρίως με την ίδια τη δολοφονία και τι καθιστά δυνατή αυτή τη δολοφονία. Το να αφιερώνουμε πολύ χρόνο στα ηθικά και πολιτικά συναισθήματα των πηγών θα ενείχε τον κίνδυνο να μετατοπίσουμε το κέντρο βάρους μακριά από τα θύματα, κάτι που δεν θέλαμε να κάνουμε.


Η παραχώρηση ανωνυμίας σε άτομα που, σύμφωνα με τις δικές τους μαρτυρίες, συμμετείχαν σε φρικτά εγκλήματα δεν είναι κάτι που παίρνουμε ελαφρά τη καρδία. Ωστόσο, δεδομένης της συνεχιζόμενης διάπραξης αυτών των εγκλημάτων, νιώσαμε την υποχρέωση να δημοσιοποιήσουμε τις μαρτυρίες τους με την ελπίδα ότι αυτό θα μπορούσε να συμβάλει στις προσπάθειες για τον τερματισμό της επίθεσης. Οι μαρτυρίες των στρατιωτών υπονοούν επίσης ένα πολύ μεγαλύτερο σύστημα, για το οποίο τα υψηλότερα κλιμάκια της πολιτικής και στρατιωτικής ηγεσίας του Ισραήλ φέρουν την τελική ευθύνη. Ελπίζουμε ότι η ταινία μπορεί να συμβάλει στη λογοδοσία για τα σοβαρά εγκλήματα του Ισραήλ και στη δικαιοσύνη για τα θύματά του.


Αλλά η ταινία δεν είναι μόνο μια συλλογή μαρτυριών στρατιωτών. Στρέψαμε επίσης τον φακό της κάμερας στο Τελ Αβίβ και τους κατοίκους του τη νύχτα, ανακρίνοντας την πόλη ως μια φούσκα στην οποία η συνηθισμένη ζωή συνεχίζεται ενώ οι Παλαιστίνιοι σφαγιάζονται μόλις 60 χιλιόμετρα μακριά. Μέσα από το βλέμμα μας στην πόλη από την οποία διαχειρίζεται ο πόλεμος στη Γάζα, προσπαθήσαμε να παρατηρήσουμε τους μηχανισμούς συμμόρφωσης που επιτρέπουν μια τόσο εκτεταμένη αδιαφορία.


Με αυτόν τον τρόπο, βρεθήκαμε να θέτουμε ερωτήματα που έθεσε η γενιά των παππούδων μας – ερωτήματα που έχουν θέσει …

author: Corey Larocque
title: ‘News’ site forces journalists to face future with AI
content:
The future arrived without warning two weeks ago, dragging Nunatsiaq News into the world of artificial intelligence controversy this paper had previously managed to avoid.


A journalist colleague at another organization sent an email, pointing out a new website that posts AI-generated articles about the North, based on news that real organizations had already reported.


We News appears to be a Hong Kong-based website using more than 100 AI-generated “correspondents” whose articles are cobbled together using artificial intelligence instead of traditional reporting. They gather their information from news articles written by real journalists and from official sources such as the RCMP and Government of Nunavut.


It calls its Nunavut correspondent Leah Qammaniq. She comes complete with an Inuit-sounding name, an AI-generated picture of a woman with Inuit features and even an AI-generated back story about being “raised in the North.”


Miriam Lafontaine, a new but very real Nunatsiaq News reporter, wrote a thorough

news story

 about this troubling development. She did it the old-fashioned way by interviewing real people, researching the issue and sitting down in front of a computer to type it out.


Our Inuit readers will decide for themselves whether We News is deceptively fabricating an imaginary Inuk reporter. But to this qalluanaaq journalist, it’s offensive to make up an Inuk correspondent out of thin air to dupe readers.


It’s bad enough that real non-Inuit pretend to be Inuit to get benefits intended for Inuit. But an AI-generated correspondent pretending to be Inuk because it’s somehow more authentic to get AI-generated news from an AI-generated correspondent?


As a journalist, this is an alarming, disappointing — but predictable — development in the intersection of news and artificial intelligence.


For the record, Nunatsiaq News does not use generative AI in its reporting or in its advertising. This is a stand news organizations are increasingly taking.


Experts in the news business were quick and unequivocal in condemning this AI intrusion into the news business.


News Media Canada president Paul Deegan called it “theft” on “an industrial scale.”


Canadian Association of Journalists president Brent Jolly said the manipulation of the public’s right to know by AI “disgusts” him. He warned that the public doesn’t realize what’s happening and more questions aren’t being asked about how to address it.


It’s not just Nunatsiaq News getting ripped off. Our hard-working colleagues — competitors at Nunavut News and CBC — are having their articles harvested by We News. Legitimate journalists must now contend with an AI-fuelled site that uses their own work to compete with them. We News appears to be displaying Google ads, so it’s making money off the backs of real journalists and their employers.


That’s why Nunatsiaq News urges its readers to be aware of where their information comes from and to avoid AI-generated information that steals the work of real journalists. We want readers to get their information from us, but if not, they should at least get it from a real news organization.


The news business is a difficult one. Having to compete for readers and advertisers against an elusive organization that uses AI to repackage our own content is going to make that even harder for real journalism to thrive.


Journalism is about storytelling — a real reporter talking to real people about what happens in their community, building trust with sources, and then sharing the story with readers.


What We News is doing is not journalism, despite the fact that it has created itself in the image of real, trusted news organizations.

author: Unknown
title: AYM Başkanı: Tayfun Kahraman dosyasında iki yönden ihlal var, karar yayımlanma sürecinde
content:
Türkiye Basın Federasyonu Başkanı Sinan Burhan ve Yönetim Kurulu üyeleri, Anayasa Mahkemesi (AYM) Başkanı Kadir Özkaya ile bir araya geldi.


ANKA'nın aktardığına göre Özkaya toplantıda, Gezi Parkı davası hükümlüsü Tayfun Kahraman'ın ikinci bireysel başvurusu ile ilgili konuştu. Kahraman'ın hem "adil yargılanma hakkının" hem de "bireysel başvuru hakkının" ihlal edildiğine karar verildiğini hatırlatarak, kararın gerekçesinin yayımlanma sürecinde olduğunu bildirdi.


Günümüzde anayasa yargısının yalnızca hukuk normlarının Anayasa’ya uygunluğunu denetleyen bir mekanizma olmadığını belirten Özkaya, anayasa yargısının temel hak ve özgürlüklerin etkin şekilde korunması ve demokratik hukuk devletinin güçlendirilmesinde de önemli bir rol üstlendiğini söyledi.


AYM'nin incelemelerinde uluslararası yaklaşımların, Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi kararlarında kullanılan ilke ve standartların, diğer ülkelerin anayasa mahkemelerinin kararlarının ve Türkiye'deki yüksek yargı organlarının içtihatlarının titizlikle incelendiğini belirten Özkaya, raportörlerin görüşleri ve Mahkemenin kurumsal birikiminin de değerlendirme sürecine dahil edildiğini ifade etti. Özkaya, bireysel başvurulardaki ihlal iddialarının "adalet odaklı bir yaklaşımla" değerlendirildiğinin altını çizdi.


"AYM, kanuna uygunluk değil, anayasal denetim yapıyor"


Bireysel başvurunun niteliği ve yüksek yargı organlarının yetkilerine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulunan Özkaya, Anayasa Mahkemesi ile Yargıtay, Danıştay ve diğer yargı kurumları arasında hiyerarşik bir ilişki bulunmadığını ifade etti.


Özkaya, her bir yargı kurumunun görev, yetki ve sorumluluklarının Anayasa ve kanunlarda düzenlendiğini, yargı kurumlarının görev ve yetkilerini bu çerçeve içerisinde yerine getirip kullandığını ifade etti. AYM'nin bireysel başvurularda bir "kanun yolu mahkemesi gibi hareket etmediğini" vurgulayan Özkaya, AYM’nin kanuna uygunluk değil, anayasal denetim yaptığını belirtti.


Kahraman kararının gerekçesi yayımlanma sürecinde


Özkaya, Gezi Parkı davası hükümlüsü Tayfun Kahraman'ın ikinci başvurusuna ilişkin olarak ise AYM'nin hem "adil yargılanma hakkının" hem de "bireysel başvuru" hakkının ihlal edildiğine karar verdiğini hatırlattı.


Kararın gerekçesinin yayımlanma sürecinde olduğunu belirten Özkaya, AYM'nin görevinin kişinin suçlu olup olmadığını belirlemek değil, yargılamada usule ilişkin güvencelerin sağlanıp sağlanmadığını denetlemek olduğunu söyledi. AYM'nin Kahraman ile ilgili ilk kararının da bu kapsamda olduğuna dikkati çekti.


AYM, Tayfun Kahraman hakkında bir kez daha "ihlal var" dedi


2 Nisan 2026


(HA)

author: Unknown
title: “12 Eylül’ün karanlık mirası sürüyor”
content:
Türk Mühendis ve Mimar Odaları Birliği (TMMOB) Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Ali Ekber Çakar, 1980 darbesinin 46. yıldönümünde yaptığı açıklamada 12 Eylül’ün karanlık mirasının sürdüğünü söyledi.


Çakar, 12 Eylül’ün yalnızca belirli bir tarihsel dönemle sınırlı kalmadığını, “ideolojisi, kurumları ve uygulamalarıyla” bugüne kadar etkisini sürdürdüğünü kaydetti.


“Bu ülke topraklarında büyük trajedilere yol açan, tarihimize kara bir leke olarak geçen 12 Eylül Askeri Darbesi’ni bir kez daha lanetliyoruz” diyen Çakar, darbe döneminde demokratik hak ve özgürlüklerin ortadan kaldırıldığını, emekçilerin örgütlü gücünün ve toplumsal muhalefetin hedef alındığını ifade etti.


“Neoliberal politikaların temelleri 12 Eylül’de atıldı”


Türkiye’nin bugün içinde bulunduğu ekonomik ve toplumsal krizin temelinde 12 Eylül sonrasında uygulamaya konulan neoliberal politikaların bulunduğunu aktardı.


“Cumhuriyetin ikinci yüzyılına girerken ülkemiz, ilerleme ve demokratikleşme yönünde bir adım atmak yerine, birikmiş tüm kazanımların aşındırıldığı, kamusal yapının zayıflatıldığı ve toplumsal yaşamın her alanda geriye itildiği bir sürecin içine çekilmiştir.” dedi.


Özelleştirme, piyasalaştırma ve güvencesizleştirme politikalarının farklı iktidarlar tarafından 46 yıldır sürdürüldüğünü belirten Çakar, bu politikaların kamusal varlıkların tasfiyesine, çalışanların hak kayıplarına ve ekonomik krizlerin kalıcılaşmasına yol açtığını anlattı.


“12 Eylül’de temelleri atılan ekonomide neoliberal, toplumsal yaşamda muhafazakar, siyasette otoriter yönetim anlayışı”nın mevcut yönetim sistemi altında daha da derinleştiğini ve kurumsal bir nitelik kazandığını söyledi.


19 Mart sonrası yaşananlara dikkat çekti


Son dönemdeki siyasal ve hukuki gelişmelere de açıklamasında yer veren Çakar şöyle devam etti:


"Bugün 12 Eylül’ün baskı ve zor anlayışı, siyasal iktidarın hukuku araçsallaştırdığı yeni biçimler altında sürdürülmektedir. Özellikle 19 Mart’tan bu yana giderek ağırlaşan hukuksuzluklar; seçilmiş belediye başkanlarının görevlerinden uzaklaştırılması, halkın iradesinin yargı ve idari kararlarla etkisizleştirilmeye çalışılması, siyasetçilerin, belediye başkanlarının, bürokratların, gazetecilerin, öğrencilerin ve toplumsal muhalefetin farklı kesimlerinin gözaltı ve tutuklamalarla baskı altına alınması 12 Eylül’den bugüne taşınan yönetim anlayışının güncel yansımalarıdır. Gerici ve faşizan politikalar altında sömürü, açlık ve yoksulluk yaşamlarımızın olağan koşulu haline getirilmiştir.


Halkın seçimlerde ortaya koyduğu iradeyi tanımayan, demokratik temsil mekanizmalarını işlevsizleştiren bu anlayış, kendi varlığını sürdürmek uğruna seçim sonuçlarını kabul etmemeyi dahi tahayyül eder hale gelmiştir. Bu durum yalnızca demokrasi açısından değil, ülkemizin geleceği açısından da büyük bir tehlikedir. Ancak milyonlarca yurttaşın demokrasi, hukuk ve adalet talepleri göstermektedir ki ülkemizin içine sürüklendiği bu krizlerden çıkışın yolu halkın ortak mücadelesinde ve demokratikleşmededir.


Bir kez daha altını çiziyoruz: Eşit, özgür, demokratik, laik ve sömürüsüz bir ülkenin kurulması; 12 Eylül’ün siyasal, ekonomik ve toplumsal alandaki tüm mirasının ortadan kaldırılması, hukukun üstünlüğünün, halk egemenliğinin ve demokratik hak ve özgürlüklerin yeniden tesis edilmesiyle mümkündür."


TMMOB’nin 12 Eylül’ün mirasına karşı mücadelesini sürdüreceğini belirten Çakar, gelecek nesillerin “eşitliğin, özgürlüğün, demokrasinin, laikliğin ve adaletin hakim olduğu bir ülkede” yaşaması için mücadele etmeye devam edeceklerini söyledi.


(HA)

author: 张皓翔
title: The General‑Strike in Human Production: Geschlechtsliebe, Marriage‑Family and the Unbinding of Labour‑Power【人的生产总罢工——Geschlechtsliebe、婚姻家庭与劳动力解绑】
content:
Rooted in the Marxist‑historical‑materialist tradition, this monograph re‑examines intimate relations, marriage, family and contemporary low‑fertility crises by drawing on Engels’ theory of two kinds of production — namely the production of material means of subsistence and the production of human‑beings themselves. It introduces the German‑language analytical category Geschlechtsliebe, which integrates bodily‑sexual dimensions (sex‑drive, sexual relations) and inter‑subjective spiritual‑affective love, to break down the common conceptual confusion among desire, romance, marital contract and demographic reproduction.

The book develops a core dialectical contradiction specific to human production: the objective reality of human production versus subjective inclinations toward human production. Against this framework, modern‑era late‑marriage, low‑fertility and child‑free choices are interpreted not merely as cultural or individual‑value shifts, but as a spontaneous general strike within the sphere of human production. Such popular refusals of procreation undermine capitalism’s access to fresh labour‑power supplies, yet remain disorganised and lack conscious socialist‑political guidance, carrying risks of self‑destruction for the working class itself.

Critically distancing itself from Social Reproduction Theory (SRT) and its “reproduction of labour‑power” paradigm, the text argues that household‑care and child‑rearing create new labour‑power, rather than repairing pre‑existing labour‑power stocks. It undertakes comparative criticism of socialist and capitalist family‑law systems, pointing out that capitalist family institutions centre on private‑property inheritance, while socialist family institutions ought to pursue de‑unilateralisation of social‑input costs in human production, mitigating the disproportionate burdens borne by women in procreation and care‑giving.

Going beyond a sole critique of private ownership, the work advances a deeper thesis: labour‑power element‑formation constitutes a more fundamental source of alienation. Even after private ownership is abolished, so long as human capacities are treated as separable, measurable, allocable elements, women will still bear one‑sided burdens within human‑production processes. Looking toward communist society, the author envisages the socialisation of human‑production workflows. Once procreation and upbringing become socialised processes, sexual relations will shed all social‑functional mandates and turn into genuinely private interpersonal affairs, and love will escape institutional regulation entirely.

This work combines political‑economy critique, comparative legal history and theoretical speculation on communist‑era gender relations. It calls for the transformation from spontaneous reproductive refusal toward the conscious socialist reconstruction of human‑production, contributing fresh arguments for Marxist theories of gender, family and emancipation.

author: Unknown
title: Cumartesi Anneleri/İnsanları Kenan Bilgin’in akıbetini sordu
content:
Cumartesi Anneleri/İnsanları, gözaltında kaybedilen yakınlarının akıbetinin açıklanması ve sorumluların yargılanması talebiyle sürdürdükleri eylemlerinin 1120’ncisini İstanbul Beyoğlu’ndaki Galatasaray Meydanı’nda gerçekleştirdi.


Kayıp yakınları ve insan hakları savunucuları bu hafta 12 Eylül 1994’te Ankara’da gözaltına alındıktan sonra kaybedilen Kenan Bilgin’in akıbetini sordu. 


Eylemde gözaltında kaybedilenlerin fotoğrafları ve karanfiller taşındı. Basın açıklamasını da Türkiye İnsan Hakları Vakfı (TİHV) İstanbul Temsilcisi Ümit Efe okudu.


“Gözaltına alındığı inkar edildi”


12 Eylül 1980 askeri darbesi döneminde yaşanan ağır hak ihlallerini hatırlatarak sözlerine başlayan Efe, çok sayıda kişinin devlet görevlilerince gözaltına alındığını, işkence gördüğünü ve daha sonra gözaltına alındıklarının inkar edildiğini söyledi.


Daha sonra Kenan Bilgin’in 35 yaşındayken, 12 Eylül 1994’te Ankara Dikmen’deki bir otobüs durağından gözaltına alınarak Ankara Emniyet Müdürlüğü Terörle Mücadele Şubesi’ne götürüldüğünü anlattı ve şunları söyledi:


“Kenan’ın ailesi, avukatları ve İnsan Hakları Derneği ona ulaşmak için girişimlerde bulundu. Ancak Ankara Emniyeti, Kenan’ın gözaltına alındığını inkar etti. Bunun üzerine 11 tanık ortaya çıktı. Tanıklar, Kenan Bilgin’i Ankara Emniyeti’nde gözaltında ve işkencede gördüklerini kamuoyuna açıkladılar.


Bilgin Ailesi, Kenan’ın bulunması ve akıbetinin ortaya çıkarılması için Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’na başvurdu. Kenan’ı bulmak, sorumlulara ulaşmak ve etkili bir soruşturma yürütmek için girişimde bulunan Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcısı Selahattin Kemaloğlu’nun görevini yapması engellendi ve Ankara’dan sürüldü.


Soruşturmayı devralan Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcı Vekili Özden Tönük ise ailenin ve tanıkların başvuruları üzerine gerekli soruşturma işlemlerini gerçekleştirmedi. Tanık Ö.A. ve M.Y., ‘Kenan Bilgin’i hücreden alıp götüren polisleri teşhis edebileceklerini’ söylemelerine rağmen bu yönde hiçbir işlem yapılmadı. Bunun yerine tanıkların polisi ve devleti küçük düşürmeye yönelik gerçek dışı iddialarda bulunduklarını ileri süren üç sayfalık bir rapor hazırlandı ve dosya kapatıldı."


Kenan Bilgin’in tanığından Cumartesi Anneleri'ne mektup: Her anına tanığım


13 Eylül 2025


AİHM Türkiye’yi mahkum etti


İç hukuk yollarından sonuç alamayan Bilgin ailesinin Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi’ne (AİHM) başvurduğunu hatırlatan Efe, AİHM yargıçlarının Ankara’ya gelerek tanıkları, savcıları ve polis yetkililerini dinlediğini söyledi.


Mahkemenin, Kenan Bilgin’in tutulduğu gözaltı merkezinde de inceleme yaptığını kaydederek şunları söyledi:


“Mahkeme, Kenan Bilgin’in 12 Eylül 1994 tarihinde güvenlik güçleri tarafından gözaltına alındığını ve 3 Ekim 1994 tarihine kadar güvenlik güçlerinin elinde bulunduğunu tespit etti. Bu süreçte Kenan’ın gözaltında tutulduğuna ilişkin hiçbir resmi kayıt tutulmadığını belirledi ve Türkiye’yi oybirliğiyle mahkum etti.”


Efe, AİHM kararına rağmen Bilgin’in akıbetini ortaya çıkaracak etkili bir soruşturma yürütülmediğini ekledi.


Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nın daha sonra, “Kenan Bilgin’in Ankara Emniyeti’ne bağlı nezarethanelerden birine alındığına dair hiçbir veriye ulaşılamadığını” ileri sürerek zamanaşımı gerekçesiyle takipsizlik kararı verdiğini, karara yapılan itirazların da reddedildiğini aktardı.


Efe ayrıca, gazeteci Özer Akdemir’in o dönemde Bilgin’e ilişkin bir mektup kaleme aldığını ve Bilgin’in gözaltına alındığına dair tanıklıkta bulunduğunu söyledi.


“Yüzleşme olmadan barış olmaz”


Açıklamanın ardından söz alan Kenan Bilgin’in kardeşi İrfan Bilgin, Türkiye’de devam eden Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci’ne değindi.


Bilgin, “Devlet barış sürecinde samimi ise bu işlenen insanlık suçlarının mağdurlarıyla yüzleşmek zorundadır. Yüzleşmediği sürece bu ülkede barış olmaz” dedi.


Eylem, karanfillerin Galatasaray Meydanı’na bırakılmasıyla sona erdi.


(HA)

author: 张皓翔
title: Praxis‑Centred Culturalism【实践性文化主义】
content:
Based on Marxist historical materialism, this paper systematically critiques contemporary symbolic cultural theories represented by Clifford Geertz, and proposes an ontological framework of "cultural duality". It points out that there exists a theoretical overreach in the current field of cultural studies, which equates culture entirely with symbolic systems and neglects the more fundamental practical foundation of culture. The author argues that culture consists of two heterogeneous forces: first, practical culture, which refers to human beings’ active practical activities of transforming the subjective and objective worlds. It is revolutionary, progressive and fundamental, and constitutes the ontological basis of all cultures. Second, symbolic (intellectual) culture, which emerges from the need to abstract and disseminate practical experience, is a derivative and subsystem of practical culture, and is inherently conservative and lagging.

The paper further reveals the rupture and inversion of cultural duality in class society: by monopolizing symbolic systems and educational apparatuses, the ruling class places symbolic culture above practical culture, resulting in the "aphasia" of working people in the symbolic world and cultural oppression. Finally, the paper extends the theory to the era of artificial intelligence. It points out that large language models are essentially probabilistic recombinations of existing human symbolic corpora, and they are systematically taking over the production of symbolic culture, thus dissolving the symbolic privileges of intellectual elites. This historical process provides a solid foundation in productive forces for "setting things right" in practical culture. Once the symbolic barriers are broken, working people will regain cultural dominance through their "consciousness as labor power" — including value judgment, aesthetic creation and practical decision-making — which cannot be replaced by algorithms, and realize the return of "the primacy of practical culture". The paper also emphasizes that technology is only a condition for liberation rather than a decisive factor, and true liberation still depends on the active struggle of the working people.

author: 张皓翔
title: On the Illegitimacy of Fairness, Democracy, and Justice【论公平、正义、民主的非法性】
content:
This monograph undertakes a systematic theoretical demystification of the three value categories enshrined in modern society—fairness, democracy, and justice—grounded in the methodology of historical materialism. Departing from Marx and Engels’s thesis that “the ideas of the ruling class are in every epoch the ruling ideas,” the author reveals that these concepts are not transhistorical, universal values, but rather an “inverse narrative” deliberately fabricated by the ruling class in class societies to conceal the structural oppression and exploitation that they are inherently incapable of resolving. The central argument of the book is that the substantive function of fairness, democracy, and justice lies in substituting recognition for abolition and piecemeal reform for radical eradication, thereby obscuring the fundamental goal that the subjugated classes should truly pursue—liberation.

The book is organised into four chapters. Chapter One systematically establishes the theoretical basis for treating fairness, democracy, and justice as an “illegitimate narrative,” arguing that they are essentially a illusory mirror-image generated by the incurable maladies of class society. Chapter Two redefines the nature of liberation from a dialectical perspective, demonstrating that liberation is not a negative narrative but rather the most momentous affirmative construction in human history. Chapter Three carries out a “double sublation” of both bourgeois democracy and proletarian democracy, contending that democracy in any form is merely a transitional instrument rather than an ultimate end. Chapter Four establishes “liberation” as the sole criterion and red line for the institutional design of socialism and communism, and elaborates how “consciousness as labour-power” can ultimately supersede the category of democracy in practice.

The book makes several original theoretical contributions. First, through the critical method of political economy, it divests fairness, justice, and democracy of their juridical guise as eternal truths, restoring them to their actual status as ideological projections of specific relations of production. Second, it proposes the analytical framework of the “inversion of affirmative and negative narratives,” revealing how the ruling class packages false fairness and justice as “affirmative constructs” while stigmatising genuine liberation as “negative destruction.” Third, it offers a novel conceptualisation of democracy as a “means rather than a stage of existence,” thereby deepening the classical Marxist tradition of the self-sublation of proletarian democracy. This work is recommended for scholars and postgraduate students in political philosophy, Marxist theory, and scientific socialism.

author: Unknown
title: Van’da görüntüleri sonrası soruşturma açılan düğünde takılan altınlar odunluktan
content:
Van'da düğün görüntüleri sonrası 'Suçtan kaynaklanan malvarlığı değerlerini aklama' suçundan tutuklanan Mehmet Fatih Tançalan ile hakkında gözaltı karar verilen ve halen aranan eşi Çağla Öz Tançalan'ın düğününde takılan altınlar, Muradiye ilçesinde polisin düzenlediği operasyonda bir evin odunluğunda valiz içerisinde ele geçirildi. Ev sahibi gözaltına alındı.

Sosyal medya fenomeni Çağla Öz ile 'Vanlı Kara Haydar' olarak tanınan Mehmet Fatih Tançalan'ın pazar günü Van'da düzenlenen düğününe ait görüntüler, sanal medyada geniş yankı buldu.

Görüntüler üzerine Van Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından soruşturma başlatıldı. Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan Mehmet Fatih Tançalan, 'Suçtan kaynaklanan malvarlığı değerlerini aklama' suçundan sevk edildiği nöbetçi sulh ceza hakimliğince tutuklandı.

Hakkında gözaltı kararı bulunan eşi Çağla Öz Tançalan'ın yakalanması için çalışmalar sürerken, hazırlanan MASAK raporunda ismi geçen annesi N.O. İstanbul'da, M.S.T. ise dün Muradiye ilçesinde gözaltına alındı.

Van Emniyet Müdürlüğü ekipleri, yaptıkları istihbari çalışmayla Muradiye ilçesinde bir adrese operasyon düzenledi. Adreste yapılan aramada, evin odunluk bölümünde bulunan bir valiz içerisinde Tançalan çiftinin düğününde takıldığı belirtilen altınlar ele geçirildi. Altınlara el konulurken, ev sahibi gözaltına alındı.

Van Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı'nın yürüttüğü soruşturma ise sürüyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: İHD: Darbelere karşı demokrasiyi savunuyoruz
content:
İnsan Hakları Derneği (İHD) İstanbul Şubesi, 12 Eylül 1980 askeri darbesinin 46. yılında, darbe bildirisinin okunduğu İstanbul Beyoğlu’ndaki TRT Radyo binası önünde açıklama yaptı.


“12 Eylül darbesinin 46. yılında darbelere karşı demokrasiyi savunuyoruz” pankartının taşındığı açıklamada basın metnini İHD Eş Genel Başkanı Oya Ersoy okudu.


Ersoy, 12 Eylül darbesinin ardından ağır insan hakları ihlallerinin yaşandığını belirterek, darbe sonrasında hazırlanan 1982 Anayasası’nın halen yürürlükte olduğuna dikkat çekti.


Benim için 80'ler ve 12 Eylül


Bugün  12:00


“OHAL uygulamalarının birçoğu varlığını sürdürüyor”


Türkiye’de olağanüstü hal (OHAL) dönemlerinde hayata geçirilen birçok uygulamanın kalıcılaştığını söyleyen Ersoy, şöyle konuştu:


“OHAL uygulamalarının birçoğunun halen varlığını sürdürdüğü ve birçok insan hakları ihlalinin yaşandığı bir dönemden geçiyoruz. Türkiye’yi 2002 yılından bu yana kesintisiz olarak yöneten AKP hükümeti darbelere karşı olduğunu ve sivil bir anayasa yapılması gerektiğini sürekli olarak vurgulamasına rağmen bu yönlü bir tavır ortaya koymak bir yana, anayasa hükümlerine uymaktan imtina etmiş, çıkarılan yasa ve yönetmeliklerle demokratik ortamın daha da daralmasına yol açan pratik içerisinde olmuştur.”


15 Temmuz 2016’daki darbe girişiminin ardından çıkarılan Kanun Hükmünde Kararnameleri (KHK) hatırlatan Ersoy, binlerce kamu görevlisinin ihraç edildiğini, belediyelere kayyım atandığını ve OHAL döneminde çıkarılan düzenlemelerin daha sonra yasalaştırıldığını söyledi.


“Geçici olağanüstü hal, kalıcı ve sürekli bir duruma dönüşmüştür. Darbe girişimi sırasında ve sonrasında yapılan yasal değişiklikler ile demokrasiyi tahkim etmek yerine otoriter rejim inşası tercih edilmiştir”

 ifadelerini kullandı.


Kürt meselesi ve çözüm süreci


Ersoy, Türkiye’de otoriterleşmenin artmasıyla birlikte Kürt meselesinin de uzun yıllar “inkarcı ve güvenlikçi” bir yaklaşımla ele alındığını söyledi.


Geçmişte sorunun demokratik yollarla çözümüne yönelik girişimlerin sonuçsuz kaldığını belirten Ersoy, Ekim 2024’te başladığını ifade ettiği yeni sürecin ise farklı gelişmelere sahne olduğunu kaydetti.


Abdullah Öcalan’ın 27 Şubat 2025’te yaptığı çağrının ardından PKK’nin kendisini feshettiğini hatırlatan Ersoy, TBMM’de siyasi partilerin temsilcilerinden oluşan bir komisyon kurulmasını, komisyon raporunun kamuoyuna açıklanmasını ve “çerçeve yasa” olarak anılan düzenlemenin Meclis Genel Kurulu’nda kabul edilmesini, eksikliklerine rağmen Kürt meselesinin çözümü açısından önemli gelişmeler olarak değerlendirdi.


“Muhalefete dönük baskılar arttı”


“Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci” devam ederken muhalefet partilerine yönelik baskıların da arttığını söyleyen Ersoy, İHD’nin tüm antidemokratik uygulamalara karşı olduğunu belirtti.


Demokratik ve çoğulcu bir anayasa ihtiyacının sürdüğünü kaydederek, yeni bir anayasa yapılabilmesi için öncelikle temel hak ve özgürlükler alanında adımlar atılması gerektiğini ekledi.


“Cuntacılar tarafından hazırlanan bir anayasa ile yönetilen Türkiye’nin gerçek anlamda demokratik ve çoğulcu bir anayasaya olan ihtiyacı gün gibi ortadadır” diyen Ersoy, şöyle devam etti:


“Ancak devlet bu ülkede yaşayan halklar ve inançlar ile ‘barışmadan’, demokratik bir anayasa yapmak da pek olası görünmemektedir. Bu kapsamda ifade özgürlüğü, protesto hakkı, medya özgürlüğü, seçmen iradesine saygı, ulusal ve uluslararası mahkeme kararlarına saygı, yargı bağımsızlığı konularında gerekli yasal ve idari düzenlemeler yapıldıktan sonra sivil bir anayasa hazırlanmalıdır.”


12’sindeydi Eylül’ün


Bugün  00:00


Onarıcı adalet ve hafıza mekanları çağrısı


Ersoy, darbeciler ve darbe döneminde işlenen suçlarla ilgili etkin yargısal süreçlerin sürdürülmesi, mağdurların zararlarının giderilmesi ve onarıcı adalet mekanizmalarının kurulması çağrısı yaptı.


Diyarbakır Hapishanesi gibi darbe döneminin simge mekanlarının tarihsel gerçeklere uygun hafıza mekanlarına dönüştürülmesi gerektiğini de belirten Ersoy, sözlerini şöyle tamamladı:


“Hak ve özgürlüklere yönelik kısıtlamalara son verilmesini, çatışma çözümü girişimlerinin yanında demokratikleşme adımlarının atılmasını ve pozitif barışın sağlanması gerektiğini vurguluyor, bunun mücadelesini vereceğimizi yineliyoruz.”


(HA)

author: Unknown
title: Tüm zamanların zam rekoru: Motorine salı günü 6 TL 62 kuruş zam bekleniyor
content:
Ankara – Akaryakıt zamları devam ediyor. Motorine, salı gününden geçerli 6 TL 62 kuruş zam bekleniyor. Sektör kaynakları, bu zamla birlikte motorinin litresinin 100 TL’ye yaklaşacağını ve tüm zamanların rekorunu kıracağını belirterek, "Motorinde, yeniden ÖTV ayarlaması yapılır ve zammın bir bölümü ÖTV’den karşılanır mı? Farklı formüller devreye konulur mu? Zam olduğu gibi pompa satış fiyatlarına yansıtılır mı? Pazartesi günü saat 16.00’da işin rengi ortaya çıkar" dedi.

Orta Doğu'da enerji tesisleri ve kritik deniz taşımacılığı güzergâhlarına yönelik saldırılar, petrol arzına ilişkin kaygıları artırdı. Gerilim, Brent petrol ile ABD Batı Teksas türü ham petrol (WTI) fiyatları üzerinde yukarı yönlü baskı oluşturdu. Brent petrol, 100 doları aştı ve 104-105 dolardan işlem görüyor.

Küresel piyasalarda benzin ve motorinin metrik ton fiyatları da yükseldi. Motorinin metrik ton fiyatı, bin 371 dolardan bin 520 dolara dek çıktı. Ardından bir miktar gevşedi. Halen bin 479 dolardan işlem görüyor.

Küresel fiyat hareketleri önce benzine, ardından da motorine zammı gündeme getirdi Benzine, bugünden geçerli 3 TL 20 kuruş zam yapıldı. Motorine de salı gününden geçerli 6 TL 62 kuruş zam bekleniyor.

Sektör kaynakları, "Cuma günü piyasa kapanış değerlerine göre motorine salı günü 6 TL 62 kuruş zam söz konusu" dedi. Kaynaklar, bu zamla birlikte motorinin litresinin 100 TL’ye yaklaşacağını ve tüm zamanların rekorunu kıracağını anımsatarak, "Motorinde, yeniden ÖTV ayarlaması yapılır ve zammın bir bölümü ÖTV’den karşılanır mı? Farklı formüller devreye konulur mu? Zam olduğu gibi pompa satış fiyatlarına yansıtılır mı? Pazartesi günü saat 16.00’da işin rengi ortaya çıkar" ifadesini kullandı.

title: „Zentrum Automobil e.V.“ – eine neofaschistische Betriebsgruppe (nicht nur) bei Daimler (nicht nur in Stuttgart)
content:
Dossier


„

Zu den Betriebsratswahlen bei Daimler in Untertürkheim ist auch in diesem Jahr wieder die Liste „Zentrum“ angetreten. Die dahinter stehende Gruppe „Zentrum Automobil e.V.“ ist eine neofaschistische Betriebsorganisation. Ziel ist gemäß ihrer Satzung der Aufbau von Betriebsgruppen in der Automobilindustrie, ausgehend vom Pilotprojekt beim Autohersteller Daimler. Dort arbeitet die Gruppe am Daimler-Stammsitz in Stuttgart-Untertürkheim seit Jahren

…“

Beitrag der MLPD aus dem Jahr 2014 (kw17)


 – siehe zu den 

Betriebsratswahlen 2018

 und den Nazis auch in anderen Branchen/Unternehmen unser

Dossier: AfD & Co: Nach den Köpfen nun auch in Betriebe und Betriebsräte?!

 und hier speziell zu Daimler die Entwicklung nach den BR-Wahlen 2018 und danach:


Der Kampf der extremen Rechten um die Arbeiter:innenklasse. Zur Verankerung und Bedeutung von Zentrum und AfD in Betrieben


„…

Für die Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) bietet Zentrum eine Gelegenheit, stärker in die deutsche Arbeiter:innenklasse zu wirken und sich einen organisierten Rückhalt in den Betrieben aufzubauen. (…) Beide behandeln sozialpolitische Themen, indem sie den Widerspruch von Kapital und Arbeit, also den Konflikt zwischen Unten und Oben, in einen zwischen dem Innen und dem Außen umdeuten. Dabei wird der Klassenkonflikt ethnisiert und bspw. schlechte Löhne nicht als Folge einer Deregulierung des Arbeitsmarktes gedeutet, sondern als Folge vermeintlich schlecht qualifizierter Arbeiter mit Migrationsgeschichte, die das Lohnniveau drücken würden. Mit dieser Herangehensweise lassen sich harmonische materielle Verhältnisse unter Deutschen propagieren, während der zentrale Verteilungskonflikt nach außen verschoben wird. (…) Zentrum ist zumindest derzeit nicht in der Lage, sich als wirkmächtige Alternative zu den DGB-Gewerkschaften in Stellung zu bringen. Die eigentliche Gefahr liegt dabei jedoch weniger in der gegenwärtig wenig realistischen Perspektive einer konkurrierenden Massengewerkschaft. Bedeutender ist vielmehr das Potenzial, politische Deutungsrahmen zu verschieben und rechte Narrative in betrieblichen Debatten zu stärken

…“

Artikel von Mathias Hoose und Tim Ackermann

 

 in

express – Zeitung für sozialistische Betriebs- und Gewerkschaftsarbeit

 Ausgabe 9/2026


Siehe auch das Dossier

Betriebsratswahlen 2026 vom 1. März bis 31. Mai – werfen bereits braune Schatten voraus


und das Dossier:

AfD & Co: Nach den Köpfen nun auch in Betriebe und Betriebsräte?!


Zentrum Automobil verursacht(e) Herzrhythmusstörungen vor Betriebsratswahlen


„…

Die Tragödie ist, dass die Faschisten ihre historische Mission wahrnehmen und einigermaßen geschickt ein Vakuum füllen, das Linke und Radikale gelassen haben. Klimawandel, Wohlstandsverwahrlosung der Facharbeiterschaft, strukturelle Dummheit und Korruption des Managements befeuern wie in den USA Klimaleugner und Verbrennungsmotorchauvinisten. Wie schon die NSDAP in den 1930er Jahren übernimmt die AfD-Gewerkschaftskeimzelle »Zentrum« – neben der Hetze gegen Grüne und Klimakleber – eine Rhetorik von links, um die arbeitende Klasse zu ködern. Damals war es die Kritik an Partei- und Gewerkschaftsbonzen. Diesen real existierenden Bonzen haben Kurt Tucholsky und Erich Mühsam literarische Denkmäler gesetzt. Aus strategischen Gründen ist das »Zentrum« diesmal pro Betriebsrat und agitiert verbal-radikal gegen »Komanagement« – zumindest in der Herzkammer der IG Metall.


Der große Vorteil des Faschismus: Er kommt über Emotionen und Mythen. Er muss nicht logisch und stringent sein; er darf lügen, hetzen, verdrehen, falsche Versprechungen machen und sich in Widersprüche förmlich einwickeln. Die AfD wird mit der CDU das Betriebsverfassungsgesetz als »Bürokratiemonster« schleifen und alternative Vertretungsorgane den Betriebsräten rechtlich gleichstellen. Ein Beispiel, wohin die Reise geht, lieferte der dubiose Solarvertrieb Enpal, der vom Erdgasschock durch Russland-Sanktionen profitiert und dessen Vertriebsmodell an ein Schneeballsystem erinnert. Ein feiernder Mob aus offenbar gehirngewaschenen Solarvertrieblern versenkte Mitte Februar zum zweiten Mal eine vorbereitende Wahlversammlung zur Betriebsratswahl im Chaos

title: Mıhçı: ‘Bearing the burden of peace’ matters most now - Part One
content:
Murat Mıhçı, a member of the Central Executive Board of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), said the framework law proposed as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process should not be viewed solely in terms of peace between Kurds and Turks. Describing the law as a historic opportunity for Turkey’s democratisation, Mıhçı said the first steps should include the release of ill prisoners and the creation of conditions in which political actors can freely engage in politics both inside and outside the country.


Mıhçı said mother-tongue rights, equal citizenship, stronger local government, civil society and the expansion of political space were among the key elements of democratic transformation. He added that abandoning policies of war would also bring significant economic and social benefits. Mıhçı said the process should reach a positive stage within two or three years and stressed that even the next six months would be critical.


The framework law is a historic opportunity for Turkey’s democratisation


Mıhçı said he regarded the framework law as highly significant for the history of the region, adding that the broad political consensus behind it was the result of a long struggle.


He argued that it would be wrong to view the law solely as a means of establishing peace between Kurds and Turks. 


Mıhçı said: “I attach great importance to this law. It is extremely significant for the history of our region. There may have been similar developments in the past, but this is the first time, in terms of the balance of forces in Parliament, that such a clear framework has emerged with the backing of almost 95 per cent of Turkey’s political representation. We consider this very important. It is also the result of an enormous struggle. I also believe it is wrong to view the framework law in this region solely as a matter of peace between Kurds and Turks. If this framework law genuinely succeeds, it will also mark one of the most important steps towards democratisation in the region. At the same time, it will significantly strengthen Turkey’s influence in the region and its surroundings under the current circumstances. A country that establishes peace within its own borders will also, in a sense, embrace communities whose relatives live abroad and those living in the diaspora. Turkey and the peoples of Turkey stand to emerge from this law stronger and with far greater gains.”


The law must be implemented without political manoeuvring


Mıhçı said the first step towards implementing the framework law was to put all of its provisions into practice sincerely and in full, stressing in particular the need to release ill prisoners and create conditions in which political actors could freely engage in political activity.


Mıhçı said: “The answer to what the first stage of the framework law should involve is clear: every provision it contains must be implemented sincerely and realistically, without political manoeuvring. First and foremost, ill prisoners must be released without delay. Conditions must also be created in which political actors can freely carry out their political activities both inside and outside the country. This would genuinely contribute both to democratisation in the region and to its political strengthening.”


Democratisation is an issue for all the peoples of Turkey


Mıhçı said the scope of the framework law was not sufficient to provide a democratic solution to the Kurdish question, but stressed that it was nevertheless important as a basis for a new process of democratisation.


He said a solution to the Kurdish question could not be considered separately from Turkey’s broader democratisation process, adding that issues such as mother-tongue rights, equal citizenship and local government should be addressed as part of this broader framework.


Mıhçı said Kurds had struggled for their linguistic and identity rights for many years, but stressed that the Kurdish movement and the DEM Party defended the rights not only of the Kurdish language but of all peoples and languages in the region.


Mıhçı said: “I believe the discussions in the media surrounding the Kurdish question have been stripped of their substance. It is not only Kurds who face problems; all the other peoples living in Turkey have their own issues as well. Democratisation concerns this entire country. If we are talking about the mother tongue, there are serious problems affecting all the mother tongues spoken in this …

title: Amed residents: Let us honour our martyrs and their struggle
content:
The Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture for Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilisations (MEBYA-DER) organised a collective condolence gathering for those martyred in the freedom struggle at the Geterler Wedding and Conference Hall in the Rezan (Bağlar) district of Amed (Diyarbakır). Photographs of the martyrs and Abdullah Öcalan were displayed at the venue, where the gathering will continue for three days.


Thousands of people from different parts of the city visited the condolence gathering and offered their condolences to the families. Residents who spoke to ANF stressed the importance of honouring the memory of the martyrs and called on the public to attend the gathering.


 


It is now our duty to honour the martyrs


Emin Kılıç, who visited the condolence gathering, said the Kurdish people had reached an important stage in their struggle for freedom and that political struggle had now come to the fore. He said the martyrs had played a major role in bringing the struggle to this point and stressed that honouring their memory was a duty for everyone.


Kılıç said the scene at the condolence gathering in Bağlar was significant and continued: “Every struggle eventually reaches a stage in which the atmosphere is one of peace and the time has come for political struggle. We, the Kurdish people, have also reached that stage. We have moved beyond the stage of war and entered a period of political struggle. This means that now is the time to honour the martyrs of freedom, those who gave their lives to bring this cause to this point. The Kurdish people must regard it as their duty to honour the martyrs who brought this cause to this stage for as long as a single breath remains on these lands. What we are seeing today at Geterler Hall in the Bağlar district of Amed is the clearest expression of this. Many martyrs, people who gave their lives, are being commemorated here. Many Kurds will come to this gathering. No one can stand in the way of this any longer, and no one can prevent people from commemorating their own martyrs at this stage. It is a scene that really has to be witnessed in person. I believe anyone who comes here and sees it will gain tremendous spiritual strength. The scene today at the Geterler Wedding and Event Hall in Bağlar shows just how important and meaningful it is to honour the martyrs. Our call to our people is to come and take part in the commemoration of their martyrs.”


The Kurdish people want peace, not revenge


Kılıç also drew attention to the calls for peace made by families who lost loved ones in the freedom struggle. Kılıç said: “We constantly hear from mothers whose hearts have been broken, mothers who sacrificed their children for this cause. They say, ‘We want peace.’ Sometimes, on the other side, on the state side, we constantly hear statements such as, ‘We will take revenge, we will avenge our children.’ The Kurdish people, however, say, ‘Enough, enough, enough. We do not want revenge either. Our hearts have already been torn apart, our children have been taken from us. Let no one else lose their life. Let mothers’ tears fall only as smiles upon the faces of their children. We want peace.’ Those we have lost are gone. Let us not suffer any more losses. We want peace. Our only demand is peace.”


I hope mothers never have to cry again


Mecit Yılmaz said those martyred in the freedom struggle had left the Kurdish people with the hope of a life in freedom. Yılmaz also said: “First of all, I offer my condolences to all the people of Kurdistan and to all our families. They were martyred to give us a life of freedom. They were martyred to give us a free Kurdistan. I bow with respect before their memory and offer my condolences to their families. I hope mothers never have to cry again. I hope no mother has to shed another tear and that the days ahead are filled with peace and beauty.”


Öcalan is the key to a solution


Yılmaz said Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom was essential for the Peace and Democratic Society Process to lead to a lasting solution. Yılmaz continued: “Of course, for this to happen, Abdullah Öcalan must be free and able to take part in a life of freedom. No one can deceive us: we are free to the extent that Mr. Öcalan is free. We can participate in democratic life to the extent that Mr. Öcalan can participate in democratic life. Mr. Öcalan wants to build the democratic nation, and within that democratic nation he wants a free Kurdistan and …
